en: Preface by the Author:

It has been three years since I resided on this mountain. A lay practitioner named Lin Hanzhai has already provided a preface for the essential teachings from my formal sermons (*shangtang*) and published them.

Later, however, I observed that the Dharma-gate was becoming increasingly corrupt and declining day by day, to the point where it became unbearable even to hear or see. Consequently, I have ceased speaking.
Regarding the responsibility for the Dharma, I have willingly settled with two or three aspirant monks to merely "plow the fields and seek our food," for I do not wish to mingle with the crowds.
Nevertheless, the various donors, possessing deep devotion to the Dharma, vied with one another to bring offerings of incense into the mountains.
He was strongly urged to ascend the seat; having no choice, he broke the dam once more, and the waters rolled on without ceasing.

The secretary continued to record it, resulting in a massive volume, which the Chief Administrator, Master Yuan, requested be carved into woodblocks for circulation. I said, "This is merely idle talk for the sake of a meal;
what need is there to carve it? Yuan replied, "It is precisely so that the monks throughout the world who possess nostrils may smell its fragrance."
He was overcome by the scent of the rice; his cranial fontanelle split open, and he departed with an empty mind yet a full belly.

May this serve as a means to rectify the decay within the Dharma gate. Having heard these words, I could not help but follow the wind and turn the rudder, thus naming him "Feeding on Fragrance" (Cānxiāng).
He then wrote at the head of each scroll: "Śākyamuni’s 'closing the room' has already fallen into triviality;
Vimalakīrti’s 'refusing to speak' leaves a tangle of vines covering the ground. Today, this mountain monk drives a stake into empty space and stirs up waves upon dry land.
I bring forth all at once: *mukha-tarpaṇa* soup and iron-nail rice. This may truly be called genuine diligence; this is named the true offering of Dharma."
If there is anyone who can chew it down and swallow it, I shall bear my own burden and you shall bear yours; both of us will be spared.
If it is otherwise, I am simply a mountain monk, and you are simply a *dārala* (disciple); I am glad that we do not drag each other down.
Written by the Daoist Weilin on the tenth day of the twelfth month in the sixth year of the Kangxi era, as a preface at the Shengjian Hall.
I have observed that the Dharma-gate has fallen into decline these days; thus, I have resolutely declined to ascend the hall, wishing not to mingle with the crowds.
Yet, the various donors, possessing a profound heart for the Dharma, vied with one another to bring incense and offerings into the mountains, earnestly requesting me to take my seat.
Unable to refuse, the dyke broke once more, and the waters rolled on without ceasing. The records I have written fill many volumes, and so it was that Master Yuan, the Abbot, [took up the task].
"I request that you carve this for circulation. I replied, "This is merely idle talk for those who eat their fill at a banquet; what use is there in carving it?

Yuan said, "It is precisely so that the patch-robed monks throughout the world with nostrils may catch the scent of the rice, their cranial gates bursting open, and depart with empty minds yet full bellies.
In this way, perhaps there will be some revival for the decay of the Dharma-gate. I approved of his words, and thus—
Titled "Cānxiāng" (Feeding Fragrance). Written by himself at the head of various scrolls,
inscribed by the practitioner Lín for the Table of Contents of the *Shèngjiàntáng Gǔshān Cānxiāng Lù* (The Record of Feeding Fragrance at Drum Mountain in the Hall of the Holy Arrow).
Volume One:
Self-Preface; Volume Two: Discourses from the High Seat and Small Assemblies.
Preface to the Biographies of Eminent Monks; Postscripts;
Expository Texts; Verses and Hymns;
Inscriptions; Buddhist Ritual Texts.
Record of Master Weilin of Gushan’s Incense-Savoring, Volume One:
Notes by Taquan; Record of the Ascending to the High Seat.
The Deputy Commander-in-Chief, Duke Zhu, whose name is Yanxi, requests that I ascend the hall.

Today, I am honored by the arrival of Deputy Commander-in-Chief Zhu to this mountain to offer a memorial feast and to request that this mountain monk ascend the seat to expound the Dharma. Within our Buddha-Dharma, there is nothing extraordinary;

it is simply a matter of each person recognizing their own original nature, thereby shedding birth and death and attaining Buddhahood on the spot. This is because such a nature is inherently possessed.
The essence is inherently perfect and luminous; yet, due to a single moment of deviation, one becomes estranged for many lifetimes.
Having already mistaken oneself for an object, one further identifies objects as oneself; thus, internally one is bound by body and mind, and externally one is deluded by the world.
All various acts of grasping and rejecting are nothing but saṃsāra. Nevertheless, the eyebrows are simply above the eyes, and the tongue does not leave the mouth.
If you can, for a single thought-moment, turn the light back within, you may immediately grasp it directly. As for this phrase "turning the light back," how would you explain it?
"When one realizes that the nature of body and mind is empty, what difference is there between such a person and a Buddha?"
[The Master] struck the whisk and descended from his seat.
The lay devotee Zhou Chihda prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. A monk asked: "The single, firm, and dense body manifests within all dust-motes.
What is this firm and dense body? The Master said: "Realize it before you open your mouth. The monk stepped forward and asked: "How about after?"
"This is manifested within the dust. The Master said, "How can you deny it right before my face?

The monk bowed, and the Master continued, "A single thought-moment without arising allows for the sudden realization of the timeless Dharma; yet if the three minds dwell upon existence, one will forever sink into the body of outflows.
Therefore, in the past, Master Xuedou composed a verse on 'The Path Decreasing Daily' which says: Three parts of time—two have already passed."
"A single point on the Spirit Terrace has not yet been wiped clean; Greedy for life, one hastens through the days in petty toil. If called, one does not turn back—what can be done?
Xuedou’s verse was intended for those in the world who do not know how to seek the Way and thus waste their time in vain; he therefore administered this bitter medicine.
It may be said that his compassionate heart was driven to its limit. Today, I, this mountain monk, cannot help but annotate it from the beginning. Part Three.

The two seasons of light and shade have already passed; how could the turtle ever have escaped from within the jar? That single point of the spiritual terrace (*lingtai*) has not yet been polished away—can it still deceive him?
Greedily pursuing life day by day in a state of frantic toil, with feet trailing behind, if one cannot turn back when called, what can be done?
Truly, O monks! If you are able to awaken beneath Xuedou’s words, you may rest for a while in the City of Transformation (*huacheng*).

They attain the bliss of the cessation of the Two Vehicles and, upon hearing the words of this mountain monk, awaken and ascend directly to the Precious Abode, attaining the Dharma-joy of the Bodhisattvas.
Yet there is another person who tramples over the conjured city and kicks the Precious Abode to its foundations.
Tell me, what else do they obtain? "The tattered robe covers the head, and all affairs cease; at this moment, even this mountain monk does not understand."
The virtuous woman Gao Jijin had cultivated merit in advance and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall.
This single set of merit-offerings from Mount Yuling has been perfected over immeasurable kalpas; today, as it is brought forth once again, its radiance illuminates the universe.
There is no need for snow to fall upon a red furnace; all dharmas remain as they were. The spring waters overflow, vying with one another in their flow; the spring mountains rise tier upon tier.
Xiu: "In spring, the birds warble in harmony; in spring, the trees flourish with lush greenery. If you can see it directly and immediately, you are the successor of Gautama.
To further deliberate upon the Buddha-dharma, this person is truly not up to much. He then raised his whisk and called to the assembly, saying, "Do you see?
This is the Great Divine Spell, this is the Great Illuminating Spell. He struck the sounding block and descended from the seat.

Virtuous Master Yuanfu, together with the assembly of donors and protectors, has prepared a vegetarian feast and invited me to ascend the hall. A thousand mountains and ten thousand mountains are but a single mountain;
a thousand waters and ten thousand waters are but a single water. Even if one were to travel to the ends of the earth, how could one ever escape this very place?
Virtuous Master Yuanfu is about to depart for Guangdong; today he has specifically come up the mountain together with the various donors and protectors to offer this service.
[The Master] provided offerings and took his leave of the mountain monk. He recalled that the ancient teachings say: "Observe the direction to know where one has gone;
yet that which goes does not arrive at a direction. Now, since it has already gone, why does it not arrive at a direction? Since it does not arrive at a direction, how can it have gone?
If you can see this point here, then you will step upon solid ground with every stride, and every place will be your own home. Naturally, the sound will harmonize and the resonance will follow.
The grass bends and the wind blows; the six states are free from anxiety, and the sovereign alone rejoices. Let us set aside these matters for now.
Consider only the offerings provided today by the assembly of patrons and protectors: where, ultimately, does this merit reside? Secretly, the roots of goodness take root in the ground of nature;
surging forth, the ocean of blessings wells up from its spiritual source.
The Upāsikā Wú Tàisù had cultivated merit in advance and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. "Human and celestial retributions need not be sought;
if you seek them, they will instead bring about extraordinary sorrow. If the myriad practices are gathered back to that other shore, the return journey can serve as a boat for saving beings.
"But how does one go to that other shore? Today, on behalf of the Upāsikā Tàisù, I request the entire assembly to join me in this communal task.
Yi! Mindfully recite the Mahāprajñāpāramitā. Hūṃ hūṃ. Farewell.
The Venerable Shihhang and his disciple Sijie requested the precepts and asked for an address to the assembly. "Take the precepts as your teacher; abide by the precepts.
This is the compassionate teaching from the Buddha’s own lips, his final clear instruction. What are the precepts? The Great Master of the Sixth Patriarch said: "The original nature..."

There is nothing that is not the precept of self-nature (*svabhāva-śīla*). One must know that from the Buddhas above down to the most minute insects, there is none who does not individually possess this nature, and likewise none who does not individually possess these precepts.
The sound of the wind and the song of the birds all expound the Vinaya of Kāśyapa;
the mountain scenery and the luster of the rivers fully reveal the mind-ground of Śākyamuni. Therefore, the former master said: "What are the five precepts? Plum blossoms."
The snow melts and opens up. What is the śrāmaṇera precept? A stone shoot breaks through the green moss. What is the bhikṣu precept?
The Yellow River freezes solid to its very bottom. What is the bodhisattva precept? The drenching rain falls in abundance.
If you can penetrate to this point, then the entire universe, the great earth, and the myriad phenomena of the forest—all are the self-nature of the person themselves.
The light of the precepts—how could it wait for one to don the robes, arrange the implements, ascend the altar, and perform the *karmavācanā* before the precepts are obtained?
If this were not so, I, this mountain monk, would follow in the footsteps of others like a dog’s tail following a fox’s fur; I cannot help but provide another path. What are the five precepts?
They are founded upon the adamantine limit (*vajra-paryanta*), firm and deep, unshakable. What are the śrāmaṇera precepts? The lotus flower is just beginning to open.
Emerging from the water, its fragrance flows throughout the world. What is the *bhikṣu* precept? Transcending the three realms with a horizontal body, one ascends spontaneously and freely.
What is the *bodhisattva* precept? Stepping through the red dust at every turn, the entire body is without shadow or form.
Do you all understand? Carefully guard the floating skin-bag to cross the sea of suffering; do not follow the rākṣasas to beg for a speck of dust. Arriving by way of the wind.
Only when you leave the raft will you truly be one of those present at that single assembly on Vulture Peak. Take care.
Venerable Miaozhan, together with Upāsaka Tanyu, requests a formal lecture from the Abbot. Venerable Miaozhan of Wenling has long relied upon the Dharma seat of Boshan;
he must have heard extensively of the patriarchal style of the Boshan lineage. Formerly, the Elder of Boshan would constantly instruct people to contemplate...
When this person’s single breath does not return, where will they ultimately go? These words possess a great capacity for saving others.
Today, taking advantage of the wind to fan the fire, I cannot help but analyze them further: when the single breath does not return, the Buddhas of the three periods have already been buried alive.
Where do they go? A yellow oriole sings in the green willow tree—light and darkness are both present.
"What is this? To watch a scale-weight solve an iron saw—let us stop this for now.
The old man Boshan is currently entangling you all right here before your eyes. Do you still remember the *huatou*? Ha ha!
If it were Tao Yuanming, he would have knit his brows and gone back home. He struck the whisk and descended from the seat.

The Abbot of Liancheng led his disciples to shave their heads, seek ordination, and request a formal lecture from the Master. "In the past," [the Master said], "the World-Honored One would not permit women to leave the household life.
Yet Ānanda, on behalf of the Buddha’s maternal aunt Mahāprajāpatī, made earnest entreaties, and the Buddha consequently granted permission.
This, however, caused the True Dharma of the Buddha to decline after five hundred years. Nevertheless, were it not for Ānanda, there would have been no one to know the World-Honored One’s secret."
I believe that it would not have been possible for women to attain liberation had it not been for the World-Honored One.
Since that time, the number of women who have left the household life within the Buddha-dharma, awakened to the Way, and realized the fruits of enlightenment is beyond counting.

Have you not seen how the bhikṣuṇīs received their predictions at Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, how Zongchi attained the "flesh" at Mount Shaoshi, how the sharp wit of Moshan was second only to [Baizhang’s], and how Guankui took his teachings to heart?

The subtle and comprehensive realization is stable and profound; it is confirmed by the Great Wisdom Seal (*Mahāmati*). This sufficiently demonstrates that while delusive conditions have distinctions, the true nature is neither male nor female.
Only when one can turn the light back for a single thought-moment will one realize that Buddhahood is one’s original state.

Today, the Abbot of Xifeng Hermitage, Liancheng, has brought forth his disciple Chuanjie and their mother—three individuals—to leave the household life. They have been specially escorted to Gushan to receive the tonsure.

Receive the precepts. Setting aside for a moment whether you will attain the Way or its fruits, merely to be presently liberated from the burdens of womanhood and to join the ranks of the Honored Three Jewels is already like a lotus blooming amidst fire—something not easily attained.

From this day forward, each of you should give rise to the supramundane mind and cultivate supramundane practices. Standing tall beyond all things, remain unstained by worldly conditions; furthermore, you should practice giving.
Liberate your own mind. Purify your own mind through the observance of ethical discipline; broaden your own mind through patience; fortify your own mind through diligence;
bring peace and happiness to your own mind through meditative concentration; and clarify your own mind through wisdom.

Thus benefiting both yourself and others, with merit and wisdom perfectly radiant, you shall become a compassionate vessel for the ocean of suffering and a pillar for the gateway of the Dharma. This is possible.
This refers to the true disciples of the Buddha. To truly repay the Buddha’s kindness, all you nuns present here should exert yourselves together. Be careful.
At the request of the Nunnery Mistress Peici and the laywoman Yu Taizheng, [the Master] ascended the hall.

He cited Chan Master Da Fayan of Qingliang, who addressed the assembly, saying: "When the three drumrolls have ceased, everyone comes forward in a throng; worldly affairs and Dharma affairs are both completed at once."
[The assembly] finished. The Master said: "The sweet melon is sweet from stem to tip. Chan Master Ni Huiwen of Jingju addressed the assembly, saying:
"When the three beats of the drum have ceased, you all come crowding forward. My staff is not here; I shall give you thirty blows with the handle of my broom.

The Master said: "The bitter gourd is bitter from root to tip. I, this mountain monk, am not like that. When the three beats of the drum have ceased, you all come crowding forward. The wind moves, and the clouds..."
Rising. The water flows and the flowers bloom.

At the request of the Abbot of Prajñā Hermitage, Wenyuan and Wenxi, he ascends the hall. The minds of sentient beings take objects everywhere, yet they alone cannot take the Great Prajñā as an object.
This is because the Great Prajñā is not an objective realm for mind, intellect, or consciousness. Therefore, the ancients...
Master De constantly taught people to depart from mind, intellect, and consciousness (*citta-manovijñāna*) and to transcend the paths of ordinary beings and sages.
But how does one depart from mind, intellect, and consciousness? How does one exit the paths of ordinary beings and sages? He gave a shout and said:

"If you can understand this one shout within, what is mind, intellect, consciousness, or the paths of ordinary beings and sages? They are merely the sound of a hot bowl clinking. At that very moment, all...
"Do people still see the Great Prajñā? "Vibrant yellow chrysanthemums welcome the morning sun; Verdant green bamboo invites the clear breeze.
[The Master] descends from the seat.
On the Buddha’s Birthday, Disciple Deng Xing’an bows to the stupa on behalf of his mother and escorts his sister into the monastic life. He requests the Master to ascend the hall. [Year...]

Each year there is the eighth day of the fourth month, when Queen Māyā gave birth to Siddhārtha. This year’s fourth-eighth is even more extraordinary: the entire body of Śākyamuni appears within a jeweled stūpa.
A filial son brings it with great reverence, praying that his parents’ blessings and longevity be equal to Mount Sumeru.
He prostrates eighty-four thousand times; in every single bow, he beholds the Buddha—a reality truly inconceivable. Thus has the Mother planted many roots of merit throughout her past lives.
Roots of goodness. Abandoning the female form to leave the household life and ascend to the stages of the precepts;
the Dharma-gate of the *Prajñāpāramitā* regarding flesh and bone—whose among the people of this world has keenly awakened to this meaning? I now speak these verses as a brief praise.

The Buddha and the devas rejoice with brilliant radiance, universally illuminating all sentient beings throughout the Dharma-realm, causing them all to ultimately reach the other shore. (A shout. Descends from the seat.

The Senior Officer Zhou Gong, whose dharma name is Shànglián, together with the lay believer Yang Shàngzōng, has delivered woodblocks for the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* to this mountain for circulation and requests that I ascend the hall to speak.
Before Śākyamuni Buddha appeared in the world, all sentient beings throughout the great earth had already attained Buddhahood;
yet from the time he appeared until his parinirvāṇa forty-nine years later, across more than three hundred assemblies, he exhausted every effort and expedient to guide them.
Upon reaching the assembly of the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra*, they receive their predictions from the very beginning; yet this seems as though there were an intervening layer.
Although it is thus, one cannot help but feel that the impoverished son has turned his back on his father and the intoxicated guest has lost sight of the pearl.

Having no other choice, one must take the wrong for the right, causing them to open, show, awaken to, and enter the Buddha’s knowledge and vision (*buddhajñānadarśana*), thereby fulfilling the original intent of appearing in the world. But what is "opening the Buddha's knowledge and vision"? Strike!

"Breaking through empty space—into how many pieces? What is the Buddha’s manifestation of knowledge and vision? Pointing directly at the face one was born with. What is the Buddha’s realization of knowledge and vision?
Steamed buns and dumplings are fundamentally made of flour. What is the Buddha’s entry into knowledge and vision?
One's entire body is already seated in the Palace of the Empty King. If you people can, within these four turning phrases of this mountain monk, directly...
It was received and carried away by those below. Today, the entire body of the World-Honored One has appeared upon the head of the board and has bestowed predictions of enlightenment upon all people.
If this is not yet clear to you, then cherish it and circulate this great Dharma-treasure; let the mark of the broad and long tongue be forever proclaimed.
The disciple Yao Taiyue, leading a multitude of virtuous friends, has prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. It is difficult to obtain a human body;

it is difficult to encounter the Buddha-dharma; it is difficult to possess faith. O Great Assembly, you have already obtained a human body, you have already encountered the Buddha-dharma, and you have already possessed faith.
One might call this a lotus blooming amidst fire. Nevertheless, tell me: in what do you place your faith? Do you not trust in the Buddha? His marks and signs are difficult to manifest.
Do you not trust in the Dharma? Its names and phrases cannot be fully revealed. Do you not trust in the Sangha? They move freely beyond the world.
Within these Three Jewels, if one can know them thus, see them thus, and believe and understand them thus, one will not give rise to the conceptualization of dharmas.
He brandishes the whisk, draws a circle in the air, and says: "I now guarantee this matter for you; it shall never be in vain.

He then raises the whisk again, calls to the assembly, and asks: "Do you understand? The Imperial Decree has been issued and has spread throughout the land; peach blossoms bloom everywhere, laughing in the spring breeze."
The lay devotee Li Yu led a group of virtuous friends to request that I ascend the hall.
The pure-faith disciple Li Yu has built a hermitage and fashioned images in Fuzhou, diligently performing good deeds and seeking blessings without turning back.

Today, he has again led a group of virtuous friends to Mount Gu at dawn to provide a meal for the monks and requested that I, a mountain monk, preach the Dharma. An ancient worthy said: "In the Buddha-dharma, what matters is this: can one practice it?"
This is indeed manifest. If you are truly able to practice it, what problem would there be? As for the Buddha-dharma, how do you practice it?
Do you understand? Generosity is practice; precept-keeping, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are all practice.
Generosity transcends stinginess and greed; precept-keeping transcends violation; patience transcends anger; diligence transcends indolence; meditative concentration...

Concentration overcomes distraction; wisdom overcomes folly. Although hundreds of thousands of immeasurable gateways of practice all ultimately return to the six perfections, there is a man who is fundamentally neither stingy nor transgressive, neither angry nor indolent, neither distracted nor foolish. What, then, would you have him practice?
The hawk-bow has been hung up and the whale-waves have subsided; ten thousand leagues of song and chant celebrate the One Man.

The Venerable Wàngyún of Eastern Lǔ has established a vegetarian feast and requested that I ascend the hall. He cites: When the Bodhisattva Maitreya descended from the Inner Court, the Bodhisattva Asaṅga asked him:
"Four hundred years among humans constitute a single day and night in that heaven.

Within a single period of time, Maitreya brings five hundred billion devaputras to realization and enables them to attain the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*). I wonder, what did he say?"
"What is this Dharma? Vasubandhu replied, "It is simply this very Dharma; it is merely that the Sanskrit sounds are elegant and refined, making it a joy for people to hear.
The Master said, "Maitreya spoke it according to reality; the Devaputra realized it according to reality; Asaṅga questioned it according to reality;
and Vasubandhu answered it according to reality. Today, if someone were to ask Drumshan, I would request the Venerable Wangyun to respond."

The Master was preaching the Dharma. [A monk] asked, "I do not know for certain—what Dharma are you preaching? He replied, "I am preaching only this very Dharma. [The monk] further asked, "What is this Dharma?
[The Master] struck his whisk and said, "Do you understand? Have you not heard it said: 'The Brahma-sound is pure and elegant, causing those who hear it to rejoice'?
Is there anyone here who has realized the patience of the non-arising of dharmas (*anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti*)? Bring him forward; I shall give him a thorough beating!"
Layman He Yuwu, seeking progeny and seeking protection, requests that I ascend the hall. "The phenomena of the three realms, above and below—I say they are all mind.
Apart from these mental phenomena, there is nothing else to be found.

Today, the disciple of Fucheng, He Zhizu, together with his wife, Lady Fang, have provided a vegetarian feast for the Sangha to seek merit. Merit has been produced! But from where does this merit come? It is like gold upon dry land.

Lotus flowers bloom one by one. Through ritual worship and repentance, transgressions are expiated. When the transgressions are extinguished, where have they gone? The long river flows day and night toward the east;
as transgressions are extinguished and blessings arise, the lineage flourishes. Branch after branch bears fruit upon the Bodhi tree. Nevertheless, there is yet another phrase:
neither transgression nor blessing can encompass it, and birth-and-death have no concern with it. [The Master] suddenly grasps his staff and calls out.

The Great Assembly said: "This very thing—reaching up to support heaven and reaching down to support earth—is as black as lacquer. It is ever present within movement and function, yet it cannot be contained within movement and function.
If there is someone who can take hold of it, they shall roam freely across the world.
If it were otherwise, one might say that the common people use it daily without knowing it. (He struck the ground once and gave a shout.)
Huiri of Kuangxiao Temple exhorted Kongsheng, Xingfan, and Jixian. When a group of fellow practitioners prepared a vegetarian feast and invited him to ascend the hall, he raised the following:
Master Baizhi said, "Because my own body is empty, all phenomena are empty; the thousand species and myriad forms are all identical."
Yunmen took up the case and said: "All of you, when standing, do not see standing; when walking, do not see walking.
Since the four elements and five aggregates cannot be found, where do mountains, rivers, and the great earth come from?
All of you, every day you take up your alms bowls and eat your food—what do you call this 'food'? Where else does there come to be even a single grain of rice? The Master said: "Yunmen merely..."
Out of compassion, I have spoken these words of descending into the weeds. If one can directly realize the place of return, what further matters would there be regarding the Buddha-dharma?
Nevertheless, I, this mountain monk, do not speak in such a manner. Because my own body is empty and all phenomena are empty, the thousand species and myriad transformations are entirely identical.
The wisdom of all wisdoms is pure; it is non-dual and without division, without distinction and without interruption.
Therefore, he eats his meals on a long couch, bathes in the continent of Uttarakuru, treads upon the five Mount Sumerus, and wears a hundred-patch robe.
Yet, he is suddenly spotted by a *caṇḍāla* dog-slaughterer at the crossroads, who draws his sharp blade and cries out loudly:
"One invocation of 'Namo Buddha,' and all shall together attain the Buddha-way. Do you understand? Great!
The assembly has concluded its affairs; may you all return to the hall in peace.

The filial son Chen Taiyu offers this memorial service for his late mother and requests that the Master ascend the hall. The laywoman Daogang, while at home, examined her conditions and diligently cultivated pure practices.
Upon reaching the age of seventy, her right mindfulness was clear and distinct; she recited the Buddha’s name until the appointed time and passed away. This is now the first [anniversary].

7. His son, Taiyu, led his kinsmen and followers to personally escort the spirit-casket to the mountain. They performed the cremation according to the Dharma and interred the remains within the Parent-Gratitude Stupa.
Furthermore, they offered prostrations, repentance, and meals to the monks to dedicate merit for the deceased’s peace in the afterlife.
They have also requested the mountain monk to ascend this seat to proclaim the vehicle of the school and assist in their rebirth. Does the assembly understand? To all sentient beings, the Buddhas...
Within the mind, one establishes a water-moon *maṇḍala* to receive and transform sentient beings so that they may return to the Pure Land.

Sentient beings, within the minds of all Buddhas, uphold the names of the Buddhas as empty sounds; by recollecting the illusory Buddha, they aspire for rebirth. Like the chick pecking and the hen pecking, there is no discrepancy between them.

When the path of resonance and response perfectly coincides, at such a moment, an infant is born upon a golden lotus pedestal; before the white jade steps, Amitābha receives his prediction of enlightenment.

The wind whistles through the jeweled trees, and the waves ripple across the golden channels; together with celestial music, they ring out in harmony, and in accord with the sūtras, they resonate in unison.
The demon of the mirror is forever subdued, and the fruit of the dream is fully realized. Thus, the life’s work of Lady Chen is complete.
It is finished. Nevertheless, is there anyone among this assembly who transcends the mundane world alone, remaining untouched by such praise?
If there is, the Elder Amitābha would have no time to nod his head in approval, and Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta would find their praises inexhaustible.
If it is otherwise, the mud of the five turbidities is many thousands of fathoms deep; let us all join hands and climb the high mountain together.
On the Buddha’s Day of Joy (*Buddhānandadivasa*), the Bhikṣuṇī Xingchang invited her fellow disciple Fazhi to ascend the hall.
[The Master said: "Yesterday, while I was napping during the day, I dreamed of a monk entering my quarters to pay his respects. Upon rising, I asked him:

'Since fundamentally there is not a single thing, what should a student of the Dharma take as his object of investigation? I replied: 'Investigate precisely that which is without a single thing. The monk said: 'Without a single thing...'"
"Regarding the 'bottom of things'—how do you practice? The mountain monk said, "There is no practicing. The monk asked, "Does this not fall into emptiness?
The mountain monk said, "As for this very one who fears falling into emptiness, where could it go to seek emptiness? The monk was left speechless.

The mountain monk spoke again, saying, "In practicing Chan, you must reach the point where the four corners touch the ground before you can truly make use of it. If you are merely like a donkey before a horse..."
Afterwards, he wagged his lips and tongue; with his feet floundering and squirming beneath him, he collapsed at a single push.
What was there worth conversing about? The monk remained silent and withdrew after hesitating for a moment. Upon waking and rising, he realized it had been a dream.
Today, before this great assembly, I shall speak yet another dream-talk. I venture to ask the assembly: to what extent have you reached in your Zen practice?
"These four edges touch the ground. Regarding this single phrase, "the four edges touching the ground," what do you intend to discuss?
Is it that you have penetrated several ancient public cases and are capable of composing verses upon them? Is it that you recognize one or two critical phrases within the sutras and treatises?
Or is it that, at the gateway of the six sense faculties, you have recognized that which is luminously clear?
"Is it that one who is truly enlightened can immediately clench their fists, point their fingers, blink their eyes, or raise their eyebrows?
Is it that by means of such a 'view,' one fuses with the myriad dharmas, and that the myriad dharmas fuse with this view?

Is it that one hides their eyes, closes their eyelids, gathers their thoughts back into emptiness, and lets everything be utterly swept away? To seek the Great Way with such an understanding is like steaming sand."
To prepare a meal while digging into the earth to seek the heavens is merely to exhaust oneself; what benefit is there for one’s own self?
Have you not seen how Master Jianguan of Jiufeng said: "To attempt to study the Chan school with the conceptual mind is much like heading west when one intends to go east.
Not only will you fail to reach home, but from the very moment you first set foot out the door, you have already lost your way. Or perhaps there is a man who...
Hearing the mountain monk speak thus, he immediately asked, "Please, Master, speak that phrase where the four corners touch the ground.
This is precisely what is called "the short man watching the play," following others up and down; it becomes increasingly unbearably so.

Nevertheless, now before this assembly of humans and devas, one cannot leave the mouth empty; I cannot help but take this opportunity to ride the slope downward and briefly address the great multitude.
I transmit this message: today is the fifteenth day of the seventh month. All Buddhas rejoice; the assembly of monks observes the *pravāraṇā*.
The Abbot has exhorted the community to establish an unrestricted *bowl-offering* (*alabana*) great assembly to universally deliver all sentient beings within the Dharma-realm.
A Bhikṣuṇī named Xingchang from Wenzhou, together with her disciple Fazhi, have traveled here from afar specifically to request the reception of the precepts. At noon, the ceremony was established.
The assembly has been provided with offerings for the fast. We request that you ascend the hall to proclaim the Prajñāpāramitā, thereby opening the path to enlightenment.

We humbly pray that the Dharma-wisdom may flourish and prosper, and that all those present in this assembly may each partake fully of the nectar of immortality and sate themselves with the finest clarified butter.

May they advance upon the Way without demonic interference and cultivate their minds with a secure foundation. May even the lanterns and pillars join in bearing witness, and may the white oxen and black slaves alike achieve Buddhahood.
The Way. We humbly observe that the Great Assembly has stood for a long time; therefore, we shall now descend from our seats.

On this occasion, the Chief Administrator Yi-maek celebrates his fiftieth birthday. His disciples, including Jo-ro and others, have prepared a vegetarian feast and respectfully request the Master to ascend the hall.
In observing the river, there is no dualistic seeing; one perceives but a single glimpse. To be born and immediately called "Honored One" still implies the existence of measure and number.
One must know that within the sphere of the person, there is a field of steady security, utterly beyond measure and number, without boundaries or limits.

Facing it, one does not see its head; following it, one cannot glimpse its rear. Even when the vast waters rise to the heavens, one is not drowned; though the kalpa-fire blazes fiercely, [one remains unscathed].
It is indestructible. Only such a person as this can truly know that there is such a matter.

Once one knows such a matter, one may freely manifest clarity in every aspect and apply it to every object; taking mastery wherever one is, one realizes the fundamental principle whenever encountering conditions.

Whether walking at will through four or five hundred lanes of flowering willows, or entering with a mere snap of the fingers into two or three thousand pavilions of pipes and strings—one remains unobstructed.
It is unimpeded; it is neither of the past nor of the present. Nevertheless, were it not for the right person, one would surely have to wring one's hands in frustration. Furthermore, he said:

"I, this mountain monk, have been in the world for three years. Only by relying on the administrative service of the Chief Administrator, Master Yuan, has the ritual of transformation been roughly prepared."
The propagation of the Dharma’s transformation is largely due to Master Yuan, who from beginning to end practiced with sincerity and integrity.

He served the community selflessly and achieved his goals through self-discipline. Unchanged by frost and snow, and unaltered by wind and rain, he may well be compared to Yangqi in relation to Ciming, or Shichuang in relation to Hongzhi;
he stands as one who can truly be said to be without shame. Today marks the fiftieth anniversary of his ordination. At its commencement...
Having conferred the Dharma upon my disciples, including Zhao and the others, as well as the great assembly of the mountain, all were harmonious and reverent, congratulating one another.
I, this mountain monk, have a thread to pull; I too must offer a word of celebration. Though the passage of time flows on without ceasing, the unmoving Suchness is simply this.
Let us not discuss knowing fate or knowing error; the primary truth is the reality of body and mind.
The great assembly has stood for a long time;
take your seats. Opening the furnace, I ascend the hall: Last night the frosty wind swept across the earth; the warm curtain was raised and the earthen stove opened.
Even for those with iron foreheads and copper eyes, one must force a sweat to break out. This is because, within the sphere of each of you, there is one...
This is a field of pure white expanse. Since beginningless kalpas, you have always been within it;
yet, because you do not know and do not believe, you cannot avoid imitating patterns and forms, engaging in long-term and short-term practices to prompt your investigation.

You must open the wisdom and vision of the Buddhas and Patriarchs, penetrate the root-source of birth and death, and clearly recognize the boundaries so that they are not encroached upon by the six thieves.
Wandering aimlessly outward, once you have recognized it, you will finally know that this place is your own original dwelling from beginningless kalpas,
your original enjoyment, which has never changed by so much as a hair’s breadth and has never diminished by so much as a hair’s breadth.
You may then establish order in the state and peace in the land, found a family and build a career, and open the great hidden treasury to provide relief for all.

Truly! Only then will you not have failed the original resolve to leave the household life and travel as a mendicant. Is there anyone among this assembly who clearly recognizes the boundaries of the dharma-realm?
If there is, then today’s lifting of the retreat restrictions shall be no different from an extraordinary occasion.
If this is not yet the case, you must truly rouse your spirit and apply your mind to investigate: look into what principle this is. Make enlightenment your goal; do not set limits.
As for the timing: one must not fail to awaken for a single lifetime, nor cease striving for a single lifetime; one must not fail to awaken for a single year, nor cease striving for a single year;
one must not fail to awaken for a single life, nor cease striving for a single life. One must be prepared to risk two or three lifetimes until awakening is attained.
One must possess such great capacity, great power, and great resolve to be fit to enter and practice within this gate. If one merely...

Those who study while associating with their peers, engaging in "fresh fish Chan" (superficial practice), discoursing on principles, and displaying their cleverness—hastily seeking to sell themselves to others—are not of our lineage;
there is no need for them to come before me. Only those of like mind shall mutually understand one another.
On the Master’s birthday, the lay practitioner Lin Shunyou prepared a vegetarian feast and requested him to ascend the hall. "Today is this mountain monk’s humble birthday," he said.

"I am deeply honored that the lay practitioner Lin Shunyou has come to the mountains to present offerings and offer his congratulations, and further requests me to preach the Dharma for the great assembly."
Just as it is, how does one offer a long-life blessing? How does one preach the Dharma? Does the great assembly see the empty space before them?
Does this empty space have seasons, days, months, or years? Does it have day and night, light and darkness?
Does it have boundaries or dimensions? Does it have mutual obstruction or separation? If you people can truly recognize this empty space—
At the very moment you reach this point, you will recognize your own place of arrival.

Once you recognize your own place of arrival, you will recognize the place of arrival of this mountain monk, as well as the place of arrival of all Buddhas and Patriarchs from antiquity, devas and humans, the multitudes of living beings, mountains, rivers, and the lands of nations.

This is that which balances the workings of creation and forges all things; it spans from the beginningless past to the endless future, unchanging and immutable. Have you not seen how the Patriarch Zhaozhou acted?
It is said: "Before the world existed, this nature already existed; when the world is destroyed, this nature is not destroyed. At that time, a monk asked, "What is this nature?
Zhaozhou said, "The four great elements and the five aggregates. The monk said, "These are subject to destruction; what then is this nature?
Zhaozhou said, "The four great elements and the five aggregates. O Great Assembly! Zhaozhou dug within the house of the poor woman.
The treasury is opened; from the forehead of the Malla, a bright pearl is cleaved forth and presented in its entirety. What further remains?
If you all can directly receive and take this up right here, then today’s Dharma service by Layman Shunyou will have been fulfilled.
Merit is never bestowed in vain. If it were otherwise, listen further to these verses: "Each person possesses a set of vajra-bones;
Within the mass of red flesh, they rise ten thousand fathoms high. Today, for your sake, I have personally pointed them out. [He plants his staff firmly on the ground.
"To support heaven and earth is not in vain. [He descends from the seat.]

At the request of the venerable Benzhao, I ascend the hall. Master Lang Benzhao of Huangmei, having been an old friend in the Way for thirty years, has specifically dispatched his disciple Zhihua Jiahe from afar, traveling over several hundred li, to prepare an offering and request the Dharma on behalf of my birthday celebration.
Unable to avoid seizing this opportune moment and occasion, I shall reveal a message to you all. Last night, the void...
It bursts asunder. A child falls down for no apparent reason. To establish his age and years for him is also to be muddled right before one's face.
Nevertheless, one cannot help but follow the error with error and say: "Above heaven and below heaven, I alone am honored.

Thus, the eight directions respectfully acknowledge him, and the ten directions look toward him in obedience; the mountains, rivers, and lands bow their bodies and lower their shadows. At such a time as this—
"Is there any lame old monk who can carry out the true command? If there is, I, this mountain monk, shall form a bond of fellow-study with him.
If not, I shall join palms with a wooden man and loudly sing the Song of Great Peace.
He then struck his staff and said, "Hūṃ! Hūṃ! and descended from the seat.

Tai Chao, Tai Zhi, and Tai Jing were ordained. They requested that [the Master] ascend the hall. These three, Tai Chao and the others, originally began by observing the Blood Bowl Festival to repay the kindness of their parents;
they subsequently entered the Buddha-dharma and came to understand the matter of leaving the household life.

Arriving at this day, they have severed their attachments and entered the mountains, earnestly requesting ordination and the reception of the precepts. As the Elder Śākyamuni said: "Filial piety is called the precept. Indeed...
If one who is a child can truly, with utmost sincerity, practice filial piety toward their parents, they embody the entirety of precepts, concentration, and wisdom.
What need is there then to shave off hair and beard, don the *kāṣāya*, and ascend the altar for *karmavācanā* before being considered a renunciant who has attained the precepts?
Nevertheless, one must first recognize one’s true parents; otherwise, it is merely a vain and exhausting toil.
To honor and provide for them while remaining attached to the bonds of affection merely binds one to the karmic cycle of worldly birth and death;
what benefit does this have for the Way of filial piety? If you recognize your true parents, you will possess the true Way of filial piety.
To possess the true Way of filial piety is itself true renunciation, true reception of the precepts, and the true repayment of parental kindness. Furthermore, who among you is your true father?
The Mother said after a long silence: "With my entire body red and raw, I lie amidst thorns; even the Buddhas of the three periods cannot support me.
Be diligent and filial throughout the twelve hours; the moment a single thought arises, it harms me."
The Abbot ascends the hall for the tonsure ceremony: "The rise and fall within the three realms are truly lamentable.
Having shaved the beard and hair and donned the *kāṣāya*, One remains eternally pure, unstained by a single speck of dust. This is truly the *utpala* flower of the human world.
Tell me, Great Assembly: what is it that lies beneath the *kāṣāya*? Do not say it cannot be shaken off; it has long been revealed in its entirety. In the morning, he washes [his face].
He rubbed his head and only then realized that the mark on the crown of his head was originally complete.
On the day the Buddha attained enlightenment, General Xu, the Commander-in-Chief, sent a Dharma robe to the mountain to provide a meal for the monks and invited the Master to ascend the hall.
The Master ascended the seat, held up the robe, and addressed the assembly, saying: "O Great Assembly! This robe belongs to General Xu of Zhangzhou Prefecture, whose name is Tian..."
The Empress Dowager, together with her consort Lady Shen (Dharma name: Taishu), bestowed this upon the mountain monk to preach the Dharma. Now tell me:
is this robe the same as, or different from, the golden brocade *kāṣāya* transmitted by the World-Honored One in days of yore?

If you say they are the same, then past and present do not meet one another. If you say they are different, their threadlines have always been interconnected. Do you understand? It pervades the entire body.
Clad in nothing but threadless rags, he appeared like bright clouds reflecting against the azure sky. He then donned his robes, took his seat, and said:

"Six years at the Snow Mountains, enduring hunger and cold; upon seeing the morning star, the Buddha was realized. Yet it is said that all sentient beings are already fully endowed [with this nature]."
"It is solely because of deluded thoughts that one falls into ordinary sentiments. Great assembly, tell me: how does one sever these deluded thoughts? After a long silence, he said:
"Wait until Old Śākyamuni becomes an ordinary person; then I will reveal it for you."
The elder Yixiang, together with his fellow practitioners, offered a vegetarian feast in praise of the Way and requested the Master to ascend the hall. Elder Yixiang asked, "The ancients said:
'Tearing through the grass and observing the wind, one seeks only to see one's nature. I ask the Master: where is this nature right now?
The Master replied, "Where is the Elder standing right now? Yixiang stepped forward and said, "Only when one recognizes one's own nature..."
"To escape birth and death—how do you escape when the light of the eyes falls to the ground? The Master spreads his two hands.

The student steps forward and says, "Once one has escaped birth and death, one knows the place of departure. When the four elements separate, to what place does one go? The Master says, "The Buddha Hall is right before you.
The student says, "Thank you for the instruction," bows, and returns to his place. The Master then says, "Today is indeed a..."

Master Xiānglǎo, fellow practitioner of the same *jùn* verse, has come specifically from our old friendship spanning over thirty years to visit me here in the mountains and request that I ascend the seat to exalt the Dharma for the great assembly.
Furthermore, when I formerly resided at my place of study, I personally received Master Xiānglǎo’s earnest encouragement, which I have long held fast in my heart.
Now that he has honored me with this visit, although we are both advanced in years, it is no longer...
In former times, we shared faces and sat with knees pressed together in pure conversation, encouraging one another as we recounted old acquaintances as if they were only yesterday.
One can see that this segment of luminosity remains unchanged and unalterable from antiquity to the present. Does the assembly know of this segment of luminosity?
If you know it, you may immediately cut off the three periods of time, remain far removed from birth and extinction, and let the single truth alone be revealed.
Profoundly still and unmoving—herein lies the seeing of one's nature through Zen meditation; herein lies the liberation from birth and death;
herein lies the place of departure. If this were not so, I shall provide further instruction. He then raised his whisk and said:
Do you see this very thing? It was seen thus in the past; it is seen thus now. Again, he strikes the whisk and says:
Do you hear this? It was heard thus in the past; it is heard thus now. Although the present and the past are different times, [the seeing and hearing remain the same].
How could there ever have been a distinction between seeing and hearing? Take, for instance, this single phrase: "not falling into seeing or hearing. How would you express it?
Auspicious vapors arise with the favorable turn of fortune; forest flowers form buds in early spring.
The lay practitioner Chixin Yu has mobilized the assembly to perform the Great Compassion Repentance Ritual (*Dabei Chanfa*). He requests that the Master ascend the hall.

Today, there is an ordinary person of great resolve named Chixin Yu in Fucheng. Because military conflict has not ceased for years in the Min region, various calamities have arisen in succession, leaving the living in misery and the world steeped in suffering;
at every turn, sorrow and bitterness are encountered. Consequently, he has specially initiated this cause to solicit the support of the assembly, requesting [the Master] from Gushan.

Virtuous practitioners of meditation, you cultivate the practice of the Great Compassion Repentance because you wish to move the compassionate power of the vows of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, so that he may sustain the world, protect all sentient beings, lead them together toward peace and stability, and provide them with benevolence and longevity.
At this very moment, your single thought and the great compassionate mind of Avalokiteśvara are of one essence and observed as one; they are non-dual and without distinction, like the sky.
The Universal Canopy is like the earth, universally supporting all sentient beings; they are all contained within it, receiving its sheltering shade and attaining liberation through it.
One must know that this mind is not possessed solely by the mental realm of a single individual, but is fully present in all sentient beings without exception.
It is simply because one is bound by attachments and entangled in craving and views that one is unable to expand [the mind].
If every person were to expand [their awareness] within a single thought-moment of the heart-mind, this would be the manifestation of the entire being of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.

One should direct a heart of loving-kindness toward all beings of the great earth and gaze upon them with eyes of compassion. Everywhere one goes, open the gate of compassion and propagate the transformation of compassion.
Thus, the world will naturally enjoy peace, the people will be healthy and prosperous, and things will flourish.

With the sovereign holding his hands high in non-action, the myriad states will all partake of this supreme bounty. This does not depend on any other artifice; it is simply the constant nature of one’s own mind.
Although it is thus, this is still merely a matter of meritorious achievement. One must further know that there is a singular path of the person’s own noble dignity before one can truly attain it.
Furthermore, what is this singular path of noble dignity? It breaks forth in the open, yet no one recognizes it;
it makes Namo Avalokiteśvara laugh to tears.

The Great Compassion Repentance was completed. The virtuous friends Li Wangshan, Li Hongtong, Yu Mingtai, Wang Jinzhong, Wang Qigang, Lin Wenruo, Zhang Daosu, Guo Zhanqing, and Chen Huisheng prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall.
The sun and moon of past and present, the mountains and rivers of past and present—though floating clouds shift and change, they do not concern them at all. Thus it is with Avalokiteśvara.
What purpose does a Bodhisattva serve by possessing so many hands and eyes? Were it not for Liu Yi delivering the letter, by what means could one have reached Lake Dongting?
[The Master] picks up his staff and says: "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva arrives! His whole body is everywhere;
to err by a hair’s breadth is to lose a thousand li. I entrust this to all of you: look with your own eyes at once! Is it?
"What? He struck the sounding block once and said, "The wondrous power of Avalokiteśvara’s wisdom can save the world from suffering. Again he struck the block once, descended from his seat, and said:
"Master Langxu has invited me to the hall on behalf of his parents. Every person has their own original father and mother; they follow one like a shadow follows a form."
It is manifest everywhere; alas, sentient beings themselves turn their backs on it. Today, it suddenly emerges in the center:

before is the Buddha Hall, behind is the Dharma Hall, to the left is the kitchen and storehouse, and to the right is the Sangha Hall. But tell me, as for that original father and mother in the middle—what is their countenance?
After a long silence, he said: "Above all, avoid touching upon a taboo."

The Dharma friend Chen Yunquan requested a formal lecture for the commemoration of his deceased relatives. A monk asked, "Today, the Dharma friend Chen Yunquan requests the Master to preach the Dharma for the sake of his ancestors.

Is this the same as or different from Prince Nalika dividing his bones to return them to his father and dividing his flesh to return it to his mother, so that he might manifest his true body to preach the Dharma for his parents?
The Master said, "You need only recognize your own true body. The monk stepped forward and said:
"If it is so, then he has personally attained liberation," [the student] said. The Master asked, "What is your own original body?
He replied, "I offer this profound mind to the dust-motes and lands. The Master said, "It still belongs to the realm of shadows and echoes.
The Master then said, "Today, the virtuous friend Chen Yunquan has come from afar from Wenling to request a word from this mountain monk to assist his parents in attaining rebirth. As for this..."

As for the parents of Yunquan: are they alive or dead? If they are alive, what need is there for ritual offerings to deliver them? If they are dead, whom then do the offerings deliver? Regarding this matter of life and death, how should one reason about it?
One must know that for those who live, there is nothing that lives; it is merely illusory existence. For those who die, there is nothing that dies; it is likewise merely illusory extinction.

Since both existence and non-existence are entirely illusory, that which is not illusory— *Note: This passage concludes with an ellipsis, as the original text appears to be an excerpt from a larger work (likely a Chan/Zen discourse record) concerning the non-duality of birth and death.*
How could existence and extinction, or concealment and manifestation, be subject to such distinctions? Furthermore, what is it that is not an illusion? Have you not seen the Patriarch say:
"Bubbles and illusions are equally unimpeded; why do you not awaken to this? To penetrate the Dharma within them is neither of this age nor of antiquity.
This refers to the bodies and minds of the great assembly present here and now, as well as those of your biological parents throughout all past kalpas. If...
Existing as if non-existent, they simultaneously emit light that mutually encompasses one another. Is there anyone here who has attained awakening?
If you can awaken, not only will the parents of Yunquan have been fully delivered, but the parents of all of you shall likewise be delivered.
There was nothing left out; it was not otherwise. On the morning of the birth of Siddhārtha, she further questioned Māyā.

On the Buddha’s birthday, the laywoman Jiang Chuanguo prepared in advance by requesting [the Master] to ascend the hall. The laywoman Jiang Chuanguo of Fucheng— *Note: The text appears to be a fragment of a Buddhist record or inscription. The phrase "明朝生悉達" (zhāomíng shēng xīdá) likely refers to the birth of Siddhārtha Gautama on the following morning. The repetition of "福城信女蔣傳果" at the end serves as a colophon identifying the patroness.*
Lay the foundation for a great field of merit in future lives. Furthermore, I request the mountain monk to turn the wheel of Dharma.
If you seek unsurpassed, great wisdom, know that cultivating merit through wisdom is true merit, and cultivating wisdom through merit is true wisdom.

When merit and wisdom are perfected together, one becomes a "Two-Legged Honored One," peerless in both the mundane and supramundane realms. Merit is the wondrous virtue of one's own mind; wisdom is one's own... [mind].
This wondrous light: if a person thoroughly penetrates the ground of the mind, all merit and wisdom will naturally become perfected.
But as for this very ground of one's own mind—how is it? Have you not heard it said: "In the heavens above and the earth below, I alone am the most honored"?
The Senior Monk Xianxin was invited to give a formal lecture while ill. A monk asked, "Fragrant clouds swirl about and the bells and drums resound;
what is the Master’s one phrase for the benefit of people today? The Master said, "You, Dharma brother, have already spoken it.

The monk pressed further, "To realize it before words is like digging the earth to find the sky; to take it up after the phrase is like swinging a club to strike at the moon. Neither before nor after—please [speak]."

The Master employed a skillful means. He held up his whisk. The monk stepped forward and said, "If one listens with the ears, it will ultimately be difficult to understand; only by hearing sound through the eyes can one truly know.
The Master said, "Outside of the skull, bring me a single phrase. The monk shook his sleeves and returned to the assembly. The Master said:
"I would give you thirty blows. The Master then said: "The Elder Xinxian has resided for many years at the Maitreya Hall on Mount Luo in Fuzhou.

He has lived apart from the world in pure cultivation and has disciplined himself in the construction and maintenance of the temple. Recently, having fallen ill, he resolved to return to his mountain retreat and requested this mountain monk to ascend the seat.
Now, all sentient beings possess the maladies of body and mind. The maladies of the body refer to the four marks [of birth, aging, sickness, and death]."
The maladies of the mind are the three poisons; alas, sentient beings do not realize this. Relying on the vigor of their blood and breath, they pursue sounds and forms without turning back.
Worldly physicians fold their hands in helplessness, unable to provide a cure. Only when the patient themselves recognizes the illness can medicine be administered.
Now tell me, what medicine will you prescribe? You must know that the illness itself is the medicine. Why is this?

It is because of the illness that one first realizes this body is suffering, empty, impermanent, and non-self. One is then able to turn back and investigate where this body comes from when born and where it goes when it dies.
By investigating without ceasing, one suddenly attains clear awakening regarding coming and going, and for kalpas of accumulated time, there is no longer any doubt.
That which was not yet understood is, in an instant, fully understood. An ancient worthy said, "Illness is the excellent medicine for sentient beings.

Is this not truly so? Nevertheless, this is still merely the mutual treatment of medicine and illness; one must further know that there is the matter of one's own fundamental nature before it is attained.
Do you not see how Guishan asked Dowu, "Where have you come from? Dowu said, "I have come from attending to the sick. Guishan said, "How many people are sick?
Dowu said, "There are those who are sick and those who are not. Guishan said, "Is the one who is not sick perhaps the Venerable Zhi?
Dowu said, "Whether sick or not sick, it does not concern him at all. Speak quickly, speak quickly! Guishan—
He said: "Even if you can speak it, it has no connection with him. Great assembly, look at these two venerable elders: one pressing, one nudging;

they briefly reveal their style and character, exhausting all their private resources until nothing remains. Not only does being ill have no concern with him, but even not being ill has no concern with him.
If you cannot speak it, it has no connection with him; even if you can speak it, it still has no connection with him."
A dialogue. Now tell me, who exactly is he? *Chan*.
At the request of the Venerable Kaimei, I ascend the hall. "Is it the wind that moves, or the banner that moves? The myriad phenomena of the universe are revealed all at once.
"It is neither the wind nor the banner that moves. The Buddhas of the three ages have nowhere to hide their bodies. It is your own mind that moves. Great!
The Junior Patriarch knew only that it was easy to open one’s mouth; he did not realize his tongue was so long. [The Master] held up his whisk and said, “Tell me, what is this?
It being noon, the venerable Kaimei provided a vegetarian feast; the mountain monk kept his mouth to eat the food.
[He] struck the whisk and descended from the seat.
On the Double Ninth, the filial son Chen Zhengmo offered a memorial for his father, Layman Chen Huyu, and requested that he ascend the hall.
Layman Chen Huyu had throughout his life maintained the fasts and recited the Buddha’s name; he delighted in goodness and took pleasure in giving.

Last year, at the age of seventy-five, he issued clear instructions to his descendants one by one before passing away peacefully. The power of his faith and progress can thus be known. This being the occasion—

At the first anniversary of the funeral rites (*xiǎoxiáng*), his son Zhèngmó and others, in strict accordance with his final testament, made offerings of rice to the monks at Gǔshān and requested the mountain monk to ascend the seat.
They sought to discover the whereabouts of their father’s original source of life (*běnmìng yuánchén*). An ancient said:
"The crimson sun is certain to sink toward the west; yet it remains unknown where the soul has gone. One must know that amidst the sky-reaching white waves, only those who exert effort can prevail.
How many people are there who can pick out the golden nugget? Only then is one a true master. Do you understand thoroughly?
Every year on the ninth day of the ninth month, chrysanthemums fill the earth with fragrance.

The monk Dunchao of Xiyin Temple, together with his virtuous friends Zheng Maoheng, Lin Tianzhang, and others, released captive animals, buried the remains of the dead, completed full repentance rites, and fed the monastic community.
He invited [the Master] to ascend the hall; amidst skulls strewn across the wilds, he loudly sang the melody of non-arising (*anutpāda*).
Facing life-and-death situations, he fully manifested the pivot of killing and giving life. This was something Zichan certainly did not know, and even King Wen had not yet seen. Yet...
The many teachers, monks, and virtuous friends of Fucheng City took it upon one shoulder to support him.
Having taken up this burden, he then ascended Mount Gu, where he cooked rice-less rice and boiled soup that was never damp, providing for the entire assembly.
He further requested the mountain monk to deliver a turning word to express his congratulations and praise. Tell me, what words could he have spoken? Do you wish to know? The world is too vast!
Peace! May all together ascend to benevolence and longevity.
The Abbot of Wénshàng invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. "The autumn wind is cool; the autumn night is long. The traveler who has not yet returned yearns for his hometown.
[He] struck the meditation seat and said: "What place is this? Everyone is right here. Be careful not to open your eyes!"
Bedwetting. Again, a case is cited. One day, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva instructed Sudhana to gather medicinal herbs, saying, "Bring back whatever is medicinal.
Sudhana surveyed the entire earth and found that there was nothing that was not medicinal; he returned and reported, "There is nothing that is not medicinal.
Mañjuśrī said, "Then bring back whatever is medicinal. Thereupon, Sudhana plucked a single blade of grass from the ground.
[Daowu] held up some grass and passed it to Mañjuśrī. Mañjuśrī took it and, holding it up, showed it to the assembly, saying: "This medicine can kill people, and it can also bring people to life.
The Master said: "The entire great earth is the illness; the entire great earth is the medicine. With such medicine as this..."

To treat such illnesses, it is complete without deficiency or excess, naturally and precisely fitting. One may say that Sudhana was skilled at gathering [the medicine], and Mañjuśrī was skilled at its application.

If there are those who take this medicine, it will immediately cause the illnesses of Buddhist Dharma and Chan practice, of self and other, arrogance, right and wrong, and attachment and aversion to suddenly arise;
yet their entire being will experience a sense of pervasive joy and liberation, and they may truly be called a free-spirited monk.
Although this is so, it only cures those who are ill. Suppose a person who is not ill should come—how would you treat them?
Do not regard the absence of affairs as being without affairs; often, affairs arise from the absence of affairs.
The Master arrived at Nanshan. Monk Ersheng invited him to ascend the hall. To sell "pine-wind" in the middle of winter is to be utterly ignorant of the season;
to beat a cloth drum at the Gate of Thunder is truly enough to make one laugh out loud. Nevertheless, one must simply take what is wrong and turn it into right:
performing a somersault in the midst of empty space, so that host and guest may find accord and the true pulse of the Dharma may flow on. [He] raised his staff.

He said, "It cannot be uttered even from a full mouth; it is picked up with a trusting hand. He struck the ground once and said, "The blind donkey’s Eye of the True Dharma was extinguished, yet it has opened again.
After it has opened, what then? After a long silence, he said, "Were it not for my brother-monk, the Abbot, who would there be to understand this together?
He struck the ground once more and descended from his seat.

The Master arrived at Shangsheng Temple. The venerable elder Jingwu, together with the lay devotees Zhu Jixi, Liu Xindu, Ye Zizhen, and others, prepared a vegetarian feast and invited him to ascend the hall.
The Master ascended the seat and offered incense, saying: "This one portion of incense is offered to Venerable Miaoying. He again offered incense, saying:
"This one portion of incense is offered to the Patriarch Caoshan Ji. I humbly pray that... [the incense burner]...
The flowers bloom once more; the garden of awakening experiences spring again. You ferry those lost at the crossroads with the precious raft and fan the true wind during this final age.

As he takes his seat, he says: "The venerable Master Miaoying and the ancestral patriarch Caoshan Ji—these two ancient sages have, for no reason, thrust their heads out upon this very patch of ground.
One acts as the elder brother, shaking his head at Guohuan; the other acts as the younger brother."
At the top, he raises his head; at the bottom, he wags his tail. He churns the world into a maelstrom and turns yin and yang upside down.
Even if one were to examine this closely, it would still be like winter observing the seasonal mandate of spring. I, this mountain monk, am a descendant of Master Ji’s lineage.

Although I have come today with the ancestral estate and the title deeds clearly in hand, I still dare not look upon them. Why? Because even in the first month of spring, the weather remains cold. I prostrate myself.
Please cherish this deeply.
The administrative officials of Kaiyuan Temple in Quanzhou—Shi Hang, Da Ji, Si, and Sheng—along with the various senior monks (upādhyāya), have escorted the Master back to the mountain.
They have prepared a vegetarian feast and invited him to ascend the hall. Perfectly identical to the great void, there is neither deficiency nor excess. This mountain monk has departed from Gushan.
When one arrives at Kaiyuan, Kaiyuan has the mountain monk, while Gushan has no mountain monk.
When one leaves Kaiyuan and returns to Gushan, Gushan has the mountain monk, while Kaiyuan has no mountain monk. How do you explain this principle of being neither deficient nor redundant?
Is it not the saying: "The clouds, mindless, emerge from the peaks; the birds, weary of flying, know how to return"? Wrong!

"Is it not that 'going, going' is actually not going, and 'coming, coming' is actually not coming? "Wrong. "Is it not that 'moving' is like drifting clouds, and 'stopping' is like the spirit of the valley?
"Wrong. "Ultimately, how can one avoid being wrong? *Pats the floor with his whisk.* "Stop wasting effort on such empty dreams.
He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.
A vegetarian feast was prepared on the birthday of Master Haoguang; he was invited to ascend the hall. "If there is neither birth nor non-birth, The iron ox strolls idly through fire.
How many cycles of the Xuanyuan era could there be? The pillar of dew stands clearly side-by-side with Geng.
But tell me: how old is this pillar of dew after all? Dust-mote kalpas, again dust-mote kalpas— Counting them all, even the sands of the ocean are exhausted.

Not clear. Contemplate the Sage, the Master of Stillness. Returning to the mountains to sweep the pagoda, he was invited to ascend the hall: "Within the white pagoda and amidst the green mountains, in the midst of the Great Samādhi of the Whole Body, neither birth nor death are spoken of;
at midnight, the sun is red. At this very moment, is there anyone who possesses true insight? Is there anyone who sees before?
What is the Master’s countenance like? If it exists, the gate of Gushan will not fall into desolation;
if it is otherwise, white waves will surge to the heavens—this is precisely when you must exert yourself.
The lay practitioner Chixin Yu invited the assembly to perform the second stage of the Great Compassion Repentance Ritual and requested the Master to ascend the hall.
A monk asked, "What is the mind of great compassion? The Master replied, "It flows forth clearly. The monk stepped forward and said, "Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva has arrived!"
The Master said, "What did I say to you just now? The student stepped forward and said, "I humbly wish you ten thousand blessings. The Master said, "Return to your place. The Master then continued:
"Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, with a single heart of great compassion, manifests a thousand hands and eyes.

Amidst the perilous and evil paths of this Sahā world, he bestows great fearlessness and grants great peace and happiness. Yet sentient beings do not know this; because they do not know it," [they remain in suffering].
The Bodhisattva’s compassionate heart grows ever more profound. At times he manifests within oysters and clams; at times within the gallbladder of an ox;
at times he becomes the wife of a horse-herder; and at times he takes the form of Master Zhigong. Through such diverse skillful means, he seeks to guide and lead beings everywhere.

Yet, alas, the delusion and ignorance of sentient beings remain exceedingly deep; they harbor internal strife within their own hearts, brandishing weapons against one another, and thus bring ruin upon themselves.

It is restricted to ordinary people. Falling into pits and ravines, their suffering is beyond words. With the city of merit as a moat and the mind as a palace, he was moved by every sight he encountered;
he gave rise to compassion based on the realization of our shared essence and made a vow to recruit the masses to perform the Great Compassion Repentance Rite for three years.

He did so universally on behalf of all people on earth to repent for transgressions and invoke blessings, praying for the attainment of peace and stability. Truly, this struck the very heart of contemplation.
The sound strikes the painful place of an old man. Now we enter the second period; having selected an auspicious day, we announce the commencement.
A special vegetarian feast is prepared, and I, this mountain monk, am invited to ascend the seat to proclaim this segment of karmic conditions.

It is my hope that everyone will together come to know this matter, together give rise to this mind, together cultivate this practice, and together realize this Dharma. Does the assembly yet know where this single thought within the heart-mind falls?
Ah! The heavens are high and the myriad forms are upright; the seas are vast and the hundred rivers flow toward them.

The filial son Wang Qigang offers this memorial service for his late father and requests that the Master ascend the hall. One’s original parents are truly such that even axes and hatchets cannot cut them open.
In the realm of birth and death, existence and non-existence, there is not even a grain of dust that separates them. Do you wish to know this matter of non-separation?
Wang Qigang, a virtuous friend from Guanzhong who has resided in Fujian Province for many years, was a man of utmost sincerity and compassion, courageous in his cultivation of merit.
His father, Master Yu Baogong, passed away at home at the age of ninety-two. Upon hearing the news of the funeral announcement, Qigang was so overcome with grief that he nearly lost consciousness.

Furthermore, harboring the regret that he was unable to see his father through to the end of life, he specifically made offerings of a meal to the monks at Gushan and requested a mountain monk to proclaim the Dharma of the School (Zongcheng) as a way to repay his boundless debt of gratitude.
You must know that when Qigang raised a thought, he met Master Baogong face-to-face;
this cannot be concealed or revealed by birth and death, nor can it be separated by the distance between Min and Shan provinces. Not only...

It was thus with Qigang and his father. Even so, all Buddhas, as well as all sentient beings, mountains, rivers, and lands, are of one and the same essence with Qigang—without duality, without division, without distinction, and without interruption.
At this very moment, do you understand? To offer this profound mind to every dust mote and land is what is called repaying the debt of gratitude to one’s father.
Take heed.
On the occasion of his sixtieth birthday, the Elder Ziyuan requested that he ascend the hall. Ziyuan asked:

"The Buddhas appear in the world for the sake of the one great cause and condition, desiring to lead sentient beings to open, reveal, awaken to, and enter the Buddha’s knowledge and vision. I ask: how shall this be done?"
"What is the Buddha’s knowledge and vision? The Master said, "Light shines forth from within a lacquered ink-pot. The student asked further, "'The Dharma abides in its place;
the characteristics of the world are eternally constant. What is this 'eternal constancy'? The Master said, "In front is the Buddha Hall; behind is the Dharma Hall.
The student asked, "This hall has but a single door, and it is moreover narrow and small. How is this so? The Master said:
"Let us go out from here. Jin said, "A single phrase, clearly transcendent; suddenly shedding the mind-monkey, the white ox is revealed.
The Master said, "Just right for plowing the field. Jin said, "Turning over the ocean of lands with a radiant face;
the Mount Sumeru bows its head in the dark. The Master said, "Why exert so much idle effort? Jin said, "The clouds have cleared at midnight."
"The golden crow appears; casually it illuminates the traveler at night. The Master said, "Look beneath your own feet.
Yuan bowed in prostration, and the Master then said, "Since you, Venerable Yuan, received the tonsure from my predecessor, you have found a place to turn yourself around within Zixia Cave.
Only then did you realize that rice is made from grain. From that time until now, for twenty years, you have been singing and laughing to yourself."
