It would not hinder you from becoming a free and easy man of the Way. Why? Because you have been summoned by the turning of the twelve hours. Is it today that you celebrate your sixtieth birthday?
You must know that beyond the curtain of the bright night, there is a distinct family style; before the hall of the withered tree, there is another kind of springtime.
It is where the two luminaries do not reach and where the four seasons do not shift. Not even a mustard seed city can contain it.

Comparing their numbers, even the *kalpa-stone* (the stone that lasts through an eon) cannot rival its hardness. Only the Stone General at the mouth of Lingyuan Cave is permitted to share its longevity.
But tell me, what excellence does this Stone General possess? Standing alone in the empty mountains with nothing to do, he passes his years of peace in continuous serenity.
Qingming Festival. The disciple Daxiang Li Sheng sends greetings to the Abbot, the Venerable Dongbai Guanzhu Yin.

A memorial service for the stupa and a vegetarian feast were held, and he was invited to ascend the hall. The Master said: "Severing the barrier of death, all is clearly and brilliantly manifest; the precious seal is dissolved and integrated."
Vast and open, it is perfectly manifest: clearly, at midday, three watches are struck. Who says that there is no trace left for the body to hide?
One can only find that one does not dwell in the two extremes, nor abide in the middle way. At this very moment, tell me:
where do the two senior monks, Dongbai and Yin, establish their dwelling and sustain their lives? Year after year, on the occasion of Cold Food and Qingming, the cuckoo calls amidst the flowers.
Mount Xue was filled with blood.
The official Chen Gongxuan, seeking blessings, prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. "The original nature of one's own mind is fundamentally pure;
it is only because of a single moment of delusion that one gives rise to immeasurable transgressions through the three karmas of body, speech, and mind. Only through wisdom..."
One who is able to awaken in a single thought can overturn and shatter delusion, thereby restoring the originally pure mind.
This mind is precisely the Buddha-mind. All afflictions and karmic obstructions are fundamentally empty and quiescent;

all wholesome dharmas and merits are inherently complete within it, requiring no external seeking. These two paths of delusion and awakening are truly the essential way to transform the ordinary person into a sage.
Furthermore, one must understand that those who are deluded are deluded by means of delusion regarding awakening, while those who have awakened are awakened by means of awakening regarding delusion.
It is like a person who falls to the ground and rises again from the ground; to seek to rise apart from the ground is ultimately impossible.
Nevertheless, there is a person who belongs neither to delusion nor to awakening, who is neither a sage nor an ordinary person, and for whom all causes and effects of sin and merit do not apply.
He cannot be confined. But tell me, what is this person’s true face? After a long silence, he called to the assembly, saying, "Return to the hall.
Disciple Xinfa offers this memorial for his teacher; he requests that the Master ascend the hall. All dharmas are unborn; the auspicious sprout originally has no root. One.
All phenomena are indestructible; a red furnace brimming with snow. If you can understand it thus, you will see through that which lies beyond the limit of time (*vīpāśyana*).
The Buddhas are ever present before you. The Great Auspicious Hermitage Master arrives! White clouds enshroud the mountain peaks; the bright moon descends upon the river ahead.
The assembly descended from their seats.
The Chief Administrator Bao-shan, Qing-heng, Wen-zhi, and Nei-ying prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall.

At this time, when we are in the final age and the Buddha-Dharma is in decline, the Great Man has returned by virtue of his vows to remedy the deficiencies of the times, propagate the Dharma, benefit sentient beings, and repay the Buddha’s kindness.
The Patriarch said: "It is not for the sake of some idle name that one forces oneself to emerge from seclusion and stage a spectacle to be ridiculed by the mundane world.
In the past, the Elder Master Zhangshi bore the seal of the White Horse and propagated the Way of Yunqi; he founded the two monasteries of Zhenji and Baoshan.
For thirty years, he could find no one who truly understood him. It was only in his later years that he finally encountered my late master."

The Master alone, having already been verified for the identity of his wisdom and realization, was subsequently granted the transmission of the Precious Precepts; it has now been more than thirty years since then.
This mountain monk once composed a eulogy for the portrait of my late teacher, saying: "He shook the hand-drum of Mount Yiyong and sold the antiques of Yunqi;
after more than thirty years of entering the mud and water, he finally met the former master as one nostril with another. Life and death, breath and sigh."
The Common Wind: Sound and Light pierce the dream of Jambudvīpa; a single drop of the Tiāoxi River flows upstream.

One knows not whether it is a ferry or a cavern—this is indeed a true record. When this mountain monk was eighteen years old, having just left his place of study, he received the precepts under the venerable Preceptor and personally accepted his guidance.
Furthermore, he was instructed to visit the former Master at Mount Hé. It has been so until this day.
When our late master swept the mountain gate, he was in every way honored by the instructions and admonitions of the venerable teacher.

Now, the Chief Administrator Baoshan Qingheng and the Inner Radiance of the Monastery, the Senior Seat-holders Wenzhi and Zhushang, have come from afar bearing letters and gifts from the various Dharma-protectors.

Because the Abbot has passed away, they have specifically requested that this mountain monk once again shake up the collapsing order, so as not to allow the legacy left by our predecessors to fall to the ground all at once.
Reflecting on the roots of the tree and the source of the water, it is logically difficult to turn back [the current].

He then brought forth the account of the meeting between the former master and his teacher, wishing for everyone to know where these two elders arrived, so that you would not merely act like a dwarf watching a performance, rising and falling along with others.
I dare ask the assembly: ultimately, where does the crux of this encounter between the two great elders lie?
In a certain place, two monks were competing to provide a verbal response. The Master said, "Not yet. He then said, "A wooden man holds a board and strikes it amidst the clouds;
a stone woman holds a flute and blows it beneath the water. When someone asked, "What about you, Preceptor?
he could not help but say to him, "How would I dare go against [the truth]? Then he descended from his seat.
The Great Compassion Repentance is complete. Disciples Lin Tae-ding and Chen Tae-yuk have prepared a vegetarian feast and requested the Master to ascend the hall.
May you awaken to the Way upon hearing its sound and clarify the mind upon seeing its form. Water does not wash water; gold is not bartered for gold. It is just as Yunmen said:
"The Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara buys a sesame cake with money. When he lets go of his hand, it turns out to be a steamed bun. How would you explain this?

"How so? He shouted, "If one had known early on that rice is made of grain, why wait until now to endure hunger? He spoke again: "The incantations are complete; the three-week period has reached its fulfillment.
To celebrate this feast, there is no wish that will not be granted. The waves of the four seas are clear and still;
throughout the heavens, all share in the joy of a time of great peace. He descended from his seat.
On the Buddha’s Birthday, the lay disciple Zheng Dao-shi of Fucheng, together with his son Lin Taiding, prepared a vegetarian feast and invited the Master to ascend the hall.
The Master took up his staff, struck it once, and said: "Siddhārtha comes this morning in such a manner;
The lotus blooms anew within the fire. A fragrant breeze rises, pervading the void and the world; Extraordinary and numinous sprouts are planted everywhere. Only...
This very thing—can the nine dragons’ spouting water ever wash it away? Can Yunmen’s striking with his staff ever strike it back?
Even if you were to have eyes all over your body, you could not discern it; even if you had mouths all over your body, you could not praise it enough.
Tell me, what is this that is so extraordinary? Do you understand? It is always in the midst of the marketplace, yet it is beyond reach.
"Everyone knows this. He struck the floor once more and descended from his seat.
The Senior Monk Zhileng requested the Master to ascend the hall. The Master took up his staff and said, "This mountain monk does not know how to speak of Chan;
all day long I shut my door and sleep. Fortunately, there is this senior monk who can expound it for me. He struck the floor once more and said:
Below, it is not in the earth; above, it is not in the heavens; in the middle, it is not within; to the sides, it is not at the boundaries.
It is bare and naked, stark and clear, with nothing to grasp. If there is anyone who can pick it out, they may roam freely across the world;

they will not see even a hair’s breadth of any phenomenon acting as an obstruction or hindrance. If they cannot pick it out, they will be lost by it and wander aimlessly, crashing into things to the east.
"Xike! Alas, how bitter it is, O Buddha! Is there anyone present who can now pick this up? He strikes the sounding block once and says, "Take care.
The filial son Huang Zhixiong and others, on behalf of their deceased parents, request that you ascend the hall. The former sages have said: "The three realms, above and below..."
Regarding all phenomena (*dharma*), I say they are entirely mind. Apart from these various mental states, nothing else can be found.
Do you wish to recognize the mind? Heaven is it; hell is it; even becoming a Buddha or an Ancestor is it. It is like a dream experienced last night:
while a person lies upon their bed, the dreamscapes may differ in a thousand ways, yet upon waking, there is absolutely nothing to be found. Even if one has not yet awakened, it is likewise so.
It is not truly existent. Arriving at this point, it is simply a matter of valuing the person upon the bed who recognizes themselves;
then, whether one is awake or not, whether one attains it or not—all such talk becomes superfluous. I dare ask the assembly: Ultimately, how does one recognize this very person?
After a long silence, he said: "Not recognizing, not recognizing. He spoke again: "The merit of having thus expounded the Great Dharma above..."
Virtue. On behalf of his filial sons, Hwang Ji-hong and Ji-kwon, etc., this is offered to dedicate for their late father, Hwang Gong Jin-shu (a Wenlin Lang), and his late wife, Lady Guo.

We repent of all transgressions and evils to adorn the ground of retribution. We humbly pray that the gates of the netherworld be suddenly shattered, so that they may manifest bodies of pure radiance;
and that they may transcend to the Land of Ultimate Bliss and realize the stage of *avaivartika*.
The lay official Huang Jianwu entered the mountains to establish an Almsgiving Festival for the Ullambana Sūtra and requested the Master to ascend the Dharma Hall.

"The aged parents upon the hall are truly living Buddhas; To serve and nourish them with such earnest devotion brings boundless merit. May this further assist our deceased mother and all kinsmen, So that all may ascend together to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
The assembly must know: Elder Jianwu’s vast resolve originated from the way of filial piety.

Now tell me: from where does this filiality arise? If you can recognize its point of origin, not only will your parents of the present life enjoy a hundred years of fortune and happiness, but your parents of the seven past generations will be reborn in the heavens.

Furthermore, all sentient beings throughout the entire Dharma-realm and the realm of empty space—including every crawling and moving creature—will be gathered within the sphere of unconditioned compassion (*nirālamba-maitrī*), and at once realize the Unborn.

The Dharma-patience of Birth has departed. Do you understand this in full detail? This old monk personally emerged from the abbot’s quarters and ascended the hall to proclaim the ancestral style before the assembly.
He then raised his whisk and called to the multitude, saying: "What is this? If you were to fix your gaze even for a moment longer, there would be no need to meet me at all.
On the birthday of the Master of Xingmou Village, the disciples Chunlin, Zhi, and others have prepared this vegetarian feast and invited you to ascend the hall.
That which is called the body is the convergence of three conditions; that which is called longevity is the shifting of the two luminaries. It is like drifting clouds arising from the vast void.
If great waves pour into a vast chasm, one must know that the true body is formless; it equalizes the ten realms as one single body.

True life does not transmigrate; it is eternally quiescent within each moment. It is neither born nor extinguished; neither ordinary nor holy; neither internal nor external; neither decreasing nor increasing.
Even if you were to awaken in this manner, you would still fall into the dharma-body and remain within the realm of numerical quantity. Therefore:
In the past, a monk asked Dongshan, "Among the three bodies, which one does not fall into the category of enumeration?
Dongshan said, "I am always most earnest regarding this. Later, the monk asked Caoshan, "What is the meaning of 'I am always most earnest regarding this'?
Caoshan said, "If you want your head, cut it off right now. He then asked Xuefeng; Xuefeng struck him in the mouth with his staff and said, "I too—"
"I have come to Dongshan. Tell me, assembly: where exactly does the intent of these three great elders lie?

*Du!* It would be better to cut out one's tongue. Nevertheless, as for the monastery steward Xingmao, who has assisted the monastic community for over thirty years with diligence and prudence, through sincere practice and a sincere heart—on this first day of the ninth month, it happens to be his sixtieth birthday."

The first cycle: A phrase for celebrating and praising during a vegetarian feast. Furthermore, how is it? Do you understand? Plucking chrysanthemums beneath the eastern fence, I see the Southern Mountain in its profound stillness.

The Nülu Zhangjing (Bannerman) Mr. Xiong, whose courtesy name was Jinxue, performed the ritual of reciting the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas* and provided a vegetarian feast for the monks, requesting them to ascend the hall.

Regarding the single gate of repentance, which is praised by all Buddhas and practiced by everyone from the stage of Equal Enlightenment downward—just as Samantabhadra, the eldest son of the *Avataṃsaka*, made the ten great kings of vows, the fourth of which states: "I repent of my karmic obstructions"—how much more so should this apply to others?
Ordinary worldlings of vast capacity have not yet attained the fruits of sainthood; their attachments everywhere are none other than transgressions. Alas, they do not realize this.

Yet, though they do not realize it, it is not that they are without transgression. It is like writing characters in the dark: when the fire is extinguished, the characters remain, and by the time day breaks, the characters finally become manifest.
Only the wise perceive this beforehand; they deeply reproach themselves, quieting their minds and reforming their conduct to restore [themselves).
This returns one to the fundamental goodness. Therefore, the Elder Śākyamuni issued this admonition: "Commit no evil; practice all that is good;

purify your own mind—this is the intention of all Buddhas. You must know that among the Buddhas of the three periods of time and the patriarchs of successive generations, there is not a single person who attained perfect enlightenment without purifying this mind. As for the phrase "purifying the mind" alone—how is it? It is the fundamental.
Upon arrival, there is not a single thing; one must strictly avoid stirring up dust of one’s own making. Shattering the realm of Jambudvīpa, the body of the Dharma King is revealed alone.
Take care.
The Beile Zhangjing Chen Gong, whose name is Jiuzhou, accompanied his son Shou into the mountains to pay homage to the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas* and provide a vegetarian feast.

The Assembly requests the Master to ascend the hall. The appearance of a thousand Buddhas in the world is not for any other purpose than to cause all sentient beings throughout the great earth to see their own original nature and bring an end to birth and death.
Why is this? It is because every person possesses an original nature; it is simply that they do not see it.
Although it is not seen, it cannot be said that it does not exist. Every person has birth and death; they simply refuse to bring it to an end.
Although they do not bring it to an end, it cannot be said that it exists. Birth and death do not exist, yet the fundamental nature is not non-existent.

Bringing this all forth at once, he offers it as a gift to the great assembly. Holding up his whisk, he asks: "What is this? If you can see directly here and now, [you will realize] that which has come down from kalpas of antiquity...
The matter lies right now. Infinite birth and death are, in a single moment, completely purified. Is this not a cause for celebration?
If it were otherwise, you must investigate with all your might: this birth and death is clearly existent; why did the Elder of Gushan say it does not exist?
This original nature is fundamentally unseen and fundamentally unheard; why did the Elder of Gushan say...
What does it mean that there is nothing that is not present? Through constant inquiry and investigation, one day there is a vast and sudden awakening.
It is like the sun rising in the sky; there is no hidden corner it does not illuminate. One’s own field of experience becomes entirely clear and manifest.

Thereafter, one uncovers the great hidden treasury and universally benefits all beings with abundant ease. This may truly be called a supreme man, transcending both the mundane and the supramundane. To him, the three... [text ends]
To walk hand in hand with the thousand Buddhas of this world—how could one be unworthy of such honor? O Great Assembly, a human body is difficult to obtain and the Great Dharma is difficult to hear.
Time does not wait for anyone; you must exert yourselves with all your might. Take care.
On the birthday of the Venerable Master Zongshen, his disciples Fayan and others prepared a vegetarian feast and invited him to ascend the hall. [The Buddha said:
"Arising in one place and ceasing in another, it does not flow further into a second thought.

Just as for us humans, from the moment we are born on this earth, from childhood to youth, and from youth to old age, the years, months, days, and hours undergo momentary flux and transformation—this constitutes the 'second thought.'"

"It is not the second thought. After a long silence, he said: "The green creeper winds its way straight up to the crest of the cold pine; the white clouds drift lightly, appearing and disappearing within the great void.
All dharmas are fundamentally at rest; it is only man who creates his own clamor. He gave a shout and asked, "What is there to clamor about? Then he added:

"In this degenerate age of the Final Dharma, Chan and the precepts are in disarray. When our former master appeared in the world, he strove with all his might to shake up what had fallen into decline."

Gang was a successor to Shouchang in the Chan lineage and propagated the precepts at Zhenji; thus, the source and its stream remained undisturbed, and the transmission from teacher to disciple was without error.

At the age of eighty, he once remarked that the "Great Good Mountain" of Shouchang’s single seat had been cast to Daopei, which was much like using a single hair to pull a thousand-jin weight—a task for which he felt ashamed, as he could not bear such a burden.
He then entrusted the precept-dharma of Zhenji to the various masters, including Kui and Cun, each of whom...

The four-line verse expresses faith. In these verses, the first two lines always describe the Dharma-gate realized within one's own mind, while the latter two lines demonstrate the intent of entrusting the precepts.
Alas, Xueqiao Mocui and the other masters have all already passed away;
furthermore, Master [So-and-so] has been rebuked by our late teacher for recklessly handling the lineage of the school. Now, there remains only Zongsheng.
Master Shan is here. Master Shan has served his late teacher with the ritual water vessel and towel for many years.

Having personally received the Vinaya precepts and taught the junior disciples, he will surely be able to honor his late teacher’s earnest entrustment, continue the noble legacy of Zhenji, and increase the lifespan of the Buddha.

To cause the Dharma to endure for a long time, today marks the fiftieth anniversary since the initial ordination of Master Shan. It coincides precisely with the anniversary of the passing of my late teacher.

His disciple Fayan and others have prepared a vegetarian feast and requested that I ascend the seat to specifically proclaim the Zen precepts entrusted by my late teacher and his intent to uphold the Dharma during the Final Age, thereby informing the great assembly.
Furthermore, I do not dare to imitate the benedictions of common people by offering excessive praise or hyperbolic eulogies.
Why is this? Have you not seen the Way? I have offered prayers for this for a long time. I humbly entreat you to take care of yourself.
Master Zhixiu, acting as the abbot, has established a vegetarian feast to celebrate his teacher’s longevity and invited him to ascend the hall. This body of the four elements is empty by nature;
if one does not know it is empty, it cannot be avoided to speak of it. Before entering the womb, where was it? One.

When breath no longer comes, and the firewood meets with flame, the ashes fly and the smoke vanishes. Where, then, does one abide? Since there is nothing before or after, how could there be anything in between?
If there is nothing in between, why is it called "the first degree of fifty"?
Have you not heard it said: "It is like an illusion"? The Patriarch said: "Bubbles and illusions are equally unobstructed; why do you not awaken to this? To realize this is to attain enlightenment.
The Dharma is within it; it is neither of the present nor of the past. The Master then rose and addressed the assembly, saying: "Is this not a bubble and an illusion?
What, then, do you call 'unimpeded'? This is not unimpeded; what, then, do you call a 'bubble and an illusion'?
If one awakens here, the realms of infinite lands—self and others—are not separated by even the tip of a hair. Ten ages..."
From antiquity to the present, from beginning to end, nothing departs from the present moment. If it were otherwise, observe how one idly watches the passing of years;
when would this migration ever cease? If for even a single kṣaṇa there were true stillness, the hundred rivers would surely flow backward.

The Chan Master Zu Xin held a vegetarian feast to offer congratulations on his teacher’s birthday and invited him to ascend the hall. Once one has entered the gate of faith, they immediately ascend the seat of the patriarchs.
But how does one have faith? The entire ten directions of the world is but a single person; infinite hundreds of thousands of kalpas are but a single lifespan.
With such a lifespan, one celebrates the life of such a person—a life that is neither long nor short, neither decreasing nor increasing. Furthermore...
The Way. What person is this person? What lifespan is this lifespan? Do you understand this thoroughly yet? Peach blossoms and flowing waters vanish into the distance;
there is another world and heaven, not of this human realm.
Pure One, the Abbot, together with his fellow practitioner Chen Huisheng, requested the Master to ascend the hall to celebrate his birthday.
Half a century of this floating life has passed in vain; I know my errors, yet I am utterly bewildered by fate. Eating when hungry and drinking when thirsty, I pass through days as usual;
Laughing until half my mouth is split open, I pierce the void of space. A fellow such as this, lacking any breakthrough, Cannot distinguish the small from the large months, nor the years.

As for the intercalary months and surplus days, they are neither gathered by the sages nor managed by them; it would be well to cast them directly into the realm of non-arising, so that not even a single point of emergence can be found.
What use is there in painting their eyebrows for them or pointing with one's fingers, piling up flowers and clustering brocades? Nevertheless—
This fellow, however, does have one point of merit: he knows how to explain to people that rice is made from grain and that a cauldron is cast from iron.
If you do not believe him, try examining it for yourself, one by one, at the mouth of your own stove and the opening of your own mouth.
The various officers of the two orders and the assembly of elders prepared a Dharma robe for the Lion to celebrate his longevity and requested that he ascend the hall.
In this Lion-like monastic community, lions surround him; those who crouch on the ground do so, those who roar do so, those who perform backflips do so, and those who roll the ball do so.
Thus, his majestic radiance becomes so formidable that all other beasts hide their tracks and purple vapors rise upward.
Teng. The multitude of demons fled their tracks. For a thousand ages thereafter, people have gazed up at him with reverence, sighing that none could equal him.
It is just like when a monk asked an ancient worthy: "When a lion seizes an elephant, it exerts its full strength; when a lion seizes a rabbit, it likewise exerts its full strength."
I do not yet understand: by what power is this achieved? An ancient worthy said, "The power of non-deception. O Great Assembly, do you wish to know the power of non-deception? [He lets out a shout.
"In this dharma-ending age, the winds of decadence are beyond description; foxes, wolves, and jackals fill the universe."
With hearts as red as cinnabar, we forget guest and host; together we bear the Tathāgata’s True Dharma Gate. May the Great Assembly take heed!

The Dharma-protectors Fang Chenlin and others of Fucheng, along with their fellow practitioners from the same pool of mind and space, have led the fourfold assembly to offer a vegetarian feast for the Master’s birthday and requested that I ascend the hall.
Today marks the fiftieth anniversary of my mother’s passing. I humbly receive the assembly...

The patrons who protect the Dharma, preceptors, teachers, and fellow practitioners of the Way, each bringing clouds of incense, clouds of flowers, clouds of music, and clouds of eloquent speech, as well as various wondrous offerings, come to present their worship.
You must know that this entire array of merit is neither merely adding flowers upon brocade nor lighting a fire in a cold hearth;
it is intended to cause everyone to realize the existence of that which has not yet entered the womb of its parents.
The previous "one phrase" is just like this very "one phrase. Does it have years and months? Does it have a lifespan?
Does it have length or brevity? Since that [other] does not exist, can this possibly exist?
Are this and that one or two? Can you definitively determine this? Have you not seen how, in the past, National Preceptor Yan...?
The Master asked Senior Monk Fu, "Before your parents were born, where was your nose? Fu said, "Brother, you go first.
The National Teacher said, "Now that you are born, where is it? Fu did not approve. The National Teacher then asked Fu, "How about it?
Fu merely shook his fan. The National Teacher then gave Fu a punch. "O Assembly! The National Teacher..."
[The Master] performed a fist-punch. He asked, "As for the distance between you and Elder Fu as you shake the fans, how much is it?

You must know that these two great elders—one shaking his head, the other wagging his tail—struggle for spring flowers upon a shadowless tree and distinguish beauty from ugliness before a stone mirror.
If someone can understand it here, I invite them to eat the midday meal; if they do not understand, I likewise invite them to eat at noon.
A vegetarian feast. Why is this so? It is because all have their share.

For the sake of celebrating the Master’s birthday, the assembly of fellow practitioners—including Linpu, Lin Yin, Ziqu, Shui, Taihe, Pan Ziqi, and others—has prepared this vegetarian feast and invited him to ascend the hall.
"The number of the Great Derangement is fifty; its application consists of forty-nine. Zhaozhou...
Holding up tea; Caoshan offers wine; the Gandharva King presents music. From the unperforated flute, the song of original existence is sung.
I respectfully congratulate the person of no-position on a thousand years of life, ten thousand years of life. But as for this person of no-position—does he still receive it or not?
The red wheel shines across the earth; beneath the sea, no flowers are planted.

Layman Lin Danzhang has solicited the assembly to bury the remains of the deceased and perform memorial rites for their rebirth. He requests that I ascend the hall. From beginningless time, we have been thus.
Within the realm of birth and death, as one discards this body and receives another, one does not know how many *gaṅgā-nadī-vāluka* kalpas have passed.

In each and every lifetime, there have been parents and various kinsmen; if one were to examine the entire earth, among all men and women, whether living or dead, there is none who has not been one’s own relative.
Yet, having changed forms and undergone different retributions, they no longer recognize one another. Now that the time for a great upheaval has arrived, [the cycle of] killing...
The vital energy flows recklessly, and many among the common people perish by untimely death. Consequently, coffins are broken and corpses cast aside, lying in chaotic disarray everywhere;
blown by the wind and scorched by the sun, they are devoured by sparrows and ravens. Having no master and no refuge, who will take pity upon them?

There was a virtuous man of Puṇyavardhana City named Lin Danzhang, whose grief for this plight weighed heavily upon his heart. He therefore specially initiated a fundraising campaign and personally [undertook the task].

The remains were collected, and both men and women were cremated; in total, there were one thousand eight hundred and some more. When the rites were completed, he again performed extensive Buddhist ceremonies to ferry them across to liberation.
It can be said that sentient beings who had not previously seen such extraordinary signs were entirely transformed into members of the same spiritual family.
To pray for the peace and prosperity of the nation and to lead one’s parents and kin to benevolent longevity—all this is the natural principle of karmic response. Although...
However, you must further know that it was only through the karmic conditions of the Seven Virtuous Women that this was attained.
Formerly, when the World-Honored One was traveling through the Śītavana cemetery with the Seven Virtuous Women, one woman pointed to a corpse and said to her sisters, "The corpse is right here;

where has the person gone? Another woman asked, "How? How? Sisters, observe closely! Each of them then realized the truth through their own awakening, moving Śakra Devendra to scatter flowers over them.
Huayan said, "I only pray that you, Holy Sister, will let me know what it is you require; I shall provide for you for the rest of my life.
The woman said, "In my home, the seven treasures and the four requisites are all fully provided. I require only three things: first, a single tree without roots."
Second, a single expanse where there is neither yin nor yang; third, a mountain valley where a shout produces no echo.
Śakra said, "Everything that is required is present here; as for these three things, I truly have none. The woman said, "If you do not possess these," [she continued].
Desiring to resolve this for the benefit of others, he went together with him to see the Buddha and reported the matter as above.
The World-Honored One said, "Kauśika, even my great disciples, the Arhats, do not understand this meaning; only the great Bodhisattvas can understand it.
The Master then addressed the assembly, saying: "All dharmas are unborn; all dharmas are unceasing. If one can thus..."
"Understood! The Buddhas are constantly manifest before us. The seven virtuous women each attained realization and clearly perceived them one by one as being ever-present.
They then approached Śakra and requested three kinds of things. Śakra said, "I truly have nothing to give. This may be called "placing the entire dish on the table.
The World-Honored One said, "Even my great Arhat disciples do not understand this meaning; it is only those [who can]."
Great Bodhisattvas, you may understand this meaning: it is still possible to deceive one who is clear-sighted, but it is difficult to hoodwink one who is in the dark.
Today, someone asked Gushan: "Friend Lin Danzhang has collected eighteen hundred skulls;
where do the people go? [Gushan] held up his whisk and said: "Simply tell him: they are all upon the tip of this mountain monk’s whisk."
Sitting upon a precious lotus flower, he has departed to attain Equal and Perfect Enlightenment. Do you all see him yet? *Pah!* Be careful not to let your eyes grow dim.

Nun Yiran of the Jingci Hall requested the Master to ascend the hall for a discourse. The Master said: "Vimalakīrti said, 'According as the mind is pure, so is the Buddha-land pure. This is the meaning of purity.
The Lotus Sutra says, 'Cultivate the body with compassion and skillfully enter the Buddha-wisdom. This is the meaning of compassion."
This is the meaning. Indeed, by cultivating the body through compassion, one enters the wisdom of the Buddha; by cultivating the body through purity, one purifies the Buddha-lands.
When this is so, all precepts, meditative concentration, wisdom, merit, and spiritual powers are complete within oneself. Why then seek them elsewhere in a fragmented manner?
Today, the Venerable Yiran of Jingci Monastery has specifically ascended Mount Gu shan to request the precepts and seek the Dharma; it is for this reason.
Seeking elsewhere is not seeking; seeking not elsewhere is also not seeking. Alas! Were it not for the geese arriving at night, how could one perceive the autumn at the sea gate?
Nizi Zude was invited to ascend the hall. The Bhikṣuṇī Zude said: "One seeks the precepts and seeks the Dharma, yet the precepts and the Dharma are fundamentally not external;
they are entirely complete within one's own mind. When the mind is empty, that is itself the precept; originally there is not a single thing. When the mind is true, that is itself..."
The Dharma does not arise or perish throughout the kalpas. If one can awaken to one’s own mind, the precepts and the Dharma are attained all at once.
As for this very mind of one's own—how is it awakened? At midday, the third watch strikes; at midnight, the sun rises. *Chan*.
The two venerable masters Faguang and Fayu requested that he ascend the hall. When the Buddha appeared in the world and the Patriarch came from the West, the Dharma-gate was opened wide everywhere.
He cast down this very thing right before one's face, wishing to cause the impoverished son to return home early.
Jizhi’s finger, Mimi’s staff, Yunmen’s "moldy cake," and Zhaozhou’s tea—if you are willing to come, I shall hand it over to you face-to-face; if you do not come, then...
Separated by the distance of the heavens for so long. Today, the two venerable ones, Faguang and Fayu, have come to seek the precepts and request the Dharma.
How shall this mountain monk respond? The mother-born eyes are originally bright and clear; there is no need to scatter further sand within them.
At the request of Jiezile Daojizhao Xiangguang of Qingcheng Temple, I ascend the hall.

In the past, when the World-Honored One first attained perfect enlightenment beneath the Bodhi tree, he immediately established the precepts. This is because the precepts are the foremost of the Three Studies and the source of the myriad practices;
they are the essential path by which both the mundane and supramundane realms must necessarily pass. Why is this? Because the three miserable realms exist due to the absence of the precepts.
They fall [into the lower realms]. Humans and devas are born because they possess precepts; even Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas attain their status through precepts;
Bodhisattvas cultivate through precepts; and the fruit of Buddhahood is realized through precepts.

As for those in the three miserable realms (*trāya*), these are those who currently do not hear the Buddha-dharma, do not believe in cause and effect, act according to their own whims, and extensively accumulate various offenses. As for humans and devas, these are those who currently remain steadfast...
Those who uphold the five precepts and practice the ten wholesome deeds are such [people].

As for the Arhats and Pratyekabuddhas, they are those who, having now ascended the platform following the *jñapti-caturtha-karman* (the formal ritual of fourfold proclamation), constantly observe the two hundred and fifty precepts; their every movement is pure, and they are practitioners of the Four Noble Truths.
As for the Bodhisattvas, they are those who have now generated the Great Mind, established the Great Vows, and carry out the Great Deeds, with their resolve set upon [attaining] the...

This is what it means to ascend to Bodhi. As for the fruit of Buddhahood—wherein the three aggregates are perfected and myriad virtues are fully endowed—it is none other than our original teacher, Śākyamuni, the World-Honored One.
One can see that within the ten dharma realms, the distinctions between the holy and the mundane, the defiled and the pure, all exist by virtue of this precept.
As the saying goes: "Who can depart without passing through the door? Who does not follow this path? Now...

The senior monks Nikyō, Jōraku, Dōjaku, Shōkō, and others entered the mountains to seek the precepts and specifically requested that [the Master] ascend the seat to reveal the intent behind the Tathāgata’s establishment of the precepts for the fourfold assembly present here.

Furthermore, each was asked to examine carefully the aspiration generated at the stage of practice: is it to seek the precepts of humans and devas? Is it to seek the precepts of Arhats or Pratyekabuddhas? Or is it to seek...?
Is this the Bodhisattva precepts? Or is it the precepts sought for the sake of attaining the fruit of Buddhahood? This is for the wise to discern for themselves with skill.

O virtuous ones, a human body is difficult to obtain, and the Buddha-dharma is difficult to encounter. Now that you have obtained a human body and encountered the Buddha-dharma, to leave the household life and receive the precepts is no small matter.
You should each, in this regard, give rise to a resolute mind and establish a firm resolve, cultivating your bodies.
By means of the precepts, cultivate the mind; by means of wisdom, destroy the cycle of birth and death from its beginningless origin and perfect the fruit of Buddhahood in a single lifetime.
When one’s kindness is shared with others and both self and others are equally benefited, one may be called a true disciple of the Buddha and one who truly repays the Buddha’s grace.
I humbly hope that the assembly will each exert themselves and take care of yourselves. Adieu.
On the day the Buddha attained enlightenment, the nuns Daoshan, Shishi, Hongyi, Chuanghui, Chuangyu, Yi, Xian, and others earnestly requested that he ascend the hall.
"Before beholding the morning star, he was Siddhārtha; after beholding the morning star, he was Siddhārtha. How could there ever have been two Siddhārthas?
It is the sentient beings who give rise to views and distinguish for themselves. What happened at that time is this very day; what happens this day is [the same as] that time."
That very moment—today and that moment are one and the same. Sentient beings give rise to views and thus fragment themselves;
without discrimination, there is no fragmentation. Directly beneath, the lotus blooms from the mud. Śākyamuni the Old Man cannot see it;
the dark-skinned ox and the white buffalo are smiling. O Great Assembly, tell me: how far apart are the dark-skinned ox and the white buffalo from Śākyamuni the Old Man?
"Little. I allow only the Old Barbarian to understand; I do not allow the Old Barbarian to know.
At the request of the Venerable Master of the Lotus School, I ascended the hall.

The Venerable Master of the Lotus School was so earnest in his quest for the Dharma that yesterday he prostrated himself upon the ground, his tears falling like rain, seeking instruction on the path to transcend birth and death. To him, I said:
I shall bring forth birth and death for you. This turning phrase is like the Vajra King’s precious sword;
it is wielded in its entirety before one's face. If you can grasp it directly and cut through with a single stroke, will not your life be brought to full realization?
Since he does not understand, I cannot help but explain it from the beginning today: "The existence of 'self' is birth and death; realizing the emptiness of self is liberation."
Birth and death: to rejoice when praised and to become angry when reviled is birth and death.

To feel no joy when praised and no anger when reviled—realizing that both the one who praises and the one who receives praise, as well as the one who reviles and the one who receives revilement, are both merely dreams—one then transcends birth and death.
This is the single great highway leading to heaven; if you can walk straight along it, you will return home and personally behold that which is without [form].

Only one who has realized the nature of birth and death can then turn themselves around, enter the realm of birth and death, kindle the great Dharma-torch, and board the great Dharma-ship to ferry across those mired in the ocean of suffering and shatter the profound darkness of the great earth;
only then does one truly fulfill the vow of leaving home to study the Way. I venture to ask: who is it that is ultimately free from birth and death? Do you understand this clearly?
"Ma! A shigu (nun) is fundamentally not a woman; simply look at it this way.

Master Línxū, while seeking precepts for his disciples, requested that the Master ascend the hall. "One person possesses eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, yet does not know a single hair's breadth of sound or form.
Another person lacks eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind, yet [knows] a single hair's breadth of sound and form."

"Not Ignorant" (Bumèi). The two men arrived together at Gushan to seek ordination. [The master] was to confer the precepts upon the one who did not know [the ritual], while the one who was "Not Ignorant" was to receive them as well.

As for the one who did not know: he did not know how to request the precepts when instructed to do so, nor did he know his own name when asked. How could the precepts be conferred upon him? As for the one who was "Not Ignorant":
he originally possessed no voice and had no form or appearance by which he could be perceived. How, then, could the precepts be conferred upon him? Both were [in this state].
If he does not transmit it, he fails the opportunity presented to him. But if he does transmit it, how does he transmit it? Have you not heard it said:
"The official court will not allow even a needle, yet in private one may pass carriages and horses"? [He suddenly picks up his staff and strikes it three times, saying:

"The five precepts, the ten precepts, the two hundred and fifty precepts, and the three clusters of precepts—all have been brought forth at once. As for the one who transmits and the one who receives, where are they right now?"
"Where? Coming straight down! [The Master] looked intently at the eyes of the assembly, threw down his staff, and descended from the seat.
At the request of the Venerable Weixiang of Cisheng Hermitage, he ascended the hall for the formal discourse:

"In the past, within the Three Vehicles, the World-Honored One separately opened the gate of the Pure Land, calling it 'cultivation via the shortcut' and also 'transcending the triple world horizontally. This refers to the practice of nianfo (reciting the Buddha's name)."
Rebirth [in the Pure Land] is exceedingly easy. Nowadays, many recite the Buddha’s name, yet few attain rebirth. What is the reason for this?
It is truly because they cannot look beyond the defects of the Sahā world and their faith in the Sukhāvatī is insufficient. The Sahā world is corrupt and evil, with all manner of oppressions;
what part of it is there that one cannot see through? The environment and inhabitants of the Sukhāvatī are of every kind of excellence, and the Buddhas of the ten directions—
The ancestral masters of successive generations have repeatedly exhorted us with bitter words to encourage rebirth in the Pure Land. What is there that you cannot believe?
If you truly cannot believe or see through this, you are blind and ignorant; such deluded sentient beings care only for what is before their eyes.
Do not fear what lies beyond this life; for at some future time or on some later day, that suffering will have no end.
Only the wise person thoroughly perceives every detail of the Sahā world and gains clear, complete faith in every aspect of the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
Thereafter, they relinquish all worldly attachments and, amidst the four modes of deportment, single-mindedly recite these three characters: "A-mi-tuo-fo."
Recite with mindfulness. Ensure that every character is distinct and every phrase flows seamlessly into the next. Recite until you reach the state where the mind is undistracted;

when the flower blooms and you behold the Buddha, you will know that recitation is itself the Buddha and the Buddha is itself recitation. Recitation is not recitation, and the Buddha is not the Buddha.
Make Amitābha himself one with yourself; merge the Land of Ultimate Bliss and this Sahā world into a single whole.
Then, by means of such a Dharma, deliver such a multitude of beings, aspiring for the nine grades of rebirth in the highest lotus and realizing the three great kalpas in a single lifetime.

To reverently repay the four debts of gratitude and to provide sustenance for all within the three realms of existence—only then are you a true child of the Buddha. O Great Assembly, time does not wait for man; each of you...
Exert yourselves! Take care!
Your virtuous friend Yuntai Shen. Regarding the request for a formal discourse on repaying one's parents: When one knows there is a body, one knows there are parents;
when one knows there are parents, one is able to contemplate and repay the kindness of one’s parents. What is this body? Who are these parents?
What constitutes repaying the kindness of one's parents? The World-Honored Buddhas of former times have said:

"The body receives birth from within the formless, just as various forms and appearances are produced by illusion. O Great Assembly, is this illusory production of form and appearance not the true body of each person themselves?
Is this formlessness not the true parents of each person? To recognize this true body—this is what it means.
One immediately recognizes one’s true parents. Having recognized one’s true parents, one is then able to repay the kindness of one’s parents.

Yun Taishen, my virtuous friend, lost both his parents in childhood; overcome by profound grief, he specifically requested that I, a mountain monk, ascend the seat to proclaim the Dharma of the Patriarchal School, thereby repaying their boundless debt.
At this very moment, the true bodies of one’s true parents appear before one all at once.
Furthermore, tell me: how, after all, is this kindness to be repaid? After a long silence, he said: "Having let go of the hand, one arrives home; people do not recognize it.
There is not even a single thing to offer to the Honored Hall."
The lay practitioner Yu Daoyou, in order to pray for peace and stability, solicited contributions from the assembly to perform the Great Compassion Repentance (*Mahākaruṇā-sādhana*).

When the three-year period was completed, a vegetarian feast was prepared and he invited the Master to ascend the hall. A monk asked, "Amidst the profusion of sounds and forms, how does one establish the teachings and principles of the One Vehicle?
The Master held up his whisk. The monk stepped forward and said, "This is sounds and forms; but what about that which is apart from sounds and forms? The Master again held up [the whisk].
[The Master] raised his whisk. The student stepped forward and said, "In that case, there is ultimately no duality of substance.
The Master said, "Feel free to discriminate as you wish. The student said, "When Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva comes, where will you, Master, meet him?
The Master said, "What is behind you? The student said, "This is mine; how about what you see, Master? The Master said:
"I am glad that you, *ācārya*, have arrived here. The monk stepped forward and said, "There is yet another offense that cannot be found;
how will the Master repent it for the sake of this student? The Master said, "It turns out you have never been here at all.
The monk said, "In that case, my skin and flesh have fallen away. The Master said, "That is indeed a fine report. The monk bowed and said, "May everyone bear witness."
The Master said: "The mess is no small matter. He then said: "Everyone is at peace. The land is fundamentally free from the three calamities and the eight difficulties.

It is only because people do not know this in their daily lives, but instead rush about seeking things externally, that they falsely imagine themselves to be oppressed by these calamities and difficulties within a state that is actually free of them.
Avalokiteśvara’s compassionate heart is so earnest that he protects everywhere; he has specifically brought this forth."
This unsurpassed secret dharma attained over vast eons is called the Dharani of the Vast, Perfect, and Unobstructed Great Compassionate Mind.
It enables all who have the karmic affinity to hear its name and recite it to emerge from all lands of difficulty and reach a state of peace and security.
Therefore, in this Sahā world, he is titled "The One Endowed with Great Compassion" and also called "The Bestower of Fearlessness.
The Master Yudaoyou of Chixin had planted roots of goodness in past lives, and his fruits of merit were fully realized; he embodied the compassion of Avalokiteśvara.

Compassionate toward the bitter suffering of all living beings, he initiated a campaign for donations and practiced according to the Dharma. When the three-year period was completed, blessings were bestowed upon the entire land;
indeed, the four seas became tranquil and still, the five grains ripened in abundance, the state flourished and households were at peace, the people were healthy, and all things prospered.
This one project of merit may truly be called beginning well and ending well; it is utterly perfect and beautiful.
At this very moment, is there anyone who has directly reached the land of peace and security? After a long silence, he said:
"It is always within that—walking, standing, sitting, and lying down. Take care.
The Venerable Rui Zhuo invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. "To awaken to the Way upon hearing a sound, to clarify the mind upon seeing a form"—Yunmen said:
"Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva buys a sesame cake with money; when he lets go of his hand, it turns out to be a steamed bun.
"Great assembly, are the sesame cake and the steamed bun one or two? If you say they are one, the sesame cake remains the sesame cake and the steamed bun remains the steamed bun. If..."

The Way is one; there are not two kinds of flour. The Master said, "Thirty blows of the staff; drive him out through the three gates! The monk stepped forward and said, "There is one person who laughs loudly, ha-ha."

[The Master] laughed. [The monk] asked, "I do not understand what you are laughing at. The Master said, "I do not know either. The monk further asked, "If one recognizes this person, the task of study is finished.
Who is this person? The Master remained silent for a long while. The monk said, "I do not speak in that way. The Master asked, "How then would you speak?
The monk replied, "The sound of the brook is itself the broad and long tongue; the mountain scenery is nothing other than the pure and serene."
The Master said, "What a fine man from outside the gate! The monk bowed. The Master then said, "The Venerable Wujin is seventy-five years of age;
his descendants are numerous, and he has had his every wish fulfilled by their service. Yet, one day he deeply realized the nature of worldly illusions and resolved to leave the household life.
Though his sons and grandsons tried to detain him, they could not prevail. He has thus been escorted here to Drum Mountain together with them to receive the tonsure and the precepts. It may be done.
It is like a lotus flower within fire; it is not easily found. One must know that those who have left the household life study the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*).
Within the unconditioned dharma, there is neither old nor young, neither slow nor fast. Thus, Rāhula left the household life at the age of seven and realized the fruit of Arhatship;
the Venerable Pārśva left the household life at eighty years of age and likewise realized the fruit of Arhatship. It is evident that this can be attained.
It lies in the person, not in the years. Great assembly, tell me: how does one study the unconditioned dharma? Do you understand?
At the two meal times, unfolding the alms bowl is a matter of daily routine; it is not permitted for others to easily know it.

At the commencement of the summer retreat, a fellow practitioner from Tánlín in Jiànzhou prepared a vegetarian feast to offer congratulations on the Master’s birthday and requested that he ascend the hall.

The Master took up his staff and said: "This very thing is, from the beginning, without form or segment; yet it manifests in hundreds of thousands of ugly appearances. I have intentionally brought it forth for you."
Who could possibly seize and carry away the head and tail of an ox? One may condense immeasurable kalpas into a single kṣaṇa, or extend a single kṣaṇa into immeasurable kalpas.
One may dwell at ease within the palaces of Māra or the dens of tigers; one may roam freely according to conditions in wine shops or brothels.
If this were not so, I would simply wish to be as pure as a wax figure or ice, sitting forever amidst the white clouds.
[The Master] leaned on his staff and descended from the seat.

The filial son Lin Taiding, on behalf of his late father, Layman Wenruo, has prepared this vegetarian feast for the first seven-day anniversary of his birthday and requests that the Master ascend the hall.
Layman Wenruo of Fucheng, father and son, have accumulated merit and maintained their family tradition; one day, he suddenly succumbed to illness...
The end was announced; those who saw or heard it could not help but give rise to sorrow and lamentation. Seven days before, the layman died; seven days after, the layman was born.
Since there is nothing that is born at the time of birth, how could there ever have been death at the time of death?

One who realizes the person who is neither born nor dies exhausts the boundless cycle of birth and death all at once. At the point where birth and death are exhausted, one turns over the body—what harm is there in this?
Constantly sporting wherever he may be, he pays homage to Amitābha and the assembly of sages. Upon the golden terrace, he hears the wondrous Dharma;

there, in that very place, his fruition is perfected and his bodhi is fulfilled. In worlds where no Buddha dwells, he acts as a Buddha—this is the filial son Ta Ding, through his ultimate filial piety.
"I request you to ascend the seat and preach this Dharma, so that all sentient beings throughout the entire dharma-realm may, at one and the same time, enter together into the ocean of dharmatā.
With a shout, he descended from the seat.

The filial son Lin Taiding requests the Master to ascend the hall. The filial son Lin Taiding, on behalf of his late father, Layman Wenruo, has requested monks to complete the recitation of the Avataṃsaka, Saddharmapuṇḍarīka, Śūraṅgama, and Yuanjue sutras.

Coinciding with this auspicious occasion when all Buddhas rejoice and the assembly of monks observes the Pravāraṇā ceremony, he has specifically submitted this confession and repentance, further requesting that I, the mountain monk, ascend the seat. No...
I shall not repeat this once more. The *Avataṃsaka* says: "Within every single atom of all the worlds in the Flower Treasury, one perceives the entire Dharma-realm.
If this is so, then the birth, death, coming, and going of all sentient beings throughout the entire earth are the Dharma-realm in its entirety;
what further room is there to speak of birth and death? The *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* says: "In the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, there is only the One Vehicle; there is no..."
Since there are neither two nor three, how can there be a "Dharma of the One Vehicle"? [It is like] filling a bowl with *bhera* rice to universally provide for the monks of the ten directions.
The *Śūraṅgama-sūtra* says: "The seer, the conditions of seeing, and the perceived objects are like flowers in the sky; fundamentally they do not exist."
This seeing and its objects are originally the wondrous, pure, and luminous essence of bodhi. When white clouds vanish into the ravines, the green peaks lean high against the void.

As the *Complete Enlightenment Sutra* says: "There is a great dharani-gate called Complete Enlightenment, from which flow forth all pure suchness, bodhi, nirvana, and the paramitas, instructing the bodhisattvas.
Even one who is capable of such great responsibility must still proceed from here.
The ground rises even higher. How can one contend with the heavens? Again, he says:
"Having thus extolled the merits of such a Great Dharma, I humbly pray that the lay practitioner Lin Wenruo may have the three obstructions thoroughly purified and the two adornments fully perfected;
that he may behold all Buddhas in a single thought-moment and open the Great Sūtra within a single mote of dust; and that together with all living beings, he may equally attain the Buddha-way."
The Layman Master Hong Gusu Jong, the Left Commander-in-Chief, has prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall.

It is said in the teachings: "It is difficult to obtain a human body; it is difficult to encounter the Buddha-dharma; it is difficult to give rise to faith. Furthermore, it is said: "For those of noble rank and wealth, it is difficult to study the Way.

This is because those of noble rank and wealth are often deluded by sounds and colors and do not weary of the root of suffering; therefore, studying the Way is difficult. Now tell me: what is it that one studies?
"The Great Way, the Great Way. Do you not see the monk who asked Venerable Zhaozhou, "What is the Way? Zhaozhou said, "It is right outside the gate. The monk said, "I am not asking about this Way.
Zhaozhou said, "Which Way are you asking about? The monk said, "The Great Way. Zhaozhou said: [It is right outside the gate.]

"The Great Way penetrates Chang'an. O assembly! If you can recognize where Zhaozhou’s tongue fell, then you will know that throughout the vast world, as people come from the south and go to the north, they tread at every step upon it; everywhere is Chang'an, and at all times they behold the Emperor.
To bring peace to the realm and assist the state, one brings about great tranquility while sitting still. If it were otherwise, try looking at daily life: by whose power does it proceed?
Supporting the heavens and propping up the earth is entirely due to him. (He strikes the whisk. He descends from the seat.
The disciples Chunji and Jiyun offered the memorial service for the late Master Jejong and requested that the Master ascend the hall.

The Master took up his staff, called out to the assembly, and said: "When living, it is this; yet this does not live. An iron ox sleeps on the ancient path. When dying, it is this; yet this does not die.
A stone horse gallops through the clear breeze. Neither living nor dying, it is this; yet this is able to live and able to die."
Death. Green mountains constantly take their steps; the white sun does not shift its wheel. *Zhuo*—a single strike—and he said:
"I hereby offer this for the sake of the newly deceased bhikṣu Jizong: may his three obstructions be eliminated and his two-fold adornment be perfected.

I pray that his true eye may open wide, reaching directly to the path of returning to the source; that the clouds of delusion may be blown away, transcending loftily to the heaven of supreme meaning. Thus, birth and extinction—

Thus one realizes the true and eternal, transforming worldly afflictions (*kleśa*) into perfect enlightenment (*samyak-saṃbodhi*). [The Master] struck the meditation staff once more and descended from his seat.

The Chief Administrator (Jianyuan) Lingshi Lixuan, together with the assembly of Dharma relatives, as well as the various patrons from the provincial capital—Chen, He, Guo, Wei, Lin, Zhou, Ao, Zhao, Chen, and Zeng—requested that he ascend the hall. Lingshi is indeed a blessed land of Fucheng. It is tranquil...

The ancestral halls of the patriarchs have their cycles of decline and revival; the time for their restoration has now arrived. Master Cao was the first to initiate this endeavor, and his disciples have followed in his footsteps.

With one mind, every brother among us has kept the restoration at heart. Consequently, we were able to move the various Dharma-protecting patrons and donors to offer their wholehearted support, specifically requesting that I, a humble monk, open the Dharma here.
As I look upon myself, I am acutely aware that my status is low and my virtue is meager.
I am unworthy to add weight to this mountain. I have declined with bitter words on several occasions, yet the resolve of the monastic community and the lay patrons has grown ever firmer;
thus, I cannot continue to evade my duty. Since there is no other recourse, I must venture to accept.
On the day the golden image and the precious hall are completed, I shall strike the stone drum once to revive the ancestral tradition, so that every person may...

Know that there is a great matter beneath one's own heels. You may see that when the Buddhas and Patriarchs appeared in the world, establishing the banner of the Dharma and founding their essential tenets, it was never in vain.
But as for today, how does this mountain monk receive and uphold a single phrase?
He picks up his staff, strikes the ground once, and says: "In all things, preserve this Way; in every flavor, trust in past conditions. Furthermore—
"Strike! Strike! He descended from his seat.
The Master arrived at Baoshan. Seat-holder Cangming led the assembly in requesting him to ascend the hall. "I have been at Baoshan for twenty days now," the mountain monk said.

"Monastics and laypeople from all quarters have come in great numbers, crowding shoulder to shoulder and foot to foot, vying with one another to make offerings. All day long, their mouths are wide open."
How vexing! Today, many senior monks from Cangming have come from afar from Yanping to respectfully present offerings at the Fragrant Accumulation Hall and formally spread the Dharma seat.
As the bells and drums are struck, they reverently request a discourse on the Dharma—thus adding yet another layer of disorder.
Nevertheless, what method do you call it? And how would you explain it? I shall instead ask Old Wooden Seat to deliver a message for all of you.
[He] takes up his staff and strikes it once, saying: "Supporting the earth and propping up the heavens, there is only this;
Spring comes and autumn passes, yet it never puts forth a branch. Held forth in the open sun, no one recognizes it; I recall, then, the moment the Dhūta broke into a smile."
He struck the meditation seat once, then descended from it.

When the Master arrived at Longshan, he ascended the hall. A monk asked, "Specifically for the sake of increasing the brilliance of the Dharma-gate, you have traveled a thousand li upstream to seek out fellow practitioners.
Now that you sit upon this high curved bench, may the great assembly truly listen as you provide a guiding instruction. The Master raised his whisk and said:
[The Master] asked, "Have you heard? The monk stepped forward and said, "I already know the path to follow; but what about returning home? The Master said, "Where are you, Upasaka, right now?
The monk then gave a shout. The Master said, "A fine shout! The monk said, "In that case, there are no two paths back to the source;
yet expedient means have many gates. The Master shouted and said, "What do you call 'expedient means'? The monk said, "It may be called a stone."
"The True Lamp has indeed continued its transmission; one stream from Cao’s source pervades all of China. The Master said, "For now, return to your place.
A monk asked, "The Buddha preached the Lotus Sutra for the sake of the Great Matter, and Prabhūtaratna Tathāgata vacated half his seat. Today you once again ascend the lion throne;
how is it that you reveal the Real by opening up the Provisional? The Master said, "I have already opened it wide with eight characters."
The attendant said, "At the peak of Litsak, the six kinds of movement stir; Longshan illuminates antiquity and shines anew today.

The Master said, "It is not improper to speak thus. The Master then continued, "In years past, this mountain monk had the honor of studying under the Dharma seat of the Venerable Longshan together with the Elder of Tiantong.
At that time, we made a pact to jointly revitalize the ancient style. It has now been nearly thirty years since then."

Longshan has for a long time manifested his ancestral style with great brilliance, and his transformation has spread throughout the world; yet this mountain monk has remained in a remote corner of the sea, limping and dragging along, feeling deeply ashamed that he does not measure up.
Today, having come specifically to the mountains to pay homage to the model of the Way and to converse about our past, my lifelong aspirations are fully comforted.
Furthermore, I have received the earnest invitation from the Chief Administrator and the two orders of officers to ascend the seat; since I was unable to decline, I have complied.
"One cannot avoid borrowing one's mother-in-law’s robe to bow for the New Year. Do you all understand? The Dharma-vehicle has declined, and true men are rarely encountered.
Lately, those who claim to be "knowledgeable" vie with one another to appear before the public; each claims to have realized the Unsurpassed Way.
Yet, if one examines them closely, they are all like those who discard gold to carry hemp. Only Longshan stands out, towering over the ravines and soaring above the clouds, majestic and solitary.
He rose up and did not fall into the ranks of the common; truly, he may be called rare. But tell me: what was Longshan’s special excellence?
Was it that he attained the secret instructions not transmitted by Taibai and revived the long-abandoned monastic community of Cuiyan?
Was it that throughout his life he maintained the resolve to uphold the Dharma and benefit others, establishing at every place the merit of non-action and non-striving? Or was it...?
"Is his wisdom like that of Śāriputra? Is his eloquence like that of Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra? It may resemble it, yet it is not yet it.
Ultimately, how is it? After a long silence, he said: "Heaven has produced a single piece of flawless jade; why must one carve patterns before its excellence is seen? He spoke again:
Just now, Master Longshan raised the koan concerning the late Master Shouchang, Great Good Mountain. Xingshan said, "Good.
Shouchang said, "Not good. Wherein, precisely, does "good" and "not good" lie? Does the assembly wish to know?
Midnight was perfectly bright; at dawn, nothing was revealed. Standing for a long time amidst the assembly’s compassion, I humbly pray that you will cherish yourself.
This is Prince Da-yong of Jingfan Gusian, who, on behalf of his late mother, Lady Lang, requests that you ascend the Dharma seat.
Today marks the first anniversary of the small memorial service for Lady Lang, the consort of Prince Gusian; he has specially entered the mountains to offer a meal.
The Sangha has prepared this memorial service and requests that I, this mountain monk, ascend the seat to proclaim the Dharma of the Patriarchal Lineage, thereby aiding the ground of awakening.

Now, this lady’s lifespan has exceeded seventy years; she has attained the first rank of nobility; her descendants are numerous and flourishing; and her fortune and blessings flow in an unending stream. In every respect, she is fully endowed with all worldly excellences.
Nevertheless, regarding the principle of birth and death as day and night, she must have a clear and penetrating realization within her heart, free from all doubt and hesitation. Now...
Today, on account of the celebration of the vegetarian feast, I cannot help but bring this up once more, so that everyone may know it. Do you know? From where does life come?
A blue lotus blooms in every direction within the fire. To where does death go? The long river flows day and night toward the east.
Since that which comes has nowhere from which to come, and that which goes ultimately has nowhere to which to go—coming and going, going and coming.
The totality of suchness is what is called the "Great Abiding in Illusion. Therefore it is said: "It is like a great illusionist who conjures up various men and women;
although their faculties are seen to move, they are all pulled by a single mechanism.

Within the ten dharma realms—the four noble ones and the six classes of ordinary beings—their diverse forms and strange appearances, their myriad distinctions and thousandfold differences, are all merely conjured men and women. If one can recognize them as such...

When a great master of illusion knows the locus of his artifice, he is not deluded by various illusory appearances. Although he manifests as a sage or an ordinary person, neither sages nor ordinary people can bind him;
he displays birth and death, yet birth and death cannot constrain him; he appears and disappears, coming and going.
Having attained great mastery, I venture to ask the great assembly: where, ultimately, does the mechanism of the illusionist reside?
[The Master] suddenly picks up his staff, strikes it three times, and says: "Temporarily donning soiled robes, he is called a Buddha; yet when he is adorned with precious regalia, who is he called?"
He struck the sounding block once more and descended from his seat.

On the day of the winter solstice, the scholar Huang Konggu of Wenling, together with the senior monk Xuanwen, hosted a vegetarian feast to celebrate the Master’s birthday and invited him to ascend the hall.
A monk asked: "The ancients said: 'The appearance of all Buddhas in the world, as well as their entry into nirvana, does not go beyond—'"
"At the limit of a single *kṣaṇa*. I do not yet know whether the Master’s lifespan remains within the limit of a single *kṣaṇa*, or if there is another path of vital function.
The Master struck the ground with his staff. The student stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then there is no difference in the soil within the same pit.
The Master said, "Only you, *śrāmaṇera*, are not included in that number. The student said, "I, your disciple, do not think so. The Master asked, "What do you think?"
The student said, "Nine in the middle, seven below; the number of all Buddhas does not exceed this. The Master said, "When have they ever exceeded it?
The student said, "Can you, Reverend, exceed it? The Master then struck him. The student said, "When have they ever exceeded it? The Master said, "I shall give you one more blow."
The monks prostrated. A monk asked, "I do not ask about the Master’s way of benefiting others before the age of fifty.
Now that you are exactly fifty, what is the one phrase for the Master’s way of benefiting others? The Master said, "That too deserves a blow of the staff.

The monk stepped forward and said, "The eye of Mahesvara protrudes from the crown of the head, illuminating the three thousand worlds and the great chiliocosm. The Master said, "I only fear it is not so. The Master [then] departed.
It is then said: "The appearance of all Buddhas in the world, as well as their entry into nirvana, does not transcend the samādhi of the limit of the instant (*kṣaṇānta*).

One must know that within this limit of the instant, the Buddhas of the three periods of time, the patriarchs of successive generations, and even all wriggling and breathing creatures are entirely contained.
Throughout the ages from antiquity to the present, not a single person has been able to emerge from it. If one were able to emerge—"
He roams freely across the world; dwelling within the rank of Buddhas, he cannot be caged.
Were it otherwise, there would be new rules for the coming year, and the spring wind’s vexations would never cease. (He strikes the meditation staff once. Again he says:
When the myriad yin energies are stripped away and the first yang returns, the True Person of No Rank comes forth in this manner. With a soiled face and disheveled hair, people do not recognize him.
A single branch of cold plum blossoms opens amidst the snow. Now tell me: does this person abide within the span of a single kṣaṇa, or does he not?
He plants his staff and says: "The heavenly wind strikes the stone drum; the great earth again hears thunder. Again, he plants his staff and says:
Take heed.
The lay official of Wenling, Zhang Huiliangyi, together with his wife, Lady Huang, have requested this formal discourse to fulfill their vows and seek blessings.
"Vast and empty, there is no sage; the reality is manifest before one's eyes. Truly, there is no merit, yet a hundred blessings are fully present. Stir the long river...
Ghee and curd. They transform the great earth into gold, with all manner of adornments, enjoyed without end. These do not come from any other place;
they all flow forth from within this very state itself. Now, what is the matter within this state? He lets out a shout. Then he says:
Good aspirations arise from one's own mind; merits are sought within one's own mind.
If only one ensures that one's own mind remains ever-awake, then merit and wisdom will never cease throughout all lifetimes.
The lay practitioner Su Cai-zhan offered a bath cauldron and provided a meal for the monks, requesting that the Master ascend the hall.

A monk asked, "In antiquity, there were sixteen noble youths who followed the custom of entering the bath and each attained enlightenment. I wonder, what did they realize? The Master said, "Today, Layman Su has invited you to bathe.
The monk stepped forward and said, "When shaking one's robes, there is nothing else; upon entering the water, one sees the Great Person."

The Master said, "By no means reveal your hands and feet. The monk stepped forward and asked, "If my hands and feet are not wet, what then? The Master said, "Then you are merely dragging mud and water along.
A monk asked, "When the single drop of water from the Lingyuan source bathes this stainless person, how is it? The Master said, "Today we are precisely opening the bath.
The monk stepped forward and asked, "Since one does not wash away dust nor wash the body, and remains at ease in between, what then?"
The Master said, "It does not hinder things to wash in this manner. The monk stepped forward and asked, "Even so, you have only bathed this one.

I wonder, does that other one receive the bath as well? The Master said, "What is 'this one' and what is 'that one'? The monk bowed. The Master then said: "A single fire’s work completes the twin iron cauldrons;
Filling them with fragrant water, they bathe the Saṃgha. The grime and oil of body and mind are washed away from head to toe."
Having washed away both body and mind, one beholds one’s father. Is there anyone such?

If there were, there would be no need for Subhūti’s awakening through causes, nor any use for Guling’s rubbing of the back; everyone’s sweat-soaked undershirts would have fallen off, and each person would be entirely at ease.
Not only do all defilements vanish together, but they are washed away all at once in their stainless purity.
Today, Layman Sujae-jam’s offering of one set of merit may truly be called no fruitless gift. Were it otherwise, the ocean of fragrant water would remain overflowing with purity;
let us therefore invite the entire assembly to bathe according to custom and the season.
Yun Taishen was a virtuous friend who, while ill, requested a rite of repentance and invited the assembly of monks for a formal lecture.

In the past, when Vimalakīrti manifested illness in the city of Vaiśālī, those who came to inquire after his health used his physical ailment as a pretext to expound the Dharma extensively, saying: "O worthy ones!"
"This body is impermanent and lacks strength; it is powerless and unsubstantial—a thing that quickly decays and cannot be relied upon.

When he spoke thus, his sole purpose was simply to have people recognize that this [body] is illusory. When Dongshan was ill, a monk asked him, "Master, while you are sick, is there anyone who does not fall ill?
Dongshan said, "There is. The monk asked, "Does the one who does not fall ill come to visit the Master?"
“Still no? Shan said, “The old monk sees that he has the potential. When he speaks thus, it is simply because he wishes for everyone to recognize what is truly real.
He took up his staff and called to the assembly, saying, “There is only this which belongs neither to the real nor to the false.”
Neither illness, nor non-illness. But tell me: what is this? It has no connection whatsoever with spring or autumn; how could it be encompassed by withering or flourishing?
It serves as the fundamental root for every generation; it is a lotus planted within the fire. *Zhuo!* (A single strike).
The Dharma protectors and fellow practitioners from Fusha—Zheng, Xie, Shao, and Pan—have requested that I ascend the hall to celebrate my master’s birthday.

Today, these various Dharma protectors, patrons, and fellow practitioners from Fusha have specifically brought silk scrolls and incense offerings into the mountains to celebrate this mountain monk’s birthday.
