Fusha is the land of our common roots; as people of those same roots, we cannot avoid [this occasion].
Let us speak of one's native roots. Within the formless body lies the body with form; moment by moment it does not abide, renewing itself anew.
The cyclical count of the *jiǎzǐ* era since Xuanyuan—though one were to exhaust the sands of the Ganges in counting them—is still not the truth. But tell me, what is the truth?
He held up the whisk and said, "The embroidered mandarin ducks are displayed for you to behold; the golden needle is not handed over to others.
He struck the whisk and descended from the seat.
Master Ziyun returned to a venerable elder on his seventieth birthday. At the request of the venerable Qi Ji, he ascended the hall. [He addressed them regarding] the four great elements...
The body takes years and months as its lifespan, yet the four great elements must inevitably decay; it possesses no substantial nature. Years and months pass swiftly, never lingering for long.
How much more so for human life, where those who reach seventy—the ancient standard for longevity—and even attain the age of one hundred, are but one in ten thousand.
Master Ben, from Ziyun Temple, cultivated his person through compassion and entered skillfully into the Buddha’s wisdom; he has reached the age of seventy. His grand-disciple Qi [writes this].
You have requested that this mountain monk bestow the gift of Dharma; you wish to make an offering of the Dharma. But what do you call "the Dharma"?
The World-Honored One, the Buddha of old, said: "The body receives birth from within the formless. If you recognize this formlessness, you will recognize your own true body. Master Sengzhao said:
"The rivers and streams rush forward in competition, yet they do not flow. If you recognize this non-flowing, then...
To recognize one’s own true life-span is for the true body not to perish; it pervades and encompasses the entire Dharma-realm. The true life-span does not shift;
it remains eternally present throughout the exhaustion of kalpa-stones. Although it is thus, this is still but a teaching to stop a child’s crying;
it cannot be said that such words exist upon the fundamental Dharma itself. What is the fundamental Dharma? After a long silence, he said: "In the end, you have made a mistake."
Commentary:

Master Kaimei prepared a vegetarian feast and requested [the Master] to ascend the hall. He said: "The world is vast and boundless, yet all are but day laborers; they do not know that within their robes there is a bright pearl.
For the sake of food and clothing, they hire themselves out in poor neighborhoods. To look closely at this is truly to see great folly. Today, he has opened [the seam].
He opens the seams of his robe and draws forth a bright pearl, showing it universally to all people. Holding up his whisk, he asks, "Do you see it?
Throughout ancient and modern times, the rain of jewels has always fallen, eternally delivering those in the dark alleys. He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.

On the day the Buddha attained enlightenment, at Qingcheng Temple, the precept-holders Xueguang, Xuexin, Huilin, Yulin, Xingsheng, Runyi, and Lingyuan prepared a vegetarian feast and invited the Master to ascend the hall.
A monk asked: "Before leaving Tuṣita Heaven, he had already descended into the royal palace;

before emerging from his mother’s womb, his work of saving beings was already complete. For what reason did he then go again to the Snow Mountains and awaken to the Way upon beholding the morning star? The Master said:
"It is simply because you do not realize it. The monk stepped forward and said, "Upon seeing the morning star, he opened his true eye.
What is the true eye? The Master said, "The pit of a longan fruit. The monk said, "If that is so, then the one on Snow Mountain in the past is the Master today.
The Master said, "After bowing, return to your place. Another monk asked, "Delusion has no self-nature; its entire substance is the Truth. For what reason did the World-Honored One [speak further]?"
"The Way. Sentient beings do not realize it because they cling to it with deluded thoughts. The Master said, "Wait until you have cast off deluded thoughts and clinging, and then I will tell you.
The student asked, "What is it like when one abandons the false and returns to the true? The Master said, "Do not have deluded thoughts.

The student said, "In that case, the clouds are gathered in and the mist has rolled away; the moon shines in every house. The trees have fallen and the vines are withered; autumn is everywhere. The Master said, "..."
Furthermore, this is a false imagination. The Master then said: "Before the Elder Śākyamuni beheld the morning star, all sentient beings had already attained Buddhahood.

After he beheld the morning star, he instead said that all sentient beings possess the wisdom, virtue, and marks of the Tathāgata, yet because of false imagination and attachment, they do not realize it.
From that time until now, for over three thousand years, [they have been]..."

They burden their descendants, rushing south and fleeing north; those who practice Chan practice Chan, those who receive precepts receive precepts, those who cultivate causes cultivate causes, and those who realize fruits realize fruits—thus, they have instead created another layer of separation. Suddenly, there is a man who, hearing such talk, flings it aside and goes forth.
Before the stars are seen and before the eyes have opened, he takes a single look and sees through it completely, straightaway causing [the Buddha] to...
Kālacitta has no place to open his mouth, no room to stretch out, nor can he act outside the bounds of reality.
If it were otherwise, he could not avoid standing behind one’s back to await his judgment. One must practice Zen as genuine practice;
one must receive the precepts as genuine reception. If the cause is not real, the fruit will surely be empty. Nevertheless, even so, it is right here before us this very day.
Great assembly, each of you don your robes and take up your implements;
with eyes wide open, ears alert, and minds clearly attentive, listen as this mountain monk, from his curved wooden seat, speaks of various matters.
As for this scene of splendor—tell me, does it occur before the sighting of the morning star, or after the sighting of the morning star? After a long silence, he said: "With this profound mind..."
To offer this to the lands as numerous as motes of dust is what is called repaying the Buddha’s kindness.
The two venerable masters Lingxu and Huilin have brought rice to the mountain and requested that I ascend the hall.
Today, the two venerable masters Lingxu and Huilin, while soliciting donations for vegetarian rice in Jianning County, have sent it to Gushan to provide for the assembly. It must be so.
There are three kinds of "unchangeability": first, the unchangeability of the transformer; second, the unchangeability of the giver; and third, the unchangeability of the recipient.
It is certainly established that the transformer and the giver are unchangeable; but how is it that the recipient is unchangeable? There are likewise three kinds.
I shall point this out for all people: first, cook it with a fire that is not hot; second, serve it in a bowl without a bottom;
third, contain it within the empty *tathāgatagarbha*. When these three conditions are fulfilled, one can plant the pure merit of *dāna* and increase the life-force of the Buddhas' wisdom.
Even if one were to spend ten thousand taels of gold daily, it would not be considered excessive. If it were otherwise, then at the two times of offering...
Venerable Sir, you must take great care not to consume even a single grain of rice belonging to another.
At Fusheng City, Huang Yanzan, the Magistrate of Xunshou, on behalf of his mother, Lady Zhang, requests that you ascend the hall to offer prayers for blessings in fulfillment of her vows.
The kindness of one’s parents is boundless; the power of the Buddha is infinite. If one can be filial toward one’s parents, one will be able to move the Buddha.
Indeed, the Buddha-mind, the mind of one’s own kin, and the mind of a child are all of one and the same substance.

Because they are of one substance, it is possible to dispel calamities in times of extreme peril and increase blessings and lifespan to the utmost degree. When the path of resonance and response intersects, its swiftness is like an echo.
This is precisely the time when one’s wishes are fulfilled according to the heart; thus, with this single phrase of praise for the merit of the *zhai* ceremony, how is it? Mother and child are one.
May your hearts take refuge in Perfect Enlightenment. In every birth, may your blessings and prosperity grow ever more exalted.
Be careful. [This concludes] the offering for the Daoist Yun Taishen. The Master ascends the hall: "Through the harmony of three conditions, there is illusory birth;

yet this [Essence] does not arise. Through the separation of the four elements, there is illusory extinction; yet this [Essence] does not perish. That which neither arises nor perishes is apart from arising and perishing. It is not...
That which undergoes arising and ceasing cannot be found; that which is free from both non-arising and non-ceasing likewise cannot be found. Therefore, the Avataṃsaka Sūtra says:
"All phenomena are without arising; all phenomena are without ceasing. If one can understand them in this way, the Buddhas will always manifest before one."
One must understand that the Buddha manifest before one is not an external Buddha with attributes; rather, it is the true, heavenly Buddha of one's own original source-nature.

By means of such a Buddha, [I] deliver Yun Taishen across the sea of birth and death and onto the shore of nirvana, constantly serving as a bridge and raft in every life, and acting as a fellow practitioner of the Dharma everywhere.

The Regional Inspector, Lord He, established a shrine for the late official and, seeking blessings and longevity, invited the monks to ascend the hall for a meal offering. The soil is rich and the fruits are bountiful;
the source is distant and the stream is long. From the Vermilion Cave the phoenix is born; from Mount Kunlun the jade emerges.

Thus, those of great merit and virtue give rise to a mind of great merit and virtue, cultivate practices of great merit and virtue, and thereby evoke offspring of great merit and virtue. For it is because the mind is great that the merit is great; this is due to the cause.
Truly real, truly real! Today, Provincial Grand Marshal He Gongwei hosted a vegetarian feast for his son, Imperial Prince Taiguan, to pray for increased merit, fortune, and longevity.
How do you express this in a single phrase? Where father and son’s innate nature perfectly harmonize, the myriad virtues of their nature flow on inexhaustibly like the sands of the Ganges.

The Elder Xuansheng requested the precepts, established a vegetarian feast, and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. Formerly, when the World-Honored One was approaching his parinirvāṇa, he exhorted his disciples:

"Abide by the four foundations of mindfulness; take the precepts as your teacher. In this age of the final dharma, those who have left the household life are as numerous as rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds.
If one does not know what the four foundations of mindfulness (*catvāri smṛtyupasthānāni*) are for, nor what the precepts (*śīla*) are, then the decline of the Buddha-dharma is surely due to this.

Today, the Venerable Xuansheng has entered the mountains to seek the precepts and requested that I ascend the seat; thus, I cannot help but bring forth these matters to bestow upon the great assembly.
What are the four foundations of mindfulness? They are the body, sensations, mind, and phenomena. One contemplates the impurity of the body, contemplates sensation as suffering, and contemplates...
The mind is impermanent; contemplate that phenomena are without self. By attaining these four foundations of mindfulness, one does not abide in saṃsāra.
Contemplate that the body is truly pure; contemplate that sensation is truly blissful; contemplate that the mind is truly eternal; contemplate that phenomena are truly self.

By attaining these four foundations of mindfulness, one does not abide in nirvāṇa. Since one neither abides in saṃsāra nor abides in nirvāṇa, this state of non-abiding is precisely the person themselves.

This is the place where one relinquishes body and life. Why? Because one takes the precepts as one's teacher. Since beginningless time, sentient beings have turned their backs on awakening and conformed to the dust of sensory objects;
in every thought-moment they grasp at conditions, and in every mind they create karma. If there were no dharma of the precepts to rein in the mind, it would surely have no boundaries.
One does not know where to find rest. What is called "restraining the mind" is named *śīla* (precept). From *śīla* arises *samādhi* (concentration); from *samādhi*, *prajñā* (wisdom) is produced.
This is truly the foundation for attaining Buddhahood. Therefore, the Sūtra says:

"O Bhikṣus, after my parinirvāṇa, you should honor, treasure, and revere the *Prātimokṣa* as if encountering light in the darkness, or as a poor man finding a treasure. You should know that this is your [true wealth]."
He is equal to the Great Master. Were the Buddha still dwelling in the world, there would be no difference between him and this person.

Any who have left the household life and can follow the Buddha’s final injunctions by abiding in the four foundations of mindfulness, and who further take the precepts as their teacher—even if they cannot realize the Way or attain the fruits in this present life—they will naturally, from lifetime to lifetime, not fall into the evil realms.
Life after life, they shall not lose their human form. When they emerge once more, [they will attain realization]. One.
To hear this and attain awakening—this is certainly not in vain. Nevertheless, one must further realize that the essence of the mind is free from thought;

where could the foundations of mindfulness (smṛtyupasthāna) be applied? Since its own nature is without fault, from where could precepts be established? Thus, although one may observe the precepts all day long, there is no mark of precept to be observed;
although one may practice the foundations of mindfulness all day long, there is no mark of mindfulness to be established. One remains serene and solitary amidst the myriad transformations.
The realm [of phenomena] functions and operates within a single void. One who can employ the mind in this manner may truly be called a disciple of the Buddha;
such a one truly repays the Buddha’s kindness. I humbly beseech the great assembly to exert yourselves deeply. Take care.
Master Huisu was invited to ascend the hall. Formerly, a monk asked Mazu, "Why do you say 'this very mind is Buddha'?
Mazu replied, "To stop a young child from crying. The monk asked, "After the crying has stopped, what then? Mazu said, "Neither mind nor Buddha.
The monk asked, "When people who are neither of these two types come, how will you instruct them? Mazu said, "I tell them: 'Not... (The Master then descended from the seat).
"This is the matter," he said. [A monk asked: "If someone suddenly encounters one of those people, what then? The Patriarch said, "Just let him realize the Great Way.
"Great assembly, the words of the ancient worthies were never uttered in vain. This is a gradual process within the absence of gradation.
Today, such a rare opportunity is difficult to encounter; therefore, I shall compose a verse for each of you: 'This very mind is Buddha'—this was merely to stop a child's crying."

A single coarse meal forgets a hundred hungers; neither mind nor Buddha, the child’s crying has ceased. Snatch away the spoon and chopsticks, and only then will abstaining from grain be truly delicious.
It is only these two who, facing the Way, are not bound by things; they transcend appearances and names, even to the point of gouging out their hearts and cutting open their bellies.
Among them, people come; the Great Way is taught. Fish swim in the bottom of the stream; magpies chirp among the trees. He calls to the great assembly, saying:
"Your faces and eyes are distinct; each of you must realize this for yourselves."
The disciples Chen Dengrong and Zheng Chuanyuan of the same residence have prepared this merit in advance and requested me to ascend the hall.
Those who seek blessings are many; those who seek the Way are few. Though one may strive to discuss the Way, it ends up remaining unresolved.
Even so, whether it is resolved or unresolved, it is this very thing. But tell me, what is this? Raising his whisk, he said: "This is non-existence."
The treasury of merit and virtue is exhausted; today, for you and your kin, I shall break it open for you. (He strikes the whisk. He descends from his seat.
The two venerable monks, Chuanbi and Chuanchan, requested the precepts and invited him to ascend the hall. Hanshan said: "Absence of anger is itself the precept."
When the mind is pure, one is a renunciant; my nature merges with yours. All phenomena are without distinction. At Mount Gu, the Way says that emptiness is itself the precept;
only when the body is empty does one truly become a renunciant. Originally there is not a single thing—where could there be a thousand differences?
O assembly, tell me: how far apart is this from the ancients? Try to discern it for yourselves!
Master Xiangguang was requested to ascend the hall for a vegetarian feast. A monk asked, "If self-nature is fundamentally empty, from where do the precepts arise?
Is it that what is right now is the precept, or is it not the precept? The Master said, "To look for bird tracks in the sky; to count fish prints at the bottom of the water.
The monk made the gesture of holding an alms bowl and said, "Is this the precept or not the precept? The Master said, "Realize it before you have even opened your mouth."
[The monk] takes [the staff]. He advances and says, “The fundamental original self-nature is the True Heaven-Born Buddha;

it is neither form nor emptiness, neither past nor present. The Master says, “No need for explanatory notes. The monk bows. The Master then says, “In the Hall of the Empty King, all traces of movement are utterly severed;

before the Hall of the Bright Moon, the spring colors are silently transmitted. Within non-precepts one establishes precepts; within non-concentration one cultivates concentration; within non-wisdom one gives rise to wisdom.”

Wisdom. Once the three trainings are complete, all myriad virtues are perfected. Thus it is said: "One performs the Buddha-work of blooming flowers in the sky; one subdues the demonic armies within the mirror;
one establishes the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa) as the moon reflected in water; and one realizes the fruit of Buddhahood within a dream. Although this is so, [one must not remain complacent].
It is simply like the flower perishing and the mirror breaking; when the moon falls and the dream awakens, what then? Outside the curtain of night-brightness, they stand in formation;
ten thousand miles of song and praise celebrate Great Peace.
At the request of the Abbot of Yanzhou, the Master ascended the hall. Holding up his staff, he said: "This very thing is free from characteristics and free from names;
it is neither emptiness nor form. It cannot be praised, nor can it be reviled; it is neither 'is' nor 'is not. To call it a Buddha-land is to add mud to the top of it;
to call it precepts is to bind oneself with no ropes; to call it mind is to carry a lamp while searching for fire. When one arrives here—" [The text breaks off.]
The Buddhas of the world stare with wide eyes and open mouths; the ancestral masters of successive generations cannot even catch its scent.
At such a moment, how can one transmit the message? Where the source of life is profound, no one arrives; there is only the sound of a few calls from a solitary bird.

On the Buddha’s birthday, the official Li Taisheng, together with his wife Zhou Taigui, hung banners and provided meals for the monks to pray for blessings, requesting that the Master ascend the hall.
Śākyamuni, the Old Man, has already come to this world eight thousand times;
yet, helpless before the failure of sentient beings to understand, he now returns once more, entering the womb of Māyā and emerging from the womb of Māyā, pointing to heaven and pointing to earth.
Looking in the four directions and claiming supremacy—this very first stroke has already brought forth the inexhaustible treasury all at once.
Yet, it remains unknown who among the assembly is the one to receive it. Later, there was Master Yunmen, who said:
"If I had seen him at that time, I would have struck him dead with a single blow and fed him to the dogs, for the sake of peace throughout the world.
Langye commented: "Yunmen may truly be said to 'offer this profound mind to every dust-mote and land'; this is what is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.
Today, on the auspicious occasion of the World-Honored One’s birthday, the official Li Taisheng, together with his wife...
The Zhou Emperor was exceedingly generous. He entered the mountains specifically to hang precious banners on high and to extensively arrange sublime offerings.

There, saints and ordinary beings gathered together, and merit and wisdom were cultivated in perfection. Now tell me: is this the same as Yunmen’s Bao’en Temple, or is it different? "The wild landscape has no further breaks between the mountains;
the heavenly light flows directly through the waters. A monk asked: "The Dharma-body is formless; the Reward and Transformation bodies are not the Truth. What do you call it?"
[The student] said, "What about Śākyamuni? The Master said, "You have added this one question. [The student] stepped forward and said, "If that is so, then not even an inch of silk hangs upon you.
The Master said, "Be careful not to fall into a pit or a ditch. [The student] stepped forward and said, "How joyful!
How joyful! Today I have run into this faceless fellow. The Master said, "I cannot save you. [The student] stepped forward and said, "Transgression! Transgression! The Master—
[The Master] said, "Take this with you yourself.
Disciple Wu Taixi of Ninghua County provided a meal for the monks and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. A monk asked, "For one who has not yet attained it, how does one apply oneself?
The Master said, "What have you lost? The monk stepped forward and asked, "For one who has already attained it, how does one maintain it? The Master—
The Master said, "And what have you attained? The monk replied, "Whether hidden or manifest, the subtle nuances leave nothing behind; though manifold, the great function lacks no integrity.
The Master said, "Try to demonstrate it for me. As the monk hesitated, the Master gave a shout. When the monk attempted to speak further, the Master said, "You are eight *ke* late.
The Master then said, "Having traversed every stream and rapids to reach this place, he feeds the monks to seek merit and transform beings in the human and celestial realms."
The roots of goodness increase constantly from lifetime to lifetime; do not obscure the conditions for *prajñā* in this life.
What are the conditions for *prajñā*? The Old Man Śākyamuni said: "All that has marks is entirely false and illusory.
If you see all marks as non-marks, then you see the Tathāgata. Holding up his whisk, he said: "This is a mark. What do you call 'non-mark'? This is..."
It is not a mark. What do you call a mark? Does the assembly see the Tathāgata?

If you can see him, then you will know that greed and anger are fundamentally empty, while merit and wisdom are fundamentally present—not obtained from elsewhere, but entirely and spontaneously complete within the natural state.
If you have not yet seen it, do not let this be forgotten throughout ten thousand kalpas and a thousand lifetimes. (He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.
On the occasion of the first anniversary of the passing of his father, Layman Wenruo, the filial son Lin Taoding requests the Master to ascend the hall. As for the principle of pure emptiness:
Ultimately there is no body; the entire world is vast and empty, with not a single person. This is the principle (*li*). But as for the phenomenon (*shi*), how is it?
The black ox and the white cow emit radiance. As for the principle, so for the phenomenon. On the road of birth and death, there is no road of birth.
Without involving either phenomenon or principle, the hundred-foot deep cold pond is clear to its very bottom. Taking these four turning phrases, I respectfully offer them for my filial son, Lin Tai.
Dingzi respectfully recommends the late father Wenruo Jushi. On the occasion of the first anniversary of his passing, we pray that his merit and wisdom may further increase. We humbly beseech you:

may he fully open the eye of right vision and suddenly shatter the barrier of delusion; may he attain the mind that is neither born nor extinguished and realize the principle that there is neither going nor coming.
Having once attained the true and eternal, may he never again regress.

Dharma friends Chi, Zhang, Chen, Lin, along with their disciples Ziyun, Xiang, Xinglin, Bitan, Shanhui, and Dequan, escort the reliquary shrine of Venerable Xuexi for cremation and request that the Master ascend the hall.
Venerable Xuexi resided in the Iron Buddha Hall of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou for many years;
he relied on his medical skills as the means for his almsgiving and took the field of merit as his pure land.
The Master was sixty years of age this year. Having been bedridden with illness for over ten days, he clearly instructed his disciples on all matters concerning his final affairs.

He then ordered a bath, changed his robes, and having struck the bell, passed away while reciting the Buddha’s name. This may be called "the head upright and the tail upright," for it was due to the reality of his original truth.
Today, my fellow practitioners and disciples have specifically fulfilled my final instructions by escorting the reliquary casket to the mountain for cremation and interment in the stupa.

They have further requested that I, the mountain monk, ascend the seat to proclaim the Dharma of our school, thereby supporting their awakening. Do you understand? This very thing is present even at birth.

This very thing is unborn; even in death, it is this very thing. This very thing does not die. If you recognize that which is neither born nor dies, you will recognize that which is constantly born and constantly dies.
If you recognize that which is constantly born and constantly dies, you will recognize that which is neither born nor dies.
Therefore, the Elder Śākyamuni said: "All phenomena are eternally quiescent; they possess no characteristic of arising or ceasing. This is precisely now.
All phenomena arise and perish. How can one speak of this principle of non-arising and non-perishing so fervently?
Is it that they "arise right where they are" and "perish wherever they are"? Is it that "arising is itself non-arising" and "perishing is itself non-perishing"?
"Is it not birth and death, coming and going? Is it not the fundamental Tathāgatagarbha, the wondrous nature of True Suchness? [The Master] said, "Has it not yet arrived?
Has it not yet arrived? Ultimately, how is it? After a long silence, he said: "Without leaving this very place, it is eternally serene;
seek it and you will know it cannot be seen. He struck the whisk and descended from his seat.
The virtuous woman Wenqin has now respectfully invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. The entirety of the worlds of the ten directions is one's own native land;

all sentient beings throughout the great earth are kin of the same substance. Saints and ordinary people are no different; birth and death are without interval; past and present do not shift. Why is this?
Because past and present are one time, birth and death are one body, and ordinary people and saints are one mind. Therefore, it is simply thus right now.

On this auspicious day, the virtuous woman Wen Jinyan ascended Mount Gu specifically to provide meals for the Sangha and request the Dharma, in order to dedicate merit for the deliverance of her parents, husband, and kinsmen—whether they be within or beyond the realm of existence.
For those present here, may this single thought-moment transcend birth and death; holding hands together, we return to the Gate of Non-duality.
Hell and celestial palaces are all pure lands; as the moon pierces the bottom of the pool, the water leaves no trace.
When the dharma friend Lindanzhang performed the ritual for burying the remains, he requested the Master to ascend the hall for a discourse on the *Sūtra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas*.
A monk asked, "Who is it that does not take the myriad dharmas as a companion? The Master said, "If you can understand this before your parents were born.
The monk pressed further, "What was one's face before one's parents were born? The Master said, "What is your face right now? The monk bowed. The Master [continued]:
He said, "You must not mistake this. The Master then said, "The entire dharma-realm of the ten directions is but a single skull.
Where would you receive it and bury it? If you can clearly accomplish its burial, all sentient beings will be fully delivered;
the Buddhas of the three periods of time shall serve as witnesses. If it is otherwise, the thousand Buddhas of the past have already passed away, and the [thousand Buddhas of the] future..."
"The thousand Buddhas of the past have not yet arrived; as for the thousand Buddhas of the present, you are about to pass them by face-to-face. Is there anyone who does not miss them?

Long ago, there was a scholar who recited the *Sūtra of the Names of All Buddhas*. He asked Master Changsha, "I see the names of hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, but I do not know in what lands they dwell.
Do they still transform sentient beings or not? Changsha said, "The Yellow Crane Tower. (Cui) 黃鶴樓崔.
Hao wrote after the inscription: "Have you seniors ever written such a thing before? Cai replied, "I have not yet written one. Sha said, "When you find leisure, it would be well to write one.

"Monks, when the scholar asked in this manner and Changsha answered in this manner, it was very much like the youth Sudhana ascending the peak of Mount Meghadri to visit the Bhikṣu Deven. For seven days he searched for him but could not find him; afterwards, however—"
We meet on a distant peak. Do you wish to know the matter of this meeting? Listen to this verse: Cui Hao inscribed his poem upon the Yellow Crane;
From ancient times to the present, the clamor is tumultuous. (He strikes the whisk. The three thousand Buddhas appear all at once;
This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing. (He lets out a shout and descends from his seat.)
The filial son Wang Daoxing, in requital of his parents, requests that they ascend the hall. Their father’s essence became the bones; their mother’s blood became the flesh.

From the union of bone and flesh, what is called a body was formed. Thus, for ten months she carried him in her womb, and for three years she nursed him with milk. He pushed aside the dry to seek out the damp.

They raised you with great hardship and toil. To repay the profound kindness of your parents, you must be like Prince Nāha, who divided his bones to return to his father and his flesh to return to his mother;
only then could he manifest his true body to preach the Dharma for his parents.
But once the bones and flesh have been divided and returned to the parents, what remains of one's own true body? Seek it before your parents were born.

Although sentient beings, from time immemorial, have emerged from one leather bag and entered another, passing through birth after birth and death after death in an unending cycle of saṃsāra—tell me, which person is within birth and death, and which is outside of birth and death? *Pah!* What do you call "birth and death"?
Take this very Dharma and respectfully offer it as a memorial service for the late father, Wang Daoxing, on behalf of his filial son, Wang Daoxing.

First, for the beloved mother, Lady Chen: having early escaped the wheel of suffering and transcended birth into the land of bliss, we humbly pray that she may exhaust the ocean of birth and death, ascend the mountain of nirvana, be reborn together within the assemblies of all Buddhas, and forever serve as a kinsman to the Dharma-gate.
The Great Compassion Repentance was commenced. Disciples Yang Taiming and Chi Taichang requested that the Master ascend the hall.

"The hands and eyes of Avalokiteśvara are his entire body; his vow-power to rescue and protect all living beings is profound. A single scroll of the *Dhāraṇī* possesses unimpeded power; with every sound, the heart of great compassion flows forth.
Therefore, when facing the mountain of blades, the mountain of blades breaks of its own accord; when facing the cauldrons of fire, the cauldrons of fire [extinguish themselves]."
If one turns toward hell, hell itself will be extinguished; if one turns toward the hungry ghosts, the hungry ghosts will be spontaneously satiated;
if one turns toward the asuras, their evil minds will be subdued; if one turns toward the animals, they will naturally attain wisdom.

Although sentient beings daily give rise to the afflictions of the four realms of rebirth, create the evil karma of the four realms, and undergo the bitter fruits of the four realms, if they can but for a single thought-moment call upon the Name with a sincere mind—
When one holds the mantra, Avalokiteśvara immediately manifests before one; liberation occurs right where one stands.
How much more so when the sounds of the wind and the songs of birds all proclaim the tones of *dhāraṇī*, and the mountain colors and river glimmers fully reveal the wondrous forms of compassion.

Just as today, at the summit of Mount Lishizi, kings and nobles gather together, and clergy and laity share a single heart, practicing the Great Compassion Repentance for the sake of the entire world.
May there be peace and prosperity. May you give rise to the bodhicitta and plant the seeds of Buddhahood. At such a time as this, tell me: where is Avalokiteśvara?
Holding up his staff and striking it once, he said: "If one listens with the ears, one will never understand."
"It is only through hearing sounds that the sense-sphere of the eye is known. He struck the floor once more and descended from his seat.
The officials who sponsored this were: Mr. Zeng [Hui] Fakong, Mr. Wang [Hui] Meili, Mr. Li [Hui] Shiyuan, Mr. Li [Hui] Ying, Mr. Zhang [Hui] Bosheng, Mr.
Xiong [Hui] Jinxue, Mr. Song [Hui] Ren, Mr. Zhang [Hui] Guowei, and Mr. Xia [Hui] Youde Xia [Hui] Jiwang. They made this repair.
The Ritual for the Great Compassion Repentance: A Lecture Requested for the Offering of a Feast. The World-Honored One said: "It is difficult for the noble and wealthy to study the Way.
This is because those who are noble and wealthy are often deluded by sounds and forms; they do not recognize the root of suffering and do not seek the essential means of liberation.
Therefore, studying the Way is difficult for them. Today, the great lay patrons and officials present here, though they occupy positions of rank and salary, keep their minds [fixed on the Way].
In the Buddha-dharma, one knows that there exists a great causal condition for transcending the world;
this is because, in the past, one has deeply planted roots of goodness within the true and pure field of the Triple Gem, and thus remains undeluded.

One must know that Śākyamuni’s appearance in the world was not for any other purpose, but solely so that every person may themselves realize the existence of the vast, perfect, and unimpeded heart of great compassion. Above...
Identical to all Buddhas, yet below, it accords with the multitudes of sentient beings. It revolves and directs the transformations of creation, giving birth to and nourishing the myriad things.

There is not a single merit that is not fully possessed within it. Throughout immeasurable kalpas, it has never moved so much as a single hair’s breadth; it has never shifted or altered by even a single hair’s breadth.
Since it has neither moved nor shifted, why is there the distinction between the holy and the ordinary, or the defiled and the pure? And so forth...
Are there not various distinctions such as noble and base, rich and poor, suffering and joy, sorrow and delight? These are merely like flowers seen in the sky by one whose eyes are clouded.

Therefore, the practitioner of the Way prizes the uprooting of the cataract; thus the Dharma-eye becomes clear and bright, allowing one to personally behold the field of one's own home and bring forth the treasures of one's own house.
In this way, one benefits both self and others, enjoying them inexhaustibly. It is just like uprooting [the cataract].
A single phrase that dispels the cataracts of the senses: How can one say it? "Not seeing a single dharma is the Tathāgata; this is also called Avalokiteśvara.
He serves as a bridge and ferry across perilous and evil paths, unimpeded throughout the mundane and supramundane realms. Descend from the seat.
The laywomen Xu and Chen of the Cheng school, acting on behalf of the man Mingshou, hung banners and provided meals for monks to seek repentance and requested that he ascend the hall.
"All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas," [the Master said], "regard all sentient beings in the great earth as if they were an only child, sustaining and protecting them with utmost thoroughness.
While everything in the world may be feigned, the single thought of loving one's child is never feigned; this is because it is identical to the Buddha-nature."
The Bodhisattva’s unconditional compassion is of one essence and non-dual, both flowing forth from the true mind.
This is what is meant by "Amitābha in every house" and "Avalokiteśvara everywhere.

Today, the female lay devotees Xu and Chen of the Cheng family have raised a magnificent, colorful banner for the sake of Mingshou, their son, and have extensively arranged offerings of incense to pray that his foundations may be firm and his life and status may flourish.
In youth, one will not be afflicted by calamities; as one grows older, the stars of officialdom will shine brightly. Whatever is sought shall be fulfilled, and all wishes shall accord with the mind.
At such a time, how do you express the single phrase of the mutual resonance between the path and its response? When the ordinary mind is first raised, Avalokiteśvara appears.
His accumulation of merit is like an immeasurable ocean; therefore, one should prostrate in worship. (He strikes the whisk and descends from the seat.)
The laywoman Xue Taichi has prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. A human body is difficult to obtain; the Buddha-dharma is difficult to encounter.

Having obtained a human body and encountered the Buddha-dharma, one must give rise to a sincere heart and practice according to the Buddha-dharma before success can be attained. Now tell me: how is this so?
How should one practice the Buddha-dharma? Amidst the myriad waves of the suffering sea of this Sahā world, a single phrase of Amitābha provides a direct crossing.
Once the high shore is reached, one arrives at one’s own native land and personally beholds the Great Compassionate Father, Amitābha. After seeing him, what then? After a long silence, he said:
"The family estate is fundamentally complete; there is no need for further entrustment."
On the anniversary of Avalokiteśvara’s attainment of the Way, the virtuous woman Taici Xingle prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall.
Each person is a Mount Potalaka; its peaks soar toward the clouds. The Great Being sits majestically within this place, his marks and signs naturally distinct.
He expounds the Dharani of Perfect Great Compassion; ten thousand apertures roar with the winds of heaven. May all beings universally receive this grace and enter the profound gate.
The great earth has no gaps; all people enter realization here. Then one knows that Avalokiteśvara is oneself, and oneself is Avalokiteśvara.
This single scroll of the Great Compassion Mantra is proclaimed in every dust mote and in every world-system, without interruption from antiquity to the present.
By seeking the Way through this, one directly attains Bodhi; by seeking merit through this, the myriad virtues are perfectly complete. Should one...
Not so. Today, Avalokiteśvara has finally attained the Way; all sentient beings, down to the most minute insects, radiate light.
I invite everyone to diligently pay homage, for in every atom the King of Dharma is fully revealed. (He strikes the whisk and descends from his seat.)
The Great Compassion Repentance was completed. Disciples Chi Taichang and Yang Taoming requested the Master to ascend the hall.

A monk asked, "The Dharma-body is unconditioned and does not fall into any categories; why then does the Bodhisattva of Great Compassion manifest a thousand hands and eyes? The Master said, "How has there ever been a single one?
The monk pressed further, "If that is so, then the golden halls, layer upon layer, reveal the Supreme Honored One. The Master said, "It is not this."
"This is the principle. The monk stepped forward and said, "But how can it be that everyone possesses it inherently? The Master asked, "What are your thousand hands and eyes?
The monk made a gesture with his hand as if holding up the sun and moon. The Master said, "You still lack one. The monk then gave a shout. The Master said:
"I am pleased to give you this staff. The Master then said: "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction.

Avalokiteśvara, through his unconditioned compassion, emits light and recites mantras from within the hearts of sentient beings. Sentient beings, through the power of their great vows, prostrate and make offerings within the heart of the Bodhisattva.
It is like space merging with space, or water poured into water. Vast as the Dharma-realm, it is ultimately..."
In the end, it is like empty space; reaching to the limits of the future, it is without interruption.

Just as today’s single session of Buddhist services has come to an end, how do you express a phrase for celebrating and praising this meal? The bow and spear have been hung up, the smoke of war has ceased;
ten thousand miles of songs celebrate the Great Peace. Again, Mazu asked Linji: "Of the Great Compassionate One’s thousand hands and eyes, which one is..."
Zhengyan (Correct Eye). Jie grabbed him and held him fast, saying, "The Great Compassionate One has a thousand hands and eyes.
What is the Correct Eye? Speak quickly! Speak quickly! Gu pulled Jie down from the meditation seat and sat back down himself. Jie greeted him, saying, "How do you do? Gu hesitated;
Jie then pulled Gu down from the meditation seat and sat back down himself. Gu then went out. The Master said, "These two venerable elders each used their hands and eyes to display their skill."
As for supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), they involve coming and going like threads; one employs only nine hundred and ninety-nine eyes.
As for the True Eye, one has never even dreamed of it. But tell me, after all, what is the True Eye? He stood up and remained so for a long while, then said: "Do you not see?"
He then descended from his seat.
The virtuous woman Wang Taijing had prepared a vegetarian feast and invited him to ascend the hall. Xinghua said, "I heard him shout in the front corridor and I heard him shout in the rear quarters.
His shouting brought this old monk up to the Thirty-three Heavens, only to crash back down with not a breath of life remaining."
There is no dependence. I have slowly awakened and say to you: "It is not yet. Why?

It is because I have never scattered real pearls from within the purple silk curtain for the sake of others. When the old man Xinghua spoke thus, he was already crying out in grievance while clutching his own stolen goods.
Today, I, this mountain monk, am here; two Chan practitioners have come forth.
Come forward. When you present one question or two, you immediately shout wildly and indiscriminately.
I, this mountain monk, see none of it and hear none of it. Why is that? Daytime birds sing in spring; nocturnal insects chirp in autumn. What room is there for comparison?
Even so, when I, this mountain monk, speak thus, tell me: is this a pearl or a piece of rubble? Leave it to everyone to examine for yourselves.

[The Master] departs. He speaks again: "This virtuous woman, Lady Wang, has long been exceedingly pure. She grew weary of the violence and evil of this Sahā world and yearned for the sublime excellence of Sukhāvatī.
She has diligently cultivated the practices of purity and resolved her will upon rebirth there for many years.

Today she has specially prepared a vegetarian feast and invited this mountain monk to ascend the seat to point out the path to the Western Land. I dare ask the assembly: what is the path to the West?"
"In what place?"—do not say "go straight ahead. Do not say "look underfoot. Do not say "ask about Chang'an while inside the Han-yuan Palace.
People nowadays exert their full strength, yet none transcend these [three]. Can they still settle their doubts?
The *Inner Classic* says: "If it is slow, treat the root; if it is urgent, treat the symptom. One must know that this applies to the Sahā world.
This world of the six realms of rebirth is nothing but the character for "attachment. The Land of Ultimate Bliss, where those of supreme goodness assemble, is nothing but the character for "purity.
Therefore, the ancient masters said: "If attachment is not heavy, one will not be born in Saha; if mindfulness is not pure, one will not be born in Ultimate Bliss.
Do you, the great assembly, wish to recognize the path to the West? It relies solely upon this single phrase: "Amitābha Buddha. Purity.
"Instead, it gives rise to much craving and attachment. When craving and attachment are purified, Ultimate Bliss manifests. What happens after this manifestation? After a long silence, he said:
"The Sahā world sinks away right where it stands. Take care."
When the King of Lotus Realization was about to ascend the hall after having previously cultivated merit, a monk asked:
"Yesterday, the Master spoke of two Chan guests who shouted wildly and indiscriminately. May I ask, what is the 'correct shout'? The Master said, "I will not shout at you.

The monk stepped forward and said, "A master of the school naturally possesses such presence. The Master struck him. The monk stepped forward again and said, "If that is so, then I shall overturn this meditation seat!"

[The monk] left the platform. The Master said, "These fabricated Chan monks are as numerous as hemp and millet," and struck him again. The Master then said, "This practitioner is from the Wang family;
his Dharma name is Chuanxi, and his religious title is Lianshi. Born into a noble lineage, he was destined for a prestigious clan."
Before the marriage rites were completed, her teacher passed away. At that time, Daozhe was still in her maidenhood;
she thus vowed to remain steadfast and chaste, purifying herself through moral cultivation. She honored the Buddha and observed the fasts, diligently practicing the pure karma.

Upon reaching the age of twenty-six, she finally returned to her family home, where she raised her successor while maintaining her vows of chastity. This year she has reached sixty-one. Such is her pure integrity.
Although you already possess the status of devas, the path is a matter of aspiration; it does not reside in the realms of humans or devas, but rather in the vow to be born in the Pure Land.

Therefore, today we perform prostrations, repentance, and provide meals for the Sangha. Every one of these various merits is dedicated toward the Pure Land. Furthermore, I have requested the mountain monk to ascend the seat.
I have elucidated the essential principles of the Pure Land as a public warrant for the Western Paradise. Do you understand? Good and evil karma are both created by the mind;
defiled lands and pure lands both arise from the mind. Therefore, the World-Honored One said: "The straightforward mind is the bodhisattva’s pure land.
When the bodhisattva attains Buddhahood, sentient beings who are not sycophantic will come to be born in that land. The profound mind is the bodhisattva’s...
The Pure Land: When a Bodhisattva attains Buddhahood, sentient beings endowed with merit come to be born in that land. The Mahāyāna mind is the Bodhisattva’s pure land;
when the Bodhisattva attains Buddhahood, Mahāyāna sentient beings come to be born in that land.

Furthermore, giving, ethical discipline, patience, diligence, meditative concentration, and wisdom are the Bodhisattva’s pure lands; when the Bodhisattva attains Buddhahood, those who are fully endowed with the six perfections [come to be born in that land].
Sentient beings come to be born in that land; therefore it is said: "If you wish to attain a pure land, you must purify your own mind.
As your mind becomes pure, so too will the Buddha-land become pure. I venture to ask the assembly: how, ultimately, is the mind purified? Do you understand?
"Originally there is not a single thing; where could dust and grime settle? As soon as Amitābha utters these words, the Pure Land has already blossomed. Five.
Turbidity is originally pure; the three *asaṃkhyeya-kalpas* require no effortful exclusion. Within the fire-houses of every person, all sit together upon the actual lotus throne.
I humbly entreat you to cherish yourself.
The disciple Ma Taiyu, together with his mother Lady Luo, have prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall. Mother and son are most earnest in their devotion.
I request the Dharma; the firm barrier is once again opened for you. I dare say that what was settled yesterday is unsettled today.
These three inches are clearly a nest of calamity. [He] suddenly picks up his staff and calls to the assembly, saying:
"This is the Dharma of these three inches. How can it be discussed? He strikes the ground once and says: "This is formless, for it is not seen by the eye. This is empty and still, for it is not..."

Because this reality is the object of the mind, it cannot be shifted by the four characteristics [of arising, abiding, changing, and ceasing]. Because this reality is beyond words, it cannot be expressed by the mouth.
Therefore, when Śākyamuni closed his room in Magadha, he saw but a single patch; when Vimalakīrti remained silent in Vaiśālī, he addressed the void from afar;
and when Subhūti proclaimed "non-speaking" to manifest the Way, he was merely catching shadows and grasping at wind.
Śakra cut off his hearing and rained down flowers; he called a bell a jar. At such a time as this, tell me:
how does one communicate? "The fire of the Way has never burned my mouth; propping up heaven and supporting the earth surely depends on him. He then struck the floor once more.
The assembly descended from their seats.
At Qingliu County, the senior monks Huiyun, Wuming, Ruotan, Meiyou, Huirui, Shaoru, and Huanzhao prepared a vegetarian feast and invited [the Master] to ascend the hall.
"Noble sons, what benefit is there in leaving the household life within the Buddha-dharma? It is simply this:"
To realize the source of one’s own self—what is this source of one’s own self? All that has form is entirely illusory.
O assembly, what a fine place for a brief rest; you may take your ease therein. If you see that all forms are no-form, then you see the Tathāgata.
[The Master] raises his whisk and says: "Do you see it? To see it is not non-existent, yet how vexing it is when gold dust falls into the eye! Right now...
At such a time, how can one speak the single phrase of "arriving home"? The summer trees cast dense shade as the white days grow long;
a stretch of clear stream shines like a mirror. (He strikes his whisk. He descends from the seat.
When the Venerable Yansheng requested to receive the tonsure and ascend the hall, he was like one who throws mud at himself and drowns in it—this is called an ordinary person (*pṛthagjana*).

To penetrate this gate is to become a *arhat* who has transcended the dust of the world. When the Venerable Yansheng renounced his three daughters to become nuns and abandoned his home and family to shave his head, by this single act alone, he possessed the power of a great man to become a Buddha or a Patriarch; it was not a matter of worldly honor, nobility, or merit.
Karma can indeed be measured and compared. Thus, in the past, Lord Cui Zhao asked Chan Master Guoyi of Mount Jing:
"I, your disciple, wish to leave the household life; may I do so? Jingshan replied, "Leaving the household life is the business of a great man;
it is not something that generals or ministers can accomplish. Is this not so? Nevertheless, tell me: ultimately, for what purpose does one leave the household life?

"What is this? Now, those who have left the household life do so for the sake of the unconditioned dharma (*asaṃskṛta-dharma*). This unconditioned dharma is the very root of all phenomena, both mundane and supramundane.

If one attains this dharma, one can bring to an end the cycle of birth and death that has been unresolved since time immemorial, repay the parental kindness of past lives that remains unpaid, transmit the life of wisdom to future generations, and deliver the masses of deluded beings during the final kalpa; only then will one not have failed the [parents who] performed the tonsure.
This was the original aspiration of my late master when he first entered the mountains. My late master, Zen Master Yuansheng, exhorted me with great earnestness to cherish and honor this resolve.
He expressed his gratitude to Layman Feiqing for sweeping the pagoda and requesting him to ascend the hall. It has already been ten years since our late master passed away.
Layman Feiqing Xie, a disciple from Jianzhou, has respectfully brought incense and offerings into the mountains to sweep the pagoda; yet, he does not know where the late master’s spirit resides.
As for the location of the Master’s remains, I specifically request that the mountain monk point it out. Consider this: the green pines are lush and dense;
the white pagoda stands majestic; the long river flows eastward day and night; and the rows of peaks constantly display their beauty from dawn until dusk.

Is this the sacred bone of the late Master? Or is it not? To say it is would be to place a head upon a head; to say it is not would be to strike the waves in search of water. This is precisely the point.
At such a time, tell me: how shall one decide? Tea is poured three times, then another three; the myriad phenomena and the entire universe nod their heads in unison.
Whether it be right or wrong, say not a word. Do not take pure gold and trade it for brass.
The Upāsikā’s disciple now records this request for the ascent to the hall:

A person of great merit gives rise to a mind of great merit, cultivates practices of great merit, and thereby receives the retribution of great merit. Why? Because the Dharma-nature is inexhaustible, the mind is inexhaustible.

Because the mind is inexhaustible, practice is inexhaustible; because practice is inexhaustible, the karmic fruition is also inexhaustible. Thus, when one repents of karmic obstructions, those obstructions vanish away;
when one seeks merit and longevity, merit and longevity become ever more vast. In every birth, one shall constantly encounter the Triple Gem.
Wherever one diligently plants the field of merit, one is not deluded by wealth and status, nor defiled by worldly toil;
each and every act flows forth from the very nature of reality (*dharmatā*). This may be called true merit. Now tell me: ultimately, what is this *dharmatā*?
Within the ten realms of beings—saints and ordinary alike—there is not a single thing; mountains, rivers, and the great earth are themselves suchness (*tathatā*). Be careful!
Senior Commander Xu Gong, whose courtesy name is Youcai, requests that you ascend the hall. Within every person’s own footsteps lies a great matter:
vast as the boundless void, bright as the sun and moon; it gives birth to heaven and earth and nurtures both sages and commoners.

Its spiritual powers and radiance, its merit and wisdom—all are fully possessed within, requiring no external seeking. It is simply that sentient beings do not realize it in their daily lives. Although this is so...
It is known; there has never been any lack. Today, Master Xu has entered the mountains to offer a feast and request the Dharma.
We cannot help but provide a further aid along this path. I also wish for all of you to clarify the point of entry.

He lifts his staff and strikes it once, saying: "Does the assembly understand? Master Sanping said: 'This very seeing and hearing is not seeing and hearing. With both hands he handed it over, with nothing remaining."
Sound and form may be presented before you, yet they are utterly lost from before your eyes. If you understand this point, there is nothing at all; once attained, it is attained forever.
Whether its essence and function are distinguished or not does not matter—everything is as it happens. [The Master] then struck the meditation staff and said, "Be careful!"
On the birthday of the official Wang Hui Weiming and his consort, Lady Qi, they requested that [the Master] ascend the hall.

"The great cause and condition for the Tathāgata’s appearance in the world is to cause every person to awaken to the celestial nature. By relying on this nature to give rise to true and authentic practice, blessings and longevity will naturally extend through life after life.
As for the single phrase 'awakening to and entering one's own nature,' how would you say it? In daily life, it is majestic and unobstructed."
A separate teaching. Clearly, before the birth of father and mother—take heed!
The Upāsikā disciple He Taiyun, having completed the full repentance ceremony for the Avataṃsaka Sūtra, requests that the Master ascend the hall.
The entirety of the worlds of the ten directions is the Flower Treasury Dharma-realm; the entirety of the worlds of the ten directions is Vairocana; the entirety of the ten directions...
Throughout the world—whether noble or ordinary, whether dependent or correct, even down to the myriad phenomena of the universe—all is this great Flower Garland Sutra (*Avataṃsaka-sūtra*).

Amidst the turmoil of the three realms, it surges with the waves of the ocean of Dharma; amidst the teeming multitudes of the six destinies, it shines like the stars and constellations of the celestial nature.
Suddenly, there may be a man of impatient temperament who, right here, seizes up his robes and goes forth, pushing open the tower.
Passing through the gates of the pavilion, they travel throughout the realms of the entire Dharma-realm;

within a single atom, they reach as many worlds as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields, and in each and every world, they personally attend upon as many Buddhas as there are atoms in unspeakably many Buddha-fields.
At each and every Buddha-field, one diligently cultivates the pure conduct (*brahmacarya*) until the end of the future, without interruption.
As it is with a single atom, so it is with all atoms; that is to say, it is thus in every atom, thus in every thought-moment, and thus in every dharma. Viewed with the correct eye, this is how it is.
It is like a single dream. Now, there is a virtuous woman named He Ta-yun who, within this sutra, has given rise to great faith, made great vows, and cultivated great practices.
She purifies her three karmas and applies herself with diligence to the five repentances; she prostrates for every single character, ensuring none pass in vain.
But tell me: how should this entire mass of merit ultimately be dedicated? May it pervade the myriad practices of Samantabhadra throughout the sands of the Ganges.
The Realm. Through ten vows, one is guided back to the Land of Ultimate Bliss; there, one personally beholds Amitābha and receives a prediction of enlightenment.
At every dust mote, one pays homage to the Dharma King. Cherish this.
A Small Sermon.

A Small Sermon for the Lantern Festival. The Master raised the following case: When Cai Jūnmó was governing Fúzhōu, on the day of the Upper Yuan (Lantern Festival), he ordered every household among the common people to light seven lamps.
Chén Lié made a lantern over ten feet long and inscribed upon it in large characters: "A single lamp in a wealthy house."
"A single grain of millet in a great granary; a single lamp in a poor household. Father and son face each other and weep.
Does the elegant Prefect know this or not? Yet he still regrets that the music lacks a sublime melody. When Cai Jingmu saw this, he returned to his carriage and extinguished his lamp.
The Master said, "Cai Duanming sets fire to a cold hearth, yet he still does not know where the seeds of fire come from. This is where Mr. Chen strikes the painful point."
The needle: alas, it first injures one's own hand, leaving it as a proverb for all eternity.
Tonight, this mountain monk, atop Shigufeng Peak, together with several hundred patch-robed disciples, shall celebrate the Shangyuan festival.
Let each person light a single lamp; though its brilliance may be dazzling, it shall not consume a drop of oil or fire. Rich indeed—rich without expense!
"Attached. Poor indeed! But poor it does not reach. Now tell me, what kind of lamp is this one? After a long silence, he said:
'The flowers bloom upon the iron tree, as bright as the sun; at all times they illuminate the traveler in the night.'"
A Small Sermon (Xiaocan). The Master said: "It has been several days since we entered the retreat. As for that matter, how is it?
Is there anyone who can cope with it? Come forward and speak. The questions and answers are not recorded. The Master then said:
"An ancient worthy said, 'A small sermon is called family instruction. Now, atop a solitary peak, we have erected several large buildings and gathered several hundred patch-robed monks."
Having established this fundamental style of our own house, what exactly am I teaching? Is it perhaps to teach people to practice Zen?
That would already be a grievance against them. What is lacking within the sphere of each person’s own share?
Have you not seen that in the past, there was a monk under Guizong who cried out one night, "I have attained great enlightenment! The next morning, Guizong went up [to him]...
The Master said: "Last night, let that monk who attained great enlightenment come forward. A monk stepped forth and said, "A nun is originally made of womanhood.
Guizong then desisted. "O assembly, had this monk not personally reached such a state, how could Guizong have been willing to desist?
If you all can truly recognize the point of this monk’s enlightenment, you will then recognize your own standing place."
As for this place: once you recognize the ground upon which you yourself stand, you will recognize the ground upon which all the Buddhas and Patriarchs of the past stand.
Is there anyone like this? If not, then tonight, as we meet on this narrow path, I cannot help but reveal it to you straightaway:
A nun is originally a woman; sentient beings are fundamentally Buddhas. If you can directly accept this, [you have found it].
Striking the desk with his fist, he said: "This thing has never been anything other than itself. Is there anyone here who can directly take it up?
If there is, I shall give you thirty blows of the heavy staff.
This was the small *sǎn*. The Master said: "The other day, I raised my fist, wishing for everyone to directly take it up. Little did you know that as soon as you rose..."
To think you can take it up is already to have missed it face-to-face; yet if you do not take it up, you will continue to sink and drift.
Therefore, if one is not the right person for this matter, it is truly difficult, truly difficult.

Having no other choice, I cause you all to grasp and identify with this physical body of flesh and blood born of your parents, and thus I command you to look into your own self before your parents were yet born.
The original face. Because you are afflicted by the cycle of birth and death, I have caused you to investigate the root source of birth and death.
Examine from where birth comes and to where death goes.
If you can truly recognize the place where birth and death come and go, you will then recognize the original face prior to the birth of your parents. You will recognize your parents...

If you recognize your original face prior to birth, you will immediately know the place from which birth and death come and go. Therefore, the ancient masters said: "To investigate, one must investigate truly;
to awaken, one must awaken authentically. To investigate truly, there must be the work of true investigation; to awaken authentically, there must be the words of authentic awakening.
Have you not seen how when National Teacher Nanyue Lett first investigated with the Sixth Patriarch, the Patriarch asked him: "What..."
"From where have you come? Letang replied, "From Mount Song. The Patriarch asked, "What thing comes in such a manner? Letang was speechless. He remained thus for eight years.
One day he said to the Patriarch, "I have reached a point of understanding. The Patriarch asked, "How so? Letang said, "To describe it as a single thing is not correct.
The Patriarch asked, "Is there still need for cultivation and realization? Letang said, "As for cultivation and realization—"
"It is not non-existent; it simply cannot be defiled. The Patriarch said, "Precisely this state of being undefiled is that which all Buddhas protect and keep in mind.
Since you are thus, I am also thus. "Great assembly, look at Master Rang. When the Sixth Patriarch asked him, 'What thing comes in such a way?
he could not utter a single word in response. Consequently, eight years passed. Do you know what those eight years were?"

What are you doing in the midst of this? If you do not apply your mind to investigate and perform the work of genuine practice, how could there ever be a time for later realization, nor any words that express such realization? Do you all wish to realize it truly?
It does not matter; look further into the place from which this thing thus comes. Look into the place where it is said that being like a single thing is not sufficient.

Look into the place where defilement is impossible. If you can penetrate through these three phrases, then as for where life comes from and where death goes, the whole body will be fully revealed—both before the parents were born and after they have already been born. Do you understand?
Do you understand thoroughly? A single word from a capable man; a single lash for a swift horse. There is no need for further tedious chatter.
Everyone, just look at it this way. The night is cold; take care.
Small Assembly (Xiaocan). The Master said: "Since the commencement of the retreat, two weeks have already passed.
As you all practice seated meditation, have you ever dreamed of the principle of seated meditation? If you can recognize the two demons of dullness and agitation, they will have no place to hide;
the two wheels of concentration and wisdom will be manifest and perfectly luminous. Have you not seen how Chan Master Nantang of old had a verse that said: Nantang..."

Sitting in meditation by a single burner of incense, one remains unmoving all day long, forgetting the ten thousand concerns. This is not for the sake of stilling the mind or eliminating delusive thoughts; it is simply because there is nothing with which to deliberate. O assembly, this state of non-affair is precisely where you all may let go of body and life. Do you know this? If you can know it, I grant that you have entered through the gate of samādhi. I, this mountain monk, shall now follow the example of the "fox-fur" [to add my own words]: Sitting in meditation by a single burner of incense, one remains unmoving all day long, forgetting the ten thousand concerns. This is not for the sake of stilling the mind or eliminating delusive thoughts; it is simply because there is nothing with which to deliberate. O assembly, this state of non-affair is precisely where you all may let go of body and life. Do you know this? If you can know it, I grant that you have entered through the gate of samādhi. I, this mountain monk, shall now follow the example of the "fox-fur" [to add my own words]: I sit in meditation by a single burner of incense, All day long, unmoving, the ten thousand concerns forgotten. This is not to still the heart or remove delusive thoughts; It is entirely because there is no matter to discuss. O assembly, this state of non-affair Is precisely where you all may lay down your lives. Do you know it yet? If you can know it, I allow that you enter through the gate of concentration. O assembly, this state of non-affair Is precisely where you all may lay down your lives. Do you know it yet? If you can know it, I allow that you enter through the gate of concentration. I, this mountain monk, following the lead of the preceding, also have one verse: I sit in meditation by a single burner of incense, All day long, unmoving, the ten thousand concerns forgotten. Verse: At Drum Mountain, sitting in stillness by a single incense burner, It is like catching a thief—one must see the stolen goods.
Tearing open empty space, not a single thing remains; Majestic and towering, the King of Dharmas stands alone revealed. Great assembly, do you know that there is this Dharma King?

If you can know him, I grant that you have entered through the gate of wisdom. Thus an ancient worthy said: "When concentration and wisdom are studied equally, one clearly perceives the Buddha-nature."
All you people should simply take these two verses and investigate them thoroughly.

If you can penetrate this matter through such investigation, you will know that what belongs to Nantang is precisely what belongs to Gushan, and what belongs to Gushan is precisely what belongs to Nantang.
If you are unable to do so, then for now press deep into a single gate, lest you weep at a forked road over lost sheep.
Small Assembly. The Master said: "All day long I have been entangling you all with complications, yet you do not seek a definitive conclusion here;
you still remain drowsing. Truly, you are not up to much! Now tell me, where does the sickness lie?
It is simply because you have abandoned your home and wandered abroad for so many years that you have forgotten it. Time and again I join hands with you to return home—to our ancestral estate."
It is complete. The contract is clear and explicit. Yet, even here, people still turn their heads and look back—how truly pitiable this is!
Now, having no other choice, I cannot help but sell the precious for the cheap. With both hands, he tosses everything into the void and says: [He remains silent.]
I have picked it up and placed it before you all. Let those with eyes see; let those with ears hear;
let those with mouths speak; let those with minds contemplate. Look at what place is not radiant? What place does not manifest the present?
Nevertheless, suppose there were a man here who lacked eyes and ears, and whose mind and mouth were incomplete—how would you receive him?
He led them away. After a long while, he said, "With shame and remorse," and returned to his quarters.
During a small-scale sermon (*xiaocan*), the Master said: "When you all come to Gushan to practice Zen, what do you hope for? Do you not hope to become Buddhas?"
To place a head upon a head—if one does not become a Buddha, one falls back into the realm of sentient beings. Indeed, "success" and "failure" are dualistic expressions.
You must know that within yourself there is the matter of your own fundamental allotment (*fenben*). What is this matter of your own fundamental allotment?
After a long silence, he said: "Difficult, difficult, difficult! Joining bamboo to point toward the sky is merely deceiving oneself. Easy, easy, easy! Run down!"
Coming alone, treading upon the earth—it is neither difficult nor easy. Riding an iron horse backward, one plays amidst the clouds. Everyone, tell me:
do these three phrases have any intimacy or distance between them? "Threaded through as one, they are cast to the other side; the old Holy Monk in the hall laughs until he falls over.
*Chan.* A monk asked: "The myriad dharmas are the radiance of the mind; all conditions are understood only through the nature. Originally there is none..."
Regarding the person of delusion and awakening: one simply must resolve it this very day. But how does one resolve it right now? The Master said, "Why do you not directly realize it?
The student asked, "Since there is fundamentally no person of delusion or awakening, what is there to resolve? The Master said, "Directly resolve that which is without delusion or awakening.
The student said, "If that is so, then it is like the moon in the empty expanse of the azure pool for ten thousand ages; only after repeatedly stirring it can one..."
The Master said, "You should know: what is this matter that you know? The student stepped forward and said, "When the grass withers, the hawk’s eye sharpens;
when the snow melts, the horse’s hooves light. The Master said, "Idle talk."
On account of a minor matter, the Master held a small-scale *sīmān* (small *chan*). He said: "All of you have left one monastic community and entered another;
each of you says, 'I am practicing *chan* and studying the Way. Yet you do not know what is called the 'Way,' nor how the Way is to be studied.
If you do not investigate and realize this clearly right here, you are merely people who eat their meals in the company of the crowd. What common ground for conversation could there be? You all..."
Do you understand? Why do you not examine the "entanglements" (*ge-teng*) of the ancients of old?
Have you not seen how, in the past, Zhaozhou asked Nanquan, "What is the Way? Nanquan replied, "The ordinary mind is the Way. Zhaozhou asked, "Can one still direct oneself toward it?
Nanquan said, "To intend to direct oneself is already to deviate. Zhaozhou said, "If one does not intend, how can one know it is the Way? Nanquan said, "The Way does not belong to..."
"Knowing does not belong to not-knowing. Knowing belongs to deluded cognition; not-knowing belongs to the indeterminate (*avyākṛta*).
If one truly penetrates the Way that is free from doubt, it is like the great void—vast, open, and expansive. How could one forcibly impose right and wrong?
At these words, Zhao attained great enlightenment. "The ordinary mind is the Way. How many among the assembly can understand such excellent words? What is there to say?
It is said: "The common people use it daily yet do not know it; therefore, the Way of the gentleman is rare.

Nowadays, those who study the Way merely make their livelihood out of knowing or not knowing. Those who "know" are constantly manipulating their consciousness, seeking extensive learning and wide erudition, wandering about in the external world.
Those who "do not know" simply suppress their delusive thoughts, attempting to collect their mindfulness and return to emptiness.
Sitting in stagnant water, you have failed to emerge from the trap of deluded perception and neutral ignorance. When have you ever even dreamed of the ordinary mind?
If you all wish to recognize that the ordinary mind is the Way, listen to this verse: "Drinking when thirsty and eating when hungry—nothing else.
Sitting in the corner of the meditation seat, one reflects with profound ease. A single blow strikes the very seat of true pain. It does not.
Jue called out with a cry. If you can realize it here, only then will you be able to receive the staff from this mountain monk.
If it is otherwise, we do not know each other face-to-face; do not say that you have come into my presence.
The Small Sermon for the Dissolution of the Retreat. The Master said: "Today is the dissolution of the retreat. I, this mountain monk, have four questions.

First, while you all have been here engaged in Chan meditation during the retreat, having set aside dullness and deluded thoughts, try to bring forth the very Chan you have been meditating upon and show it to me.
Second, one practices Chan to resolve the matter of birth and death; how do you practice the Chan that resolves birth and death? Third..."
Question: The three-month *anvaya* (summer retreat) is now complete; what exactly will you offer in exchange for the funds for the monastery’s daily meals? Question Four:
Every person possesses the mark of a broad and long tongue, speaking horizontally and vertically day and night without interruption.
Set aside that skull and utter a single phrase! If these four questions can be answered correctly, you may be granted the opportunity to study under me. If not—
This is not definitive. Going east and going west, when one is bitten to death by a venomous snake in the wild grasses, do not say that this mountain monk has not already exposed the truth.
At the Small Assembly (Xiaocan) on the Mid-Autumn Festival, the Master said: "While I was in the mountains, I have celebrated the Mid-Autumn Festival with the great assembly three times. He ate...
Tea speaks; tea does not know how to eat. Where has it gone? Speech also does not know how to listen. Where has it gone?
Tonight we happen upon the Mid-Autumn Festival while drinking tea, and you ask the mountain monk to speak. I do not know what to say. Shall I speak of the moon?
At Vulture Peak, [the Buddha] pointed toward Caoxi; Master Mazu and his father played with Hanshan.
Verse: This moon has been thoroughly exploited by this troupe of shadow-play performers; they have exhausted every trick. What more can this mountain monk say?
Nevertheless, I cannot help but turn the non-existent into the existent to respond to the occasion. Long ago, a monk asked Caoshan, "What is it like when the bright moon is suspended in the sky?
Caoshan said, "He is still a man standing on the steps. When the bright moon is suspended in the sky—
"How many people have reached this stage? Caoshan still said, "They are but men standing at the foot of the steps. You tell me, where does the fault lie? Have you not heard it said:
"The clear light shines before the eyes, yet one is as if lost in one's home; though one turns with clarity, one still falls into a position"?
Is this not the point where this man errs? This monk was indeed clever; he stepped forward and said, "I ask the Master to receive me onto the steps. Caoshan—
He said, "We shall meet after the moon has fallen. But how can one meet after the moon has fallen?
Listen to this verse: Last night Lady Heng-er delivered a message: "Gold coins are not permitted for playing with the shrimp.
Together we topple the Palace of Broad Cold, And invite one another to drink Zhaozhou’s tea. Take care.
The filial son Chu Gu (Chù Gǔ) offers this memorial for his late father, General Huáiyuǎn Kūixù (Huái Yuǎn Jiāngjūn Kuí Xù), Duke Chūgōng, and his late mother, Lady Tàshū rén Shèng.
He requests a small private discourse before the spirit. The Master said: "If we discuss the Buddha-dharma, it requires nothing more than recognizing one's own source.
