You have swept away all obstacles to unify the realm and established peace within the borders of the nation.
He conversed with ease and grace, never withholding his full effort. When he suddenly passed away, people suspected it was a "corpse-liberation" (*shijie*), a transformation without death.
That such words are not startling—may the sea of Min dry up and the mountains of Min crumble, yet the Master’s good reputation shall resound like thunder for ten thousand ages.
The layman Zeng Weifu composed this eulogy for this man:

"From his youth, he possessed a spiritual bone; dwelling within this Saha world, he yearned for the Pure Land. Though trained in the Confucian arts, he applied himself diligently to the study of Buddhism.

With a single phrase of Amitābha, he achieved the perfect integration of principle and phenomenon; with ten fascicles of the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, he attained a thorough mastery of its words and meanings."

When the time arrived, he let go of his hands and departed. For several days, the fragrance of the lotus remained rich and pervasive. As the proof of his rebirth in the Western Paradise was thus made manifest, one can finally believe that this man was like jade;
who could say that the ocean of worldly toil is so deep as to be able to bury him forever? Ultimately, it could not obscure him.
Inscription for the Great Bell of Kaiyuan Temple in Fuzhou.

When Master Da Kou preaches the Dharma, the striking of this bell is never deficient; its sound reaches everywhere and benefits all. The ignorant are awakened and the violent become benevolent—ten million beings [are transformed].
Carrying on the tradition of daily renewal.
Inscription for the Bell at Lingshi Temple in Fucheng:
This Lingshi Temple is an ancient center of Chan practice. As its fortunes were revived, a great bell was first fashioned as a model. Once the mold was cast and the form was complete...

The myriad virtues are fully perfected; perfect, eternal, and quiescent, yet responding. The faculty of hearing encompasses all sounds. Amidst the vast night of ignorance, sentient beings slumber for long;
with one strike from Rāhula, they are instantly awakened. The nine peaks rise in layered splendor; the patriarchs return once more. The thunderous voice shall forever resound.
A lotus blooms within the flames.
This is the epitaph for Master Huigao of Ya Mountain.
The Way of Xinfeng rose anew with Shouchang; Boshan inherited it, its waves vast and surging. He firmly held the gate of the Dharma.

The crowing of the rooster was no deception; only the Master stood preeminent. Truly he was one who had attained the essential meaning. The fragrance of flowers upon an iron tree; at the third watch, the sun shines bright. His word was always followed;
he was as careful in the end as he was in the beginning. Having forgotten both taking and rejecting, who could say what life or death were? A stupa was erected on Yashan.
A mere foot or span from the heavens, yet spanning billions of years, the pure breeze has never ceased.
At Mount Huayan in Longshu, stands the stupa of Dharma Master Taichu Kun.
The ocean of the Dharma is vast and expansive, its depths boundless; who can board the boat of wisdom to traverse it with ease? There was, indeed, a Great Being.

Returning by virtue of his vows, he opened the essential points of *dharmatā* and *lakṣaṇa* with a single blow. Renowned scholars bowed their hearts and requested instruction upon holding their scriptures.

As he thundered forth a majestic voice like a great clap of thunder, they drew back in awe, their robes tucked in. Throughout the entire *Dharmadhātu* of the Flower Store (*Huazang*), every place was fully revealed. Longshu Huanglong.

Never departing from the site of enlightenment, the white stupa towers toward the clouds and the green mountains are lush and magnificent. The spiritual radiance of the Master remains as bright as day for a thousand ages.
As for the inscription on the square bamboo staff:
"Treading perilous paths as if they were level; ascending heights as if descending. Such is the heart of this noble companion—empty and void, requiring no external support.
The Buddha-work at the stupa grove of the ancestral master Yunkong of Sǎolín Mountain is formidable, like a sleeping tiger’s fierce majesty.
The paths are slippery and the clouds deep; one rarely encounters it. In days of yore, Shòuchāng suffered its venom.
Mouth. It would simply cause a wind of stench to rise throughout the entire world. But tell me, what serves as the proof? [Zhaozhou] raised his incense burner and said, "Heh! Then he burned it.
He swept the pagoda of the late Master Wuming Shouchang.
Thirty years ago, it was a magnificent mountain; thirty years later, the mountain is no longer good. It has deceived the descendants into dwelling nowhere.
"Abiding here, for now I only sweep the ancestral stupa. How do you understand the phrase 'sweeping the stupa'? He then burned incense and said:
"I respectfully pay homage to Master Yunqi, the Elder Monk Lianchi. You were a master of transformation for the Land of Bliss and a guide for this Sahā world."

Opening a single gate to the burning house, he points directly to the path for returning to the source. With the sword that kills and the sword that gives life, his single phrase of Amitābha spreads clouds of compassion and showers nectar.
His three clusters of pure precepts resound through the universe; his Way is disseminated throughout antiquity and the present.

I, Daopei, am but a single leaf among a thousand flowers, yet I have received the connection with those who share this affinity. Transmitting the subtle words of the six characters, I shall act as a successor to propagate the purity [of the Dharma].
The ten thousand folds of the Min Mountains are all the true body of the Dharma-realm; the vast expanse of the Min Sea is entirely the Dharma-rain of the five clouds.
Bringing this incense of devotion from a thousand li away, I express my humble sincerity for eternity.

I only pray that you will turn back the Compassionate Vessel to cut through the surging waves of the river of craving, raise high the red banner to subdue the wild heresies of the degenerate age, and rekindle the lamp of the mind to illuminate all.
At this time, we reverently pay homage at the Great Stupa of the Venerable Master Zhenji (Sweeping the Jar Kiln), who was the true Dharma.
We respectfully consider that the Venerable Master Zhenji, the Elder Master Zhangshi, held the tally of the White Horse and carried out the mandate of Yunqi. When—

Yang Ba cut off [all attachments], such that neither demons nor Buddhas could fathom his spiritual traces. In the secret ground he opened wide, so that even mosquitoes and gnats may drink from his ocean of Dharma.
Having just emerged from the burning house, Daopei first prostrated before the lion throne; pointing toward Mount He, he then entered the chamber of Chou.

Cherishing the grace of the Dharma, he felt that nothing short of grinding his own bones could repay it; following the final testament, he held that only the transmission of the Dharma could serve as a true requital. From afar...
I present these offerings from a thousand li away, merely to manifest my inexhaustible devotion. The white stupa stands majestic; gazing upon it, the True Form seems as if present.
The green mountains rise in layers; bathed in the transformation of the Dharma, they flourish ever anew.

I pray only that you will not arise from the samādhi of cessation, but instead steer the compassionate vessel back toward us, to rescue those drowning in the degenerate age and to sustain the eternal life-force of wisdom.
We reverently enshrine the successive patriarchs of this mountain in the Hall of Ancestral Masters and offer incense, saying:
"In the depths of white clouds, a pack of rākṣasas has stirred up the world, creating waves upon dry land. Today, they have fallen into the hands of this mountain monk;
there is no choice but to suppress them all at once. He burns incense and says: "The idle fame of ten thousand ages cannot be removed..."
Exhausted. Daily incense smoke, nightly lamps.
On the nineteenth day of the seventh month in the Dingwei year, on the ninetieth birthday of the Old Monk, Zhaozhou offered incense:
"Zhaozhou was able to employ the twelve hours; yet when one looks closely, he was still being employed by the hours. My Master has once realized that there is no time."

The Dharma: throughout ten thousand kalpas, in a single kṣaṇa, there is neither "this" nor "that. From descending to be born, attaining enlightenment, and entering nirvāṇa, it has not yet transcended the limit of that kṣaṇa.
Encompassing heaven and covering earth, it lacks nothing and has no surplus. Turning the earth and revolving the heavens—what movement or stillness can there be?

A stone woman gives birth to a child at the age of ninety; human years and months are counted from the beginning. A single cloud of sandalwood fragrance envelops the entire dharma-realm; in every atom and every land...
A fragrant wind arises throughout the lands.
Layman Xie Feiqing offers this memorial for the late Master Wufei:

"To awaken to non-being is to realize one's original nature; only then does one know that today is truly being. To sit and sever the barrier between right and wrong is to arrive at the stage of the Tathāgata."
Awakening is not something superior; the gate of right and wrong has already been cut off. Where, then, is the stage of the Tathāgata?
Ultimately, it has never departed from its original station. Within this, who awakens and who is deluded?
Arriving at Mount Yunju, the primary mountain of the ancestral lineage, I offer incense for the supreme offerings;
it has been thirty years since we last met. We have been parted for over ten years, yet today I come once more; there is no interval between life and death.

With profound reverence, we pay homage to the founding patriarch Yunju, who received the ancestral lineage from Master Jue; you left the household life for the True Cause and planted your feet firmly upon the ground of reality.

Your words and deeds were flawless, free from regret or reproach. You cultivated Chan and Pure Land in perfect harmony, abiding in neither attachment nor clinging. Through the power of your vows, you transformed the green mountains into a Buddhist monastery;
through the purity of your mind, you attained the vision of the golden lotus in the jeweled land. With causes fulfilled and fruits perfected, you have reached the ultimate destination.
The channel is complete; he sits, cutting off the present moment, and ascends high to the superior grade.

Just as Dao-pai has come today specifically to burn this single offering of *candana* incense—tell me, is there still a place where we can meet? Then, burning the incense, he said: "Sukhāvatī and Sahā are not separated by even a hair’s breadth;
within the shadows of the incense clouds, his entire body appears. Whether it be birth or death, neither is spoken of—how could one discuss it?"
The person of old is not the person of old.
On the seventh day of the tenth month of the Bingwu year, the tenth anniversary of the passing of my late Preceptor, I offer incense:
My Master’s single thought transcends the three periods of time; This deluded son, with solitary heart, remembers ten years. He grasps at empty space to seek a bird.
The Trace: Turning over the great earth to seek the dragon’s abyss; the ancient melody of Xinfeng is heard throughout the dharma-realm.
The sound of the stone drum is rare, yet it shakes the great trichiliocosm. To repay this profound kindness, there is only this: a single thread of fragrant incense, perpetually continuous.
Offering Incense for the Memorial of the Late Venerable Zhuan’an:
Respectfully, we pay homage to the late Venerable Zhuan’an of Nanyue at Changqing, a son of Tianjie and a grandson of Shouchang.
Rebuilding the ancestral hall amidst the ashes; upholding the Way and the Dharma at a time of decline. Pouring forth from the "hanging mouth," pulling the trigger of the lightning mechanism:
great functions flourish and the profound gate is opened wide. Now, withdrawing from the midst of clamor, why not follow the path back home?
Letting go over there, one simply allows the empty flowers to fall to the stem. At this very moment, tell me: what is it?
When he met Master Zhu, how did they greet one another? He snapped his fingers and said: "At midnight, the wooden boy knocks at the moon-gate;
in the darkness, he startles the jade maiden from her sleep. Thereupon, he burned incense.

For you, the vessel-like Chan practitioner, I have spent several years in seeking and inquiry so that you may resolve the matter of birth and death. When the four mountains press in from all sides, how can one turn and evade them?
When the eyes open within the skull, there is not an inch of soil throughout the great earth, the mountains, and the rivers.

To clarify this: a single master of stillness took up his fire from Mount Guzhu and settled it in his nostrils; he patted his chest and claimed for himself a spirit like a rainbow, further endowed with a mouth fit for cursing.
Only at the very end did he realize the merit of true practice: kicking over the shore of birth and death and smashing through the great void—ordinary and sage alike.
One cannot find it within the various positions. A bottomless boat is steered amidst fierce flames. [The Master] hurls a torch and lets out a shout, saying:
"Be most careful not to evade or follow after it!
He then performed the funeral rites for the Abbot Huiyun.
The whistling western wind penetrates the distant forests; the traces of the Way-man are truly difficult to find.

Meeting once more upon the road through the night, how could a single phrase have any distinction between past and present? I respectfully pay homage to the nun Huíyún Jué, who entered the monastic life in her youth and embraced the Way until her white-haired old age.
Throughout her life, she cultivated vast aspirations and established immeasurable causes and conditions. Her single point of compassion—
With his mind, he transformed and guided countless men and women. Now that his karmic conditions in this Sahā world have exhausted, what prevents him from withdrawing from the fray?
As the flowers bloom in the Pure Land, let him freely behold the Buddha within meditative concentration. At such a time as this, there remains one final phrase for parting: how shall it be said?
Relying solely upon the fire of the nature-emptiness, he smelts and purifies the five-leakage body of the human realm. He sits, having cut off all [delusions].
"The entire manifestation of the ten directions is present; Amitābha was originally no other. He then cast down a torch.
For the sake of the venerable elder Yixiang, he raised the torch and respectfully paid homage:
"We reverently contemplate the passing into parinirvāṇa of the senior elder Yixiang Jing. Having donned the black robes at the age of twenty, he immediately entered the chamber of Bozan."

Throughout his life he lived in secluded retirement. For a long time he dwelt on the banks of the Jian River, where he cultivated his mind with diligent perseverance, sitting or standing as motionless as an iron stake.
In his compassion for all beings, he was as gentle and simple as an infant. The fourfold assembly took refuge in him, and the mountains revered him from afar.

Having early received his guidance and encouragement, I have come late to behold his radiant countenance; I was just beginning to contemplate dwelling for a long time amidst the white clouds, yet I never expected that I would so suddenly return to the clear [mountains].
"Peace! This is the day when the cause is perfected and the fruit is fulfilled; it is precisely the moment when the flowers bloom and the Buddha is seen.
We have prepared this cremation simply to burn away these floating illusions. Does the Master of the Single Mark know? Entering meditative concentration in the East, he arises in the West;
among the nine grades of rebirth, the first branch of the flower has blossomed. Re-smelted and refined before the Gate of Victory, the radiance of the flames reflects back into the Jewel Lotus Pond."
For the sake of the virtuous friend Luo Xinchao, we have lit this fire;

the nature of fire is without self and depends upon various conditions. The four great elements and the five aggregates are likewise all thus. We respectfully consider the virtuous friend Luo Xinchao:

he cultivated his person through filial piety and fraternal duty, and received others with kindness and harmony. Living in the world, he was free from worldly attachments; while residing at home, he remained detached.
With the aspiration for renunciation, he took up residence in the Lotus Land in the Golden Quarter and established an araṇya at Shigong.
Now, as the conditions of his retribution have come to an end, he has cast off his hands and returned home. Looking back upon the dust and clamor of the world, it is but a single dream-event.
One must know that life is a dream and death is also a dream; even to say "neither born nor dead" is likewise a dream. As for shattering this dream—
He uttered a single phrase: "How do you say it? Holding up a torch, he drew a circle in the air and said, "When not a single dharma is seen, that is the Tathāgata;
only then is one named Avalokiteśvara. He then cast away the torch.
He came to perform the cremation for the Venerable Shi-yi and sweep his father’s stupa;
his entire body returned to his father within a great radiance, with every detail and pattern clearly revealed.
He then performed the cremation for Layman Zhang Xi-yi.

That which cannot be heard when listened to is called "the rare" (xī); that which cannot be seen when looked upon is called "the level" (yí). Realize for yourself this state of neither hearing nor seeing;
verify it at the moment when ashes fly and smoke vanishes. Then, cast away the torch.
For the sake of the Elder Bensu, he held up the fire upon the pure ground;
one must strictly avoid defiling it. Within the mass of fierce flames, he restored it to its original purity.
For the sake of the Elder Zhileng, he held up the fire.
Having seen through the dream of Jambudvīpa, he came to study under Shigong Chan. For three years it was as if but a single day; his practice was like a blue lotus.
Returning from his alms-round, he passed away while seated before his birth. Re-smelted in the great furnace of the forge, his great function is once again manifest and clear.
For the sake of Venerable Lianggong, I raise the torch:
karma is created by the mind and manifested by the mind; repentance is performed by the mind and insight is seen by the mind. Within the light of Prajñā, the activities of the mind are empty.
Here, quickly realize your original face.
"For the sake of the venerable Master Shaoxin, I shall ignite his body.
"The body is the root of suffering; it can naturally invite illness. When illness reaches the point where there is no body, only then does illness find peace.

"This very 'no-body' must be subjected to further intense smelting. "After being smelted, what then? "A long sword leaning against the sky, its coldness overwhelming all who approach. He then cast [the ashes] into the torch.
For the sake of the attendant Jinghui, I have held up this skin-bag for you to burn.
How many such things have been cast away? And yet, here is yet another—still not resolved. If you wish to reach resolution, recognize that single aperture prior to birth.
(He hurls the torch and says: After the fire, it is but a single blade of grass.
For the sake of the Elder Master Qinglin, I raise this torch:
throughout his life beneath the forest trees, he has polished himself until he was refined; in his meticulous cultivation, he stands alone as a true elder.

He cut off the flow of all streams so that not a single drop remained, yet he achieved complete merit in turning back the Dharma-ending age. I respectfully venerate the Venerable Elder Qing, the Hall-Master of Shilin Temple in the Zen Forest. [End of] Zen Forest [Record].
A jade tree; a sea-treasure among monks. Having traveled early through all quarters, he attained the "lion crouching on the ground" method;

ultimately, he remained hidden in the forests and thickets, employing the "antelope hanging its horns" device. With a single-minded devotion to the Buddha, his practice and principle were perfectly complete; the lotus was divided into nine grades.
Fools and sages are both embraced; birds and fish alike rejoice in their lives. Monastics and laypeople alike praise his virtue.
With causes complete and fruits fulfilled, the water reaches and the channel forms. Letting go of the hand, one proceeds; taking a single step, one arrives.
At this very moment, when facing the words of Śūraṅgama, how would you speak? When the fires break out on all four sides and no shadow remains, the blossoming of the supreme flower is precisely now.
He then cast a torch into it. Although Master Yuanzheng entered the monastic life late in life, his religious practice was consistently diligent.
He settled his mind upon the Pure Land, remaining untainted by the dust of the mundane world. At the sound of the morning bell, he awoke from his dream.
In an instant, he returned to the truth. Within the furnace of the eminent assembly, he underwent further refinement; in the West, the precious tree was met with the arrival of spring.
He then cast down the torch, lighting the funeral pyre for the venerable elder of the Three Studies.
A single illness lingered for eight months; who could know the method by which he remained so peaceful?

Sitting and reclining with a radiant composure upon his meditation seat, it was already proven that he had attained power through his practice. But right now, as wind and fire have dispersed and both medicine and disease are forgotten—where does this one pivotal point fall?
(He strikes a circular shape with a torch. "The Samādhi of the Torch Light has no..."
Upon seeing the shadow of the remains— and further, seeing a lotus flower emerge from the mud—
he threw a torch into it. For Shangshi Shouzuo,
who has dwelt on this mountain for thirty years, purifying his Brahma-conduct as purely as a blue lotus, I now offer you a single handful of assistance.
Fire! It returns to the state prior to the emergence of the skull’s signs.

For the sake of the Venerable Liansheng, he maintained the fire and observed the fast for sixteen years; he constructed three or five pavilions, extended his benevolence to care for his two nephews, and served his aged mother with all his strength.
At the end of his life, he requested to don the black robes and join the ranks of the Triple Gem. With single-minded devotion to the Buddha’s name, he vowed to cross over birth and death.
At the moment of his passing, his mind remained undisturbed; he sat upright and died. Neither humans nor devas could retain him; his fruit has ripened in the Lotus Land.
Having cast off all myriad conditions, only this skin-sack remains. It serves as fuel for the fire of *prajñā*, causing true radiance to emanate from every part of the body.
Thereupon, he threw it into the torch.
In reverent contemplation of the late Venerable Master Wuyi:
dwelling at home yet studying the Way, he realized the truth within the mundane; though his ordination came late, he donned the black robes with profound sincerity.

His conduct was characterized by diligent industry; he engaged in ritual recitations without ceasing from dawn until dusk. He possessed a profound understanding of the nature of reality through both doctrine and practice, remaining unerring in his application of the teachings according to the theory of the intrinsically present nature.
As a paradigm for the Dharma-gate, he served as a model for later students. Now that he has reached the age of seventy, [the disciples] have gathered to celebrate this occasion.
Thus, the karmic conditions of this present life are brought to an end; one is certain to enter the *Śūraṅgama-samādhi* and vow to return to the Land of Ultimate Bliss.

This may be called being correct from beginning to end, where cause and effect are entirely authentic. At such a time, how would you express the single phrase of mutual support at the very last moment?
Holding up a torch and drawing a circle, he said: "When space meets space, there is no seam or crack; when fire burns fire, it is naturally cool and refreshing."
Every land and every speck of dust is a pure realm; what prevents one from playing, whenever the occasion arises?
Taking the bones to enter the stupa is the indestructible body; having undergone further refinement, the Stone Drum returns and appears in the West (Master Dongluan).
The skin has fallen away, leaving only the true reality; it is gathered and placed within the white stupa of the Secret Treasury. Sitting and cutting off the source, there is no noble rank above;
the peach blossoms still smile at the spring breeze (the sacred remains of the assembly of monks).

A single stupa for both parents; though a thousand autumns have passed, they remain as if present. In both the mundane and supramundane realms, there is no attachment or obstruction (Dingxiang’s parents).
The mind is pure and the land is pure; because the cause is true, the fruit is true. Amidst the clouds stands a white stupa: the entire body within the dharma-realm (Taiyu’s mother Dao’gang).
Taijing left the household life; his parents entered the stupa. The sacred and the secular were both manifested; the fire-lotus blossomed in splendor (Taijing’s parents).
A child born of one’s own flesh covered the bones of one’s own kin. Birth and death are fundamentally empty; a wondrous harmony arises spontaneously (the parents of the assembly).
Amidst a mound of white bones, birth and death do not reach; within the seamless stupa, sound and light are vast and surging (Deng Yusheng’s father).
Refining them into a single set of golden bones, when struck casually, they ring like bronze. Within the seamless stupa, the light flashes brilliantly;
having cut off past and present, his name remains unknown (the Elder Yixiang).
In the eighty-second year, Zhibai and Zhixuan shattered the dream of birth and death and transcended the two extremes.
Within this, there stands a single round stupa, which occupies the three thousand worlds and the great chiliocosm (for the parents of Elder Xuanwen).
Refined through diligent practice for seventy years, like pure gold refined a hundred times; it is right here within this mountain, yet the Buddha-eye cannot see it (Master Qinglin).
The three trainings of precepts, concentration, and wisdom are fundamentally inherent. When the fruit is fulfilled and the cause is perfected, all is gathered back here.

(The Elder of the Three Trainings) Values reality and does not value the empty; there is neither deficiency nor excess. Jambudvīpa returns to the White Stupa; the Land of Ultimate Bliss manifests as lotuses.
(The Elder Who Values Reality)
The Record of Inhaling the Fragrance by Venerable Gushan Weilin, Volume Lower (End)
